`docs/pages/operations/capture-and-replay.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Capture and replay"
description: "Record traffic from a session and feed it back through the real receive path."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Capture and replay

A capture records every event a module sends, receives or drops, with a readable summary of its data and, where allowed, the raw bytes. Use it to reproduce a bug from a real session, or to see exactly what an exploiter sent.

## Recording

```lua copy
Network.Capture.Start({
    Limit = 500,
    Redactions = { "Password", "Token" },
})

-- ... play ...

Network.Capture.Stop()
local entries = Network.Capture.Entries()
for _, entry in entries do
    print(entry.Direction, entry.Name, entry.Status, entry.Reason, entry.PayloadSummary)
end
```

- The buffer keeps the newest [`CaptureLimit`](/reference/options/diagnostics#capturelimit) entries.
- Fields named in the redaction list appear as `[redacted]` in summaries.
- Outside the `Development` profile, raw bytes are not kept unless you turn off [`NoRawCaptureInProduction`](/reference/options/diagnostics#norawcaptureinproduction). Summaries are always kept.

See [Capture](/reference/api/capture) for every entry field.

## Replaying through your own logic

[`Capture.Replay`](/reference/api/capture#replay) calls a handler per endpoint for each accepted entry. Nothing is decoded; you get the entry and its summary.

```lua copy
local result = Network.Capture.Replay(entries, {
    Purchase = function(entry)
        print("purchase at", entry.Time, entry.PayloadSummary)
    end,
})
print(result.Accepted, result.Dropped, result.Replayed)
```

## Replaying raw bytes

[`Capture.ReplayRaw`](/reference/api/capture#replayraw) feeds each entry's raw bytes into the module's real receive path, as if they had just arrived: every check, the decoder, validation and your listeners run. This reproduces decoding bugs and exploit packets exactly.

```lua copy
local received = {}
for _, entry in entries do
    if entry.Direction == "receive" then
        table.insert(received, entry)
    end
end
Network.Capture.ReplayRaw(received, Players:GetPlayers()[1])
```

<Callout type="warning">
Only replay in Studio or a private test server. On the server, always pass a real player as the source: captured sources are stored as strings. Filter to received entries, or your own sends are replayed as if a player sent them.
</Callout>

## Capturing on demand

Capture costs an allocation per event. Instead of leaving [`EnablePacketCapture`](/reference/options/diagnostics#enablepacketcapture) on, start a capture from an admin command when you need one, and stop it after.

```

`docs/pages/operations/inspector.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Inspector"
description: "One table with everything the module knows, for debug panels and bug reports."
---

# Inspector

The inspector bundles metrics, handshake results, captured packets, and integrity state into one snapshot. Enable it on demand from an admin command or in Studio.

```lua copy
Network.Inspector.Enable(true)

task.delay(30, function()
    local snapshot = Network.Inspector.Snapshot()
    print(snapshot.Metrics.DroppedPackets)
    print(#snapshot.Capture, "captured events")
    Network.Inspector.Enable(false)
end)
```

While enabled, the inspector also records events into the capture buffer, so `snapshot.Capture` has recent traffic even if you never called `Capture.Start`.

| Field | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `Metrics` | [`Stats()`](/reference/api/module#stats) |
| `Protocol`, `Peers` | [Handshake results](/reference/api/protocol) |
| `Capture` | [Captured entries](/reference/api/capture#entries) |
| `ClientIntegrity` | [Client integrity state](/reference/api/security#clientintegrity) |
| `CharacterIntegrity` | [Character integrity state](/reference/api/security#characterintegrity) |
| `Runtime` | Protocol, schema version, security profile |

`Snapshot` errors unless the inspector is enabled with `Inspector.Enable(true)` or the [`EnableInspector`](/reference/options/diagnostics#enableinspector) option.

```

`docs/pages/operations/large-schemas.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Large schemas"
description: "Splitting a big network surface across files and modules, and staying under Studio's script size limit."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Large schemas

## Splitting the source

Use [`import`](/reference/declarations/import) to split one schema across files. Each file becomes a scope, and everything still compiles into one pair of modules.

```cheeto nocheck
option ClientOutput = "Network/Client.luau"
option ServerOutput = "Network/Server.luau"

import "./Combat"
import "./Economy"
import "./Social"
```

```lua copy
Network.Combat.Hit.Fire(target)
Network.Economy.Purchase.Invoke(itemId)
```

## Studio's 200,000-character limit

Studio refuses to save a script longer than 200,000 characters. A generated module is the runtime (about 135 KB) plus roughly 1 to 3 KB per endpoint, so a module with many endpoints can hit the limit. Two options help.

### Share the runtime

[`RuntimeOutput`](/reference/options/output#runtimeoutput) writes the runtime once as its own module, and the generated modules require it instead of containing it:

```cheeto copy
option ClientOutput = "Network/Client.luau"
option ServerOutput = "Network/Server.luau"
option RuntimeOutput = "Network/Runtime.luau"
option RuntimeRequire = "script.Parent.Runtime"

event Ping {
    From: Server,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: ManyAsync
}
```

This writes `Runtime.luau` and `RuntimeClient.luau`. The generated modules then contain only your endpoints.

### Split into several schemas

For very large surfaces, compile several schemas, each with its own outputs and its own [`RemoteScope`](/reference/options/output#remotescope), all pointing at one shared runtime. Each schema gets its own pair of remotes and its own state.

<Callout type="warning">
Policies, auth rules, kill switches, groups and configuration are per module. When you split into several schemas, register rules and connect `OnViolation` on every server module, not just one.
</Callout>

Check generated sizes in your build, so a module that grows past the limit fails CI instead of failing to install in Studio. [`--benchmark`](/reference/cli#--benchmark) fails when a module passes its size threshold.

```

`docs/pages/operations/lockfile.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Lockfile"
description: "Using cheeto.lock to make schema changes visible in review."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Lockfile

`cheeto.lock` is a small JSON file next to your schema that records its surface: every endpoint and type by name, the schema version and key security options. Committing it turns every change to that surface into a diff someone has to approve.

```sh copy
cheeto network --write-lock --yes
git add network.cheeto cheeto.lock
```

In CI:

```sh copy
cheeto network --check-lock --yes
```

`--check-lock` fails when the schema no longer matches the lockfile: an endpoint or type added, removed, renamed or reordered, or the version or security options changed. The fix is to run `--write-lock` and commit, which is exactly the moment a reviewer should ask whether the change is intended and whether `Version` went up.

<Callout type="warning">
The lockfile records names, not contents. Changing a field's type inside a struct does not change the lockfile, even though it changes the wire format. Review schema diffs themselves, and increase `Version` for any layout change. See [cheeto.lock format](/reference/lockfile).
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/operations/metrics.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Metrics"
description: "Reading traffic and drop counters from a live module."
---

# Metrics

Every module counts what it does. Read the counters with [`Stats()`](/reference/api/module#stats), print them with [`Report()`](/reference/api/module#report), or print them on a timer with [`StartReporter()`](/reference/api/module#startreporter).

```lua copy
local stats = Network.Stats()

print("reliable bytes out", stats.BytesSent.Reliable)
print("damage events in", stats.EventBytesReceived.DealDamage)
print("rate limited", stats.DroppedPackets.RateLimit)
print("pending invokes", stats.PendingInvokes)
```

## What to watch

| Signal | Where | Suggests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bytes per endpoint | `EventBytesSent`, `EventBytesReceived` | Which endpoints to optimize first |
| Drops by reason | `DroppedPackets` | Attacks, bugs, or limits that are too tight |
| Rate limit hits | `RateLimitHits` | Limits below real usage if normal players appear |
| Queue drops | `QueueDrops` | Events arriving before listeners connect, or polling queues nobody reads |
| Invoke timeouts | `InvokeTimeouts` | Handlers too slow, or requests dropped by policies |
| Hook errors | `HookErrors` | Bugs in middleware, auth rules, policies or samplers |

Counters only increase. To get rates, subtract two snapshots.

```lua copy
local previous = Network.Stats()
while task.wait(60) do
    local current = Network.Stats()
    local sent = (current.BytesSent.Reliable or 0) - (previous.BytesSent.Reliable or 0)
    Analytics.Gauge("net.reliable_bytes_per_min", sent)
    previous = current
end
```

## Profiling

With [`EnableMicroProfiler`](/reference/options/runtime#enablemicroprofiler) on (the default), decoding and flushing appear in the MicroProfiler as `Cheeto.Decode.Reliable`, `Cheeto.Decode.Unreliable`, `Cheeto.Flush.Server` and `Cheeto.Flush.Client`.

## Turning metrics off

[`ExposeMetrics = false`](/reference/options/runtime#exposemetrics) makes `Stats`, `Report` and the inspector error. Counting continues internally.

```

`docs/pages/operations/production-checklist.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Production checklist"
description: "Everything to check before a schema goes live, and how to enforce it in CI."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Production checklist

## Schema options

```cheeto copy
option ClientOutput = "Network/Client.luau"
option ServerOutput = "Network/Server.luau"

option Version = 1
option MinimumSchemaVersion = 1

option SecurityProfile = Production
option RequirePolicies = true
option MaxPacketBytes = 65536
option RateLimitPerSecond = 120
option InvokeTimeoutSeconds = 10
option SyncValidation = false
option WriteValidations = false
option StrictProduction = true

event Ping {
    From: Client,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Policy: "ping",
    RateLimitPerSecond: 2
}
```

- [ ] `SecurityProfile` is `Production` or `Competitive`, or [`SecurityPreset = Maximum`](/security/maximum-security).
- [ ] `RequirePolicies = true`.
- [ ] `MaxPacketBytes`, `RateLimitPerSecond` and `InvokeTimeoutSeconds` are written explicitly. Strict mode does not count profile defaults, and the profile's invoke timeout is not applied to generated invokes.
- [ ] `SyncValidation` and `WriteValidations` are `false`.
- [ ] `Version` was increased if the wire layout changed.
- [ ] `StrictProduction = true`, so the build fails if any of the above regresses.

## Endpoints

- [ ] Every client-sent event and function has a `Policy`, `PolicyGroup` or `Auth`, and every name [`--doctor`](/reference/cli#--doctor) lists is registered. Unregistered names drop everything, so test every endpoint once.
- [ ] `cheeto.lock` is committed and CI runs `--check-lock`.
- [ ] Every client-sent endpoint has a cooldown or rate limit that fits real play.
- [ ] Types are tight: bounded strings and arrays, ranged numbers, classes on instances, no `unknown` from clients.
- [ ] Clients send intent (`BuyItem(itemId)`), never results (`SetCoins(amount)`).
- [ ] Objects clients act on are referred to by [handles](/security/handles-and-capabilities), not raw instances, where ownership matters.
- [ ] Constraint fields have a matching `Validate` hook or policy.
- [ ] Server-sent events and channels have no `Auth`, `Policy`, cooldown or rate-limit fields.
- [ ] A few [honeypots](/security/honeypots) are declared, and nothing calls them.

## Server code

- [ ] `Security.OnViolation` is connected and logs to somewhere you read.
- [ ] Every server teleport uses `Security.TeleportCharacter` if character integrity is on.
- [ ] Every function handler can error safely; clients `pcall` their invokes.

## CI

Run these on every change to the schema:

```sh copy
cheeto network --hardening-checklist --yes
cheeto network --check-lock --yes
cheeto network --benchmark --yes
```

| Command | Fails when |
| --- | --- |
| [`--hardening-checklist`](/reference/cli#--hardening-checklist) | Any strict check fails, `RequirePolicies` is off, or raw production capture is on |
| [`--check-lock`](/reference/cli#--check-lock) | The schema surface changed without an updated `cheeto.lock` |
| [`--benchmark`](/reference/cli#--benchmark) | Generated modules grew past the size thresholds |

<Callout type="info">
`--ci` runs doctor, benchmark, load-sim, capture-replay, golden-snapshots, compatibility, schema-docs and check-lock together, but not the hardening checklist. Run that separately.
</Callout>

## After launch

- [ ] Watch `Stats().DroppedPackets` and `RateLimitHits` on live servers; real players hitting limits means limits are too tight.
- [ ] Review violation logs weekly, and kill-switch any endpoint under active abuse.
- [ ] Keep security kicks off until reports from live servers look clean.

`docs/pages/reference/api/capture.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Capture"
description: "Record sent, received and dropped events, and replay them."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Capture

`Network.Capture` records what the module sends, receives and drops. See [Capture and replay](/operations/capture-and-replay) for workflows.

Capturing is off until [`Start`](#start) is called, [`EnablePacketCapture`](/reference/options/diagnostics#enablepacketcapture) is on, or the [Inspector](/reference/api/inspector) is enabled.

## Start

<Sig side="both">{"Start(options: { Limit: number?, Redactions: string | {string}? }?): ()"}</Sig>

Starts recording. `Limit` sets how many entries to keep (default [`CaptureLimit`](/reference/options/diagnostics#capturelimit)); `Redactions` replaces the redacted field names, as a comma-separated string or an array.

## Stop

<Sig side="both">{"Stop(): ()"}</Sig>

Stops recording started with `Start`. Entries are kept.

## Clear

<Sig side="both">{"Clear(): ()"}</Sig>

Deletes every recorded entry.

## Entries

<Sig side="both">{"Entries(): {CaptureEntry}"}</Sig>

A copy of the recorded entries, oldest first. Each entry has:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Name` | Endpoint name, `$handshake`, or `nil` for packet-level drops |
| `Direction` | `"send"` or `"receive"` |
| `Source` / `Target` | The peer, as a string |
| `UserId` | Sender's user id, for received events |
| `Channel` | `"Reliable"` or `"Unreliable"` |
| `Status` | `"accepted"` or `"dropped"` |
| `Reason` | Drop reason, for dropped entries |
| `Size` | Bytes |
| `PayloadSummary` | Readable summary of the values, with redacted fields shown as `[redacted]` |
| `Buffer`, `Instances` | Copy of the raw bytes and instances, when kept |
| `Redaction` | `{ Raw: boolean, Fields: {[string]: true} }` |
| `Time`, `WireFormat`, `SchemaVersion`, `SchemaHash` | Metadata |

Raw buffers are not kept when the profile is not `Development` and [`NoRawCaptureInProduction`](/reference/options/diagnostics#norawcaptureinproduction) is on.

## Replay

<Sig side="both">{"Replay(entries: {CaptureEntry}, handlers: {[string]: (entry) -> ()}?): { Accepted: number, Dropped: number, Replayed: number }"}</Sig>

Walks the entries and, for every accepted entry whose `Name` has a handler, calls the handler with the entry. Nothing is decoded or sent; this is for re-running your own logic against recorded traffic. Returns counts.

## ReplayRaw

<Sig side="both">{"ReplayRaw(entries: {CaptureEntry}, sourceOverride: any?): { Accepted, Dropped, Replayed, MissingRaw }"}</Sig>

Feeds each entry's raw bytes back through this module's real receive path, exactly as if they had arrived over the remote: guards, decoding, validation and listeners all run. Entries without raw bytes are counted in `MissingRaw`.

<Callout type="warning">
On the server, pass a real `Player` as `sourceOverride`: recorded sources are strings, and policies and listeners expect a player. Filter the entries to `Direction == "receive"` first, or your own sends are replayed as if they came from that player. Only use this in Studio or a private test server.
</Callout>

## Redact

<Sig side="both">{"Redact(fields: string | {string} | nil): ()"}</Sig>

Replaces the list of redacted field names. `nil` or `""` clears it.

```

`docs/pages/reference/api/channel.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Channel endpoint"
description: "Server writers and client readers generated for every channel."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Channel endpoint

Every [`channel`](/reference/declarations/channel) becomes `Network.<ChannelName>`. The server stores the state per player and decides when to send it; the client keeps the latest value it received.

In the signatures, `T` is the channel's `Data` type and `Patch` is a table of changed fields.

## Server

| Method | Targets |
| --- | --- |
| [`Set`](#set) / [`Patch`](#patch) / [`Flush`](#flush) | Chosen by [`Scope`](/reference/fields#scope) and [`Interest`](/reference/fields#interest) |
| `SetPlayer`, `PatchPlayer`, `FlushPlayer` | One player |
| `SetAll`, `PatchAll`, `FlushAll` | Every player |
| `SetList`, `PatchList`, `FlushList` | A list of players |
| `SetGroup`, `PatchGroup`, `FlushGroup` | A [group](/reference/api/module#setgroup) |
| `SetZone`, `PatchZone`, `FlushZone` | Players in a zone for this channel |
| `SetDistance`, `PatchDistance`, `FlushDistance` | Players near a position |
| [`SetScope`](#setscope), `PatchScope`, `FlushScope` | Players in a party, match, team, cell or owner set |
| [`SetInterestZone`](#setinterestzone), [`SetInterestPosition`](#setinterestposition) | Interest bookkeeping |
| [`Get`](#get-server), [`Clear`](#clear) | Read or forget stored state |

### Set

<Sig side="server">{"SetPlayer(player: Player, value: T): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"SetAll(value: T): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"SetList(players: {Player}, value: T): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"SetGroup(groupName: string, value: T): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"SetZone(zone: string, value: T): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"SetDistance(origin: Vector3, value: T, radius: number?): ()"}</Sig>

Stores a full value for each targeted player and marks them for a **full snapshot** at the next flush. `SetAll` also stores the value as the channel's global value, returned by `Get()` with no player. Players who have left are skipped.

`Set` without a suffix is `SetPlayer` for `Scope: Player` (the default), `SetAll` for `Scope: Global`, `SetGroup` for `Scope: Group`, `SetZone` for `Scope: Zone` or `Interest: Zone`, `SetDistance` for `Interest: Distance`, and `SetScope` with the declared kind for `Party`, `Match`, `Team`, `Cell` and `Owner`, called as `Set(key, value)`.

```lua copy
Network.PlayerState.Set(player, { Health = 100, Stamina = 100 })
```

### Patch

<Sig side="server">{"PatchPlayer(player: Player, patch: Patch): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"PatchAll(patch: Patch): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"PatchList(players: {Player}, patch: Patch): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"PatchGroup(groupName: string, patch: Patch): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"PatchZone(zone: string, patch: Patch): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"PatchDistance(origin: Vector3, patch: Patch, radius: number?): ()"}</Sig>

Merges the fields in `patch` into each targeted player's stored value and marks just those fields dirty. At the next flush, players with dirty fields get a **delta**: a bitmask plus the changed fields. Use [`State.Tombstone`](/reference/api/state#tombstone) as a value to clear an optional field.

Deltas require a struct `Data` and [`Delta`](/reference/fields#delta) not set to `false`. Otherwise a patch still updates the stored value, and the next flush sends it in full.

`Patch` without a suffix follows the same mapping as `Set`.

```lua copy
Network.PlayerState.Patch(player, { Health = 72 })
```

### Flush

<Sig side="server">{"FlushPlayer(player: Player, forceFull: boolean?): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"FlushAll(forceFull: boolean?): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"FlushList(players: {Player}, forceFull: boolean?): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"FlushGroup(groupName: string, forceFull: boolean?): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"FlushZone(zone: string, forceFull: boolean?): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"FlushDistance(origin: Vector3, radius: number?, forceFull: boolean?): ()"}</Sig>

Writes pending state into the targeted players' batches now, instead of waiting for the automatic flush. `forceFull` sends a full snapshot even when only deltas are pending. The batch itself still leaves at the next replication step.

`Flush` without a suffix is `FlushAll`.

Automatic flushing happens every replication step, limited by [`TickRate`](/reference/fields#tickrate), with a full snapshot forced every [`KeyframeRate`](/reference/fields#keyframerate) when set.

### SetScope

<Sig side="server">{"SetScope(kind: string, key: any, value: T): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"PatchScope(kind: string, key: any, patch: Patch): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"FlushScope(kind: string, key: any, forceFull: boolean?): ()"}</Sig>

Targets every player in a membership kept by [`Network.Replication`](/reference/api/replication): `kind` is `"Party"`, `"Match"`, `"Team"`, `"Cell"` or `"Owner"`, and `key` names the party, match, team, cell or owned object. `"Team"` also includes every player whose Roblox `Team` has that name. Available on every channel, whatever its `Scope`.

```lua copy
Network.Replication.SetParty(partyId, player, true)
Network.SquadState.SetScope("Party", partyId, { Objective = "Hold B", Score = 12 })
```

### SetInterestZone

<Sig side="server">{"SetInterestZone(player: Player, zone: string?): ()"}</Sig>

Records the zone a player is in for this channel, used by the `Zone` variants. `nil` removes the player from every zone of this channel.

### SetInterestPosition

<Sig side="server">{"SetInterestPosition(player: Player, position: Vector3?): ()"}</Sig>

Records a player's position for this channel, used by the `Distance` variants. The runtime does not track characters; call this from your own loop.

```lua copy
RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
    for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
        local root = player.Character and player.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
        Network.WorldEffects.SetInterestPosition(player, root and root.Position)
    end
end)
```

### Get (server)

<Sig side="server">{"Get(player: Player?): T?"}</Sig>

Returns the value stored for `player`, or the global value set by `SetAll` when called without a player.

### Clear

<Sig side="server">{"Clear(player: Player?): ()"}</Sig>

Forgets the stored value, pending deltas and pending snapshot for one player, or for everyone when called without a player. Nothing is sent to clients; their last value stays until the next `Set`.

## Client

### On

<Sig side="client">{"On(listener: (value: T, version: number, patch: Patch?) -> ()): () -> ()"}</Sig>

Called after every snapshot or delta is applied, with the full current value, the channel's version counter and, for deltas, the patch that was applied. Returns a disconnect function.

```lua copy
Network.PlayerState.On(function(state, version, patch)
    if patch == nil or patch.Health ~= nil then
        HealthBar.Set(state.Health)
    end
end)
```

<Callout type="info">
`On` does not fire for the value received before it was connected. Read [`Get`](#get-client) once when connecting, or use [`Connection:OnState`](/reference/api/connection#onstate) with `fireImmediately`.
</Callout>

### Get (client)

<Sig side="client">{"Get(): T?"}</Sig>

The latest value received, or `nil` if nothing has arrived yet.

### Version

<Sig side="client">{"Version(): number"}</Sig>

A counter that increases every time a snapshot or delta is applied. Useful for cheap change detection.

```

`docs/pages/reference/api/codecs.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Codecs"
description: "Quantization helpers for numbers, vectors and angles."
---

import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Codecs

`Network.Codecs` converts values to integers at a chosen precision so they fit small integer fields. Pair them with integer schema types. For most cases, declaring the encoding in the schema (`vector<i16>`, `f16`) is simpler.

## QuantizeNumber

<Sig side="both">{"QuantizeNumber(value: number, scale: number, min: number?, max: number?): number"}</Sig>

Clamps `value` to `min`..`max` (if given), multiplies by `scale` and rounds. With `scale = 100`, `12.345` becomes `1235`.

## DequantizeNumber

<Sig side="both">{"DequantizeNumber(value: number, scale: number): number"}</Sig>

Divides by `scale`.

## QuantizeVector3

<Sig side="both">{"QuantizeVector3(value: Vector3, scale: number): {number}"}</Sig>

Returns `{ x, y, z }`, each quantized with `scale`.

## DequantizeVector3

<Sig side="both">{"DequantizeVector3(value: {number}, scale: number): Vector3"}</Sig>

Rebuilds a `Vector3` from `{ x, y, z }`.

## QuantizeAngle

<Sig side="both">{"QuantizeAngle(radians: number, steps: number?): number"}</Sig>

Wraps `radians` to one turn and maps it onto `0`..`steps` (default 65,535, which fits a `u16`).

## DequantizeAngle

<Sig side="both">{"DequantizeAngle(value: number, steps: number?): number"}</Sig>

Maps back to radians in `0`..`2π`.

```cheeto copy
event Aim {
    From: Client,
    Type: Unreliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Policy: "aim",
    Data: (u16, u16)
}
```

```lua copy
local yaw = Network.Codecs.QuantizeAngle(camera.yaw)
local pitch = Network.Codecs.QuantizeAngle(camera.pitch)
Network.Aim.Fire(yaw, pitch)
```

`docs/pages/reference/api/connection.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Connection"
description: "Group endpoints and channels behind route names, inject them into controllers, and tear subscriptions down together."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Connection

`Network.Connection.new` creates an object that maps friendly route names to generated endpoints and channels, tracks every subscription made through it, and releases them all on `Disconnect`. Every message still goes through the generated endpoint, so encoding, validation and policies are unchanged. See [Controller connections](/guides/controller-connections) for a walkthrough.

## new

<Sig side="both">{"Connection.new(config: { Routes: {[string]: Endpoint}?, State: {[string]: Channel}?, Target: Player? }?): Connection"}</Sig>

`Routes` maps names to event or function endpoints (or plain functions). `State` maps names to channel endpoints (`States` is accepted as an alias). `Target` is a player that server-side sends and state writes are addressed to automatically.

```lua copy
local connection = Network.Connection.new({
    Routes = { Action = Network.UIAction, Message = Network.UIMessage },
    State = { UI = Network.UI },
})
```

## Methods

Every method errors with `Connection is disconnected.` after [`Disconnect`](#disconnect), and with `Connection route "X" is not bound.` for an unknown name.

### Bind

<Sig side="both">{"connection:Bind(name: string, endpoint: Endpoint | function): Connection"}</Sig>

Adds or replaces a route. Returns the connection, so calls chain.

### BindState

<Sig side="both">{"connection:BindState(name: string, channel: Channel): Connection"}</Sig>

Adds or replaces a state channel. Returns the connection.

### SetTarget

<Sig side="both">{"connection:SetTarget(target: Player?): Connection"}</Sig>

Changes the target player. Returns the connection.

### Send

<Sig side="both">{"connection:Send(name: string, ...data): ...any"}</Sig>

Calls the route's `Fire` (or `Invoke`, or the function itself). With a target, the target is passed as the first argument. Returns whatever the endpoint returns, so for a function route it yields for the reply. Errors if the route cannot send on this side.

### On

<Sig side="both">{"connection:On(name: string, listener: (...) -> ()): () -> ()"}</Sig>

Connects to the route's `On` and tracks the subscription. Returns a disconnect function. A target does **not** filter incoming events; server listeners still receive every sender.

### Once

<Sig side="both">{"connection:Once(name: string, listener: ((...) -> ())?): () -> ()"}</Sig>

Like `On`, but disconnects after the first event.

### GetState

<Sig side="both">{"connection:GetState(name: string): any"}</Sig>

Reads the channel's current value: the client's latest value, or on the server the value stored for the target (or the global value without one).

### OnState

<Sig side="client">{"connection:OnState(name: string, listener: (value, version, patch) -> (), fireImmediately: boolean?): () -> ()"}</Sig>

Subscribes to a channel's changes. With `fireImmediately`, the listener is also called right away with the current value.

### SetState, PatchState, ClearState, FlushState

<Sig side="server">{"connection:SetState(name: string, ...): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"connection:PatchState(name: string, ...): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"connection:ClearState(name: string, ...): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="server">{"connection:FlushState(name: string, ...): ()"}</Sig>

Write to a bound channel through its `Set`, `Patch`, `Clear` or `Flush`. With a target, the target is prepended, and `FlushState` uses `FlushPlayer`. Without one, pass the player yourself, and `FlushState` flushes everyone. Clients cannot write channels, so these error on the client.

```lua copy
local connection = Network.Connection.new({ Target = player, State = { UI = Network.UI } })
connection:SetState("UI", { Visible = true, Title = "Welcome" })
connection:PatchState("UI", { Title = "Ready" })
```

### IsConnected

<Sig side="both">{"connection:IsConnected(): boolean"}</Sig>

`false` after `Disconnect`.

### Disconnect

<Sig side="both">{"connection:Disconnect(): ()"}</Sig>

Releases every subscription made through `On`, `Once` and `OnState`, and makes further calls error. Calling it twice is safe. `Destroy` is an alias.

<Callout type="info">
Subscriptions you create directly on endpoints, without the connection, are not tracked.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/api/diagnostics.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Diagnostics"
description: "Listener counts per endpoint."
---

import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Diagnostics

## Listeners

<Sig side="both">{"Listeners(): {[string]: number}"}</Sig>

The number of listeners connected to each event, by endpoint name. Use it to spot events with no listener, or listener counts that keep growing because a controller connects without disconnecting.

```lua copy
for name, count in Network.Diagnostics.Listeners() do
    if count > 5 then
        warn(name, "has", count, "listeners")
    end
end
```

For live connect and disconnect notifications, use the [`Listener`](/reference/api/hooks#listener) hook.

`docs/pages/reference/api/event.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Event endpoint"
description: "Methods generated for every event: Fire, FireAll, FireList, FireExcept, FireGroup, Predict, On and Iter."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Event endpoint

Every [`event`](/reference/declarations/event) becomes a table on the module, `Network.<EventName>`. Which methods it has depends on the side and on `From`. Method names follow [`Casing`](/reference/options/output#casing); this page uses `Pascal`.

In the signatures, `...data` stands for the event's `Data`: one value, several values for a type pack, or nothing.

| Method | Exists on | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`Fire`](#fire) | sending side | always |
| [`FireAll`](#fireall), [`FireList`](#firelist), [`FireExcept`](#fireexcept), [`FireGroup`](#firegroup) | server | `From: Server` |
| [`Predict`](#predict) | client | `From: Client`, unless prediction is disabled |
| [`On`](#on) | receiving side | `Call` is not `Polling` |
| [`Iter`](#iter) | receiving side | `Call: Polling` or `Poll: true` |
| [`Next`](#next) | receiving side | deprecated alias of `Iter` |

## Fire

<Sig side="server">{"Fire(player: Player, ...data): ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="client">{"Fire(...data): ()"}</Sig>

Sends the event to one player (server) or to the server (client).

- **Reliable** events are appended to that peer's batch and sent at the next replication step, in order with every other reliable event to the same peer.
- **Unreliable** events are sent immediately as one `UnreliableRemoteEvent` call. One that encodes larger than [`MaxUnreliablePacketBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxunreliablepacketbytes) is dropped on the sender.

A send is silently dropped when the endpoint is [killed](/reference/api/security#kill), a [`BeforeSend`](/reference/api/hooks#beforesend) hook returns `false`, or [backpressure](/reference/fields#priority) sheds it. A value that cannot be serialized, such as a string where a number is declared, raises an error at the call site.

```lua copy
Network.Announce.Fire(player, "Welcome back")
```

## FireAll

<Sig side="server">{"FireAll(...data): ()"}</Sig>

Sends to every player in the server. The value is encoded once and copied into each player's batch; an unreliable event uses a single `FireAllClients`.

## FireList

<Sig side="server">{"FireList(players: {Player}, ...data): ()"}</Sig>

Sends to each player in the list.

## FireExcept

<Sig side="server">{"FireExcept(except: Player, ...data): ()"}</Sig>

Sends to every player except one, typically the player whose action caused the event.

```lua copy
Network.PlayerEmoted.FireExcept(player, player, "wave")
```

## FireGroup

<Sig side="server">{"FireGroup(groupName: string, ...data): ()"}</Sig>

Sends to every member of a group set with [`SetGroup`](/reference/api/module#setgroup) or [`AddToGroup`](/reference/api/module#addtogroup). An unknown group sends to nobody.

## Predict

<Sig side="client">{"Predict(...data): number"}</Sig>

Sends the event like `Fire`, but also starts a [prediction](/concepts/prediction) and returns its id. The packet carries the id as a sequence number, which enables [replay protection](/reference/options/limits#replaywindowsize) and [`Idempotency`](/reference/fields#idempotency) for it.

When the server decodes the event successfully it replies with an acknowledgement, and the client calls [`Prediction.Ack`](/reference/api/prediction#ack) for you. If decoding fails it replies with a rejection and the client calls [`Prediction.Rollback`](/reference/api/prediction#rollback) with the reason.

<Callout type="warning">
An event dropped before decoding (by a policy, auth rule, cooldown, rate limit or kill switch) gets **no** reply, so its prediction stays in [`Prediction.Pending`](/reference/api/prediction#pending) until you roll it back. Expire old pending predictions yourself.
</Callout>

Errors when prediction is disabled with [`EnablePrediction`](/reference/options/runtime#enableprediction).

```lua copy
local id = Network.PlaceBlock.Predict(position)
Blocks.PlaceLocally(position, id)
```

## On

<Sig side="server">{"On(listener: (player: Player, ...data) -> ()): () -> ()"}</Sig>
<Sig side="client">{"On(listener: (...data) -> ()): () -> ()"}</Sig>

Connects a listener and returns a function that disconnects it.

| `Call` | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `SingleSync`, `SingleAsync` | One listener. Calling `On` again replaces the previous one |
| `ManySync`, `ManyAsync` | Any number of listeners |
| `*Sync` | Listener runs inline and must not yield |
| `*Async` | Listener runs in a new thread |

Reliable events that arrived before any listener was connected are queued (up to [`MaxQueuedEvents`](/reference/fields#maxqueuedevents)) and delivered to the first listener as soon as it connects.

Each connect and disconnect runs the [`Listener`](/reference/api/hooks#listener) hook, and [`Diagnostics.Listeners`](/reference/api/diagnostics#listeners) counts them.

```lua copy
local disconnect = Network.ChatMessage.On(function(player, text)
    Chat.Post(player, text)
end)
```

## Iter

<Sig side="both">{"Iter(): () -> (number, ...)"}</Sig>

For polling events. Returns an iterator that removes and yields every queued event, in arrival order, as `(index, [player,] ...data)`. The server side includes the sending player. Events that arrive while you iterate are included.

```lua copy
RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
    for index, player, input in Network.Input.Iter() do
        Simulation.Apply(player, input)
    end
end)
```

Received polling events wait in a queue bounded by [`MaxQueuedEvents`](/reference/fields#maxqueuedevents). If nothing reads the queue, new events are dropped with `QueueFull` once it is full.

## Next

<Sig side="both" deprecated>{"Next(): () -> (number, ...)"}</Sig>

Identical to [`Iter`](#iter). Kept for compatibility; use `Iter`.

```

`docs/pages/reference/api/exports.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Exported type"
description: "Read and Write functions generated for types declared with export."
---

import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Exported type

Every type declared with [`export`](/reference/declarations/export) becomes `Network.<TypeName>` with two functions, on both modules.

## Write

<Sig side="both">{"Write(value: T): buffer"}</Sig>

Serializes `value` into a new buffer sized exactly to fit, using the module's current [encoding options](/reference/options/encoding). Errors if the value does not match the type.

## Read

<Sig side="both">{"Read(data: buffer): T"}</Sig>

Deserializes a buffer produced by `Write`. Errors if the buffer is too short or a value fails its range check.

```lua copy
local encoded = Network.Snapshot.Write({ Tick = 120, Position = position, Health = 90 })
DataStore:SetAsync(key, buffer.tostring(encoded))

local decoded = Network.Snapshot.Read(buffer.fromstring(DataStore:GetAsync(key)))
```

Values containing `Instance` or `unknown` do not round-trip through a standalone buffer.

```

`docs/pages/reference/api/function.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Function endpoint"
description: "Invoke on the client and On on the server, generated for every function."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Function endpoint

Every [`function`](/reference/declarations/function) becomes `Network.<FunctionName>`, with `Invoke` on the client and `On` on the server.

## Invoke

<Sig side="client" yields>{"Invoke(...data): ...return"}</Sig>

Sends a request and waits for the server's reply. With `Yield: Coroutine` it yields the calling thread and returns the reply's values. With `Future` or `Promise` it returns immediately with a Future or Promise that resolves to them.

The request is appended to the client's reliable batch, so it leaves at the next replication step.

**Errors** (raised by `Invoke`, or rejected by the Future/Promise):

| Message | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `There was an exception while processing "Name".` | The server's listener errored |
| `Invoke timed out after N seconds.` | No reply within [`InvokeTimeoutSeconds`](/reference/fields#invoketimeoutseconds) |
| `The server rejected "Name": <reason>` | The server dropped the call before the handler ran, or the handler failed (`HandlerError`) |
| `More than N calls ... are awaiting a response` | [`MaxPendingInvokes`](/reference/fields#maxpendinginvokes) reached |
| `Invocation id is already awaiting a response` | More than 255 invokes outstanding |
| `Invoke was cancelled.` or your reason | [`CancelInvocations`](/reference/api/module#cancelinvocations) was called |

```lua copy
local ok, inventory = pcall(Network.GetInventory.Invoke, 1)
if not ok then
    warn("Inventory request failed:", inventory)
end
```

<Callout type="warning">
A request the server drops before running the listener is answered with the reason, so `Invoke` fails straight away instead of waiting for its timeout. Only [honeypot](/reference/fields#honeypot) functions stay silent.
</Callout>

## On

<Sig side="server">{"On(listener: (player: Player, ...data) -> ...return): () -> ()"}</Sig>

Sets the function's handler. There is one handler per function; calling `On` again replaces it. The handler runs in its own thread, may yield, and its return values are sent back to the invoking client. If it errors, or returns something that does not fit the `Return` type, the error is logged on the server and the client's `Invoke` raises `The server rejected "Name": HandlerError`.

Requests that arrive before a handler is set are queued and handled once `On` is called. `On` returns a function that unbinds the handler if it is still the bound one; requests arriving after that queue again until the next `On`.

```lua copy
Network.GetInventory.On(function(player, page)
    local inventory = Inventories[player]
    if not inventory then
        error("No inventory loaded")
    end
    return { Items = inventory:Page(page), Capacity = inventory.Capacity }
end)
```

If the invoking player leaves before the handler returns, the reply is discarded.

```

`docs/pages/reference/api/handles.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Handles"
description: "Server-issued numeric handles for objects, and expiring capability grants."
---

import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Handles

`Network.Handles` lets the server give clients a number that stands for an object, instead of letting clients name objects directly. The server resolves the number back and checks who is using it. See [Handles and capabilities](/security/handles-and-capabilities).

These functions exist on both modules, but handles and capabilities only live in the module that issued them. Register them on the server and resolve them on the server.

## Register

<Sig side="both">{"Register(object: any, owner: Player?, expiresAt: number?): number"}</Sig>

Returns a handle for `object`. Registering the same object again returns the same handle and updates its owner and expiry. `owner` restricts who can resolve it. `expiresAt` is an absolute `os.clock()` time.

```lua copy
local handle = Network.Handles.Register(buildPiece, player, os.clock() + 60)
Network.PieceSpawned.Fire(player, handle)
```

## Resolve

<Sig side="both">{"Resolve(handle: number, player: Player?): any?"}</Sig>

Returns the object for a handle, or `nil` if the handle is unknown, expired (it is then removed), or owned by someone other than `player`. Passing `nil` for `player` skips the owner check, so always pass the sender when resolving a client's request.

```lua copy
Network.MovePiece.On(function(player, handle, cframe)
    local piece = Network.Handles.Resolve(handle, player)
    if piece then
        piece:PivotTo(cframe)
    end
end)
```

## Revoke

<Sig side="both">{"Revoke(handle: number): ()"}</Sig>

Removes a handle immediately.

## IssueCapability

<Sig side="both">{"IssueCapability(object: any, owner: Player?, permissions: {[string]: boolean}?, durationSeconds: number?): number"}</Sig>

Returns a one-off token granting `owner` the listed permissions on `object` for `durationSeconds` (default 30). Unlike handles, each call returns a new token.

```lua copy
local token = Network.Handles.IssueCapability(plot, player, { Edit = true }, 15)
```

## ValidateCapability

<Sig side="both">{"ValidateCapability(token: number, player: Player?, permission: string?): any?"}</Sig>

Returns the object if the token exists, has not expired, belongs to `player`, and grants `permission`. Otherwise returns `nil`; expired tokens are removed.

```

`docs/pages/reference/api/hooks.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Middleware hooks"
description: "Every hook name accepted by Use, when it runs, what it receives, and whether it can reject."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Middleware hooks

Register a hook with [`Network.Use(name, callback)`](/reference/api/module#use). Each callback receives one context table. Hooks marked **can reject** stop the packet when a callback returns exactly `false`; for the others the return value is ignored. A callback that errors is logged and counted in `HookErrors`, and processing continues as if it returned nothing.

Hooks run only while [`EnableMiddleware`](/reference/options/runtime#enablemiddleware) is on. They run on the side where the module is required.

| Hook | When | Can reject | Drop reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`BeforeSend`](#beforesend) | Before an event is written | Yes | `MiddlewareRejected` |
| [`AfterSend`](#aftersend) | After an event is queued, and after each remote call | No | |
| [`BeforeReceive`](#beforereceive) | Before a packet, then before each event in it | Yes | `MiddlewareRejected` |
| [`Validate`](#validate) | After decoding, before the listener | Yes | `ConstraintRejected` |
| [`AfterReceive`](#afterreceive) | After an event is decoded and accepted | No | |
| [`Drop`](#drop) | When anything is dropped | No | |
| [`Error`](#error) | When decoding an event fails | No | |
| [`Violation`](#violation) | For every drop and security report | No | |
| [`Predict`](#predict), [`Ack`](#ack), [`Rollback`](#rollback) | Prediction lifecycle | No | |
| [`Listener`](#listener) | A listener connects or disconnects | No | |
| [`Telemetry`](#telemetry) | Internal events worth logging | No | |

## BeforeSend

**Can reject.** Runs before an event, invoke reply or channel update is serialized.

```lua
{ Name: string, Channel: "Reliable" | "Unreliable", Target: Player? }
```

`Target` is `nil` for broadcasts and for everything the client sends.

## AfterSend

Runs twice for a reliable event: once when it is queued, with `Name`, and once when the batch containing it is sent over the remote, without `Name`. Unreliable events also run it for their remote call.

```lua
{ Name: string?, Channel: string, Size: number, Target: Player? }
```

## BeforeReceive

**Can reject.** Runs once per received remote call, before anything is decoded:

```lua
{ Source: Player | "Server", Channel: string, Size: number }
```

and again for each event in the packet, after its size and rate checks and before auth and policy:

```lua
{ Name: string, Source: Player | "Server", Channel: string, Size: number }
```

`Size` is the size of the whole packet in both cases.

## Validate

**Can reject.** Runs after an event's payload is decoded and before its listener, **only for endpoints that declare a payload constraint** (`MaxDistance` or a `Require*` field other than `RequireCharacterState`). This is the only hook that can inspect decoded data and reject it.

```lua
{
    Name: string,
    Source: Player | "Server",
    Channel: string,
    Size: number,
    Constraints: Constraints,
    Payload: { n: number, [number]: any }, -- the event's values, as table.pack(...)
}
```

`Constraints` has every constraint field: `Risk`, `CooldownSeconds`, `MaxDistance`, `RequireOwnership`, `RequireTeam`, `RequireZone`, `RequireMatch`, `RequireInventoryOwnership`, `RequireCharacterState`, `RequireObjectHandle`, `RequireServerKnownId`, `Idempotency`. Undeclared ones are `nil`, `false` or `0`.

```lua copy
Network.Use("Validate", function(context)
    local maxDistance = context.Constraints.MaxDistance
    if maxDistance > 0 then
        local target = context.Payload[1].Target
        return Distance(context.Source, target) <= maxDistance
    end
    return true
end)
```

See [Constraints and Validate](/security/constraints).

## AfterReceive

Runs after an event is decoded and passes validation, just before its listener is called or it is queued.

```lua
{ Name: string, Source: Player | "Server", Channel: string, Size: number }
```

## Drop

Runs for every dropped packet or event, in either direction.

```lua
{ Name: string?, Source: any, Channel: string, Reason: string, Size: number }
```

`Reason` is one of the [drop reasons](/reference/drop-reasons), or a custom reason returned by a policy.

## Error

Runs when an event's payload fails to decode, just before it is dropped as `MalformedPacket`.

```lua
{ Name: string, Source: Player | "Server", Channel: string, Error: string }
```

## Violation

Runs for every drop and for every client shield, client integrity and character integrity report. [`Security.OnViolation`](/reference/api/security#onviolation) is a shortcut that registers this hook. The context is a [`ViolationReport`](/reference/violation-report).

## Predict

Runs when [`Predict`](/reference/api/event#predict) or [`Prediction.Begin`](/reference/api/prediction#begin) starts a prediction.

```lua
{ Id: number, Name: string, Payload: any }
```

## Ack

Runs when a prediction is acknowledged.

```lua
{ Id: number, Prediction: { Name: string, Payload: any, Started: number } }
```

## Rollback

Runs when a prediction is rolled back.

```lua
{ Id: number, Prediction: { Name: string, Payload: any, Started: number }, Reason: string? }
```

## Listener

Runs when an event listener connects or disconnects.

```lua
{ Name: string, Listener: function, Count: number, Duplicate: boolean, Action: "connect" | "disconnect" }
```

`Duplicate` is `true` when the same function was connected twice to the same event, which usually means a controller initialized twice.

## Telemetry

A single stream for internal events you may want to forward to logging.

```lua
{ Name: string, Payload: any, Time: number }
```

| `Name` | Payload |
| --- | --- |
| `security.violation` | The [`ViolationReport`](/reference/violation-report) |
| `security.clientShield` | Shield report entry |
| `security.clientIntegrity` | Integrity evidence entry |
| `security.characterIntegrity` | Movement evidence entry |
| `security.characterIntegrityError` | `{ Player, UserId, Error, Time }` when sampling a character failed |
| `transport.flush` | `{ Target, Channel, Size, QueuedBytes, QueuedEvents }` |
| `transport.fragment` | `{ Target, FragmentId, Count, Size }` |
| `transport.reassembled` | `{ Source, FragmentId, Count, Size }` |

<Callout type="info">
Hooks run on the networking hot path. Keep them cheap, and do not yield in them: a yielding hook delays every event after it in the same packet.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/api/inspector.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Inspector"
description: "A single diagnostic snapshot of the module's state."
---

import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Inspector

`Network.Inspector` gathers the module's diagnostic state into one table, for debug UIs and bug reports. Enabling it also turns on capture recording. See [Inspector](/operations/inspector).

## Enable

<Sig side="both">{"Enable(enabled: boolean): ()"}</Sig>

Turns the inspector on or off for this module, independent of the [`EnableInspector`](/reference/options/diagnostics#enableinspector) option.

## Snapshot

<Sig side="both">{"Snapshot(): InspectorSnapshot"}</Sig>

Errors with `Inspector is disabled` unless the inspector is enabled. Returns:

| Field | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `Metrics` | Same as [`Stats()`](/reference/api/module#stats) |
| `Protocol` | Same as [`Protocol.Info()`](/reference/api/protocol#info) |
| `Peers` | Copy of [`Protocol.Peers`](/reference/api/protocol#peers) |
| `Capture` | Same as [`Capture.Entries()`](/reference/api/capture#entries) |
| `ClientIntegrity` | Same as [`Security.ClientIntegrity()`](/reference/api/security#clientintegrity) |
| `CharacterIntegrity` | Same as [`Security.CharacterIntegrity()`](/reference/api/security#characterintegrity) |
| `Runtime` | `{ WireFormat, SchemaVersion, SchemaHash, SecurityProfile }` |

```lua copy
Network.Inspector.Enable(true)
task.wait(30)
print(Network.Inspector.Snapshot().Metrics.DroppedPackets)
```

`docs/pages/reference/api/module.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Network module"
description: "Members on the root of the table returned by a generated Server or Client module."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Network module

Requiring a generated module returns a frozen table. It holds one entry per declared endpoint (see [Event](/reference/api/event), [Function](/reference/api/function), [Channel](/reference/api/channel) and [Exported type](/reference/api/exports)), plus the members on this page and the namespaces listed at the bottom.

```lua copy
local Network = require(ReplicatedStorage.Network.Server)
```

The server module errors when required on a client, and the client module errors when required on the server. Requiring two modules with the same [`RemoteScope`](/reference/options/output#remotescope) on one side also errors.

## Summary

| Member | Side | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`StepReplication`](#stepreplication) | Both | Flush queued events now |
| [`Stats`](#stats) | Both | Copy of all metric counters |
| [`Report`](#report) | Both | Print and return metrics |
| [`StartReporter`](#startreporter) | Both | Print metrics on an interval |
| [`Configure`](#configure) | Both | Change runtime options |
| [`Use`](#use) | Both | Add a middleware hook |
| [`UseAuth`](#useauth) | Both | Register an auth rule |
| [`CancelInvocations`](#cancelinvocations) | Both | Fail every pending `Invoke` |
| [`SetGroup`](#setgroup), [`AddToGroup`](#addtogroup), [`RemoveFromGroup`](#removefromgroup), [`GetGroupPlayers`](#getgroupplayers) | Both, used on the server | Named player groups |
| [`SetInterestZone`](#setinterestzone), [`GetInterestZonePlayers`](#getinterestzoneplayers), [`SetInterestPosition`](#setinterestposition), [`GetInterestDistancePlayers`](#getinterestdistanceplayers) | Both, used on the server | Per-channel zone and distance interest |

## StepReplication

<Sig side="both">{"StepReplication(): ()"}</Sig>

Runs one replication step: expires timed-out invokes, runs integrity checks (server), flushes channel state (server), and sends every peer's queued reliable batch.

By default this is connected to `RunService.Heartbeat` and you never call it. With [`ManualReplication`](/reference/options/runtime#manualreplication) on, you must call it yourself, typically once per frame.

```lua copy
RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(Network.StepReplication)
```

## Stats

<Sig side="both">{"Stats(): Metrics"}</Sig>

Returns a copy of the module's counters. Each bucket is a table of counts keyed as shown. Errors with `Metrics are disabled` when [`ExposeMetrics`](/reference/options/runtime#exposemetrics) is `false`.

| Key | Keyed by | Counts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BytesSent`, `BytesReceived` | `"Reliable"` / `"Unreliable"` | Bytes over each remote |
| `PacketsSent`, `PacketsReceived` | channel | Remote calls |
| `EventBytesSent`, `EventBytesReceived` | endpoint name | Bytes per endpoint |
| `DroppedPackets` | [drop reason](/reference/drop-reasons) | Drops |
| `ValidationFailures` | channel | Malformed and auth-rejected packets |
| `RateLimitHits` | channel or endpoint | Rate limit drops |
| `QueueDrops` | channel | `QueueFull` drops |
| `InvokeTimeouts` | function name | Timed-out invokes |
| `HookErrors` | hook name | Middleware and rule errors |
| `MiddlewareRejections` | hook name or channel | Hooks returning `false` |
| `ClientShieldReports`, `ClientIntegrityReceipts`, `ClientIntegrityFailures`, `CharacterIntegrityActions` | reason or action | Security events |
| `PendingInvokes` | (number) | Invokes awaiting a reply |
| `PendingInvokesByName` | function name | Pending invokes per function |
| `CapturedPackets` | (number) | Entries in the capture buffer |

```lua copy
local stats = Network.Stats()
print(stats.DroppedPackets.RateLimit or 0)
```

## Report

<Sig side="both">{"Report(): Metrics"}</Sig>

Prints every metric bucket to the output, one line per bucket, and returns the same table as [`Stats`](#stats).

## StartReporter

<Sig side="both">{"StartReporter(intervalSeconds: number?): () -> ()"}</Sig>

Calls [`Report`](#report) every `intervalSeconds` (default 5) in a background thread. Returns a function that stops it.

```lua copy
local stop = Network.StartReporter(10)
task.delay(60, stop)
```

## Configure

<Sig side="both">{"Configure(options: {[string]: any}): ()"}</Sig>

Changes runtime options on this module only. Keys are option names from the schema, such as `RateLimitPerSecond` or `EnableHoneypots`.

- An unknown key errors with `Unknown runtime option`.
- Unknown keys error, including the removed `ProtocolVersion`, `ProtocolMode` and `AcceptProtocolVersion1`.
- `CharacterIntegrityMode` must be `Observe`, `Report`, `Correct` or `Kick` (any case).
- Options that only affect code generation, such as `MaxQueuedEvents`, per-endpoint limits or function timeouts, are accepted but change nothing.

```lua copy
Network.Configure({
    RateLimitPerSecond = 30,
    RateLimitBurst = 60,
    EnableHoneypots = true,
})
```

<Callout type="warning">
Configure both the server and client modules when an option affects both sides, and never change [encoding options](/reference/options/encoding) at runtime.
</Callout>

## Use

<Sig side="both">{"Use(hookName: string, callback: (context) -> boolean?): () -> ()"}</Sig>

Adds a middleware callback. Hooks run in the order they were added. For hooks that can reject, returning exactly `false` stops the packet; any other return value continues. A callback that errors is logged, counted in `HookErrors`, and treated as continue.

Returns a function that removes the callback. An unknown hook name errors. See [Middleware hooks](/reference/api/hooks) for every name and context.

```lua copy
local remove = Network.Use("BeforeReceive", function(context)
    return context.Size < 4096
end)
```

## UseAuth

<Sig side="both">{"UseAuth(name: string, rule: (context) -> boolean): ()"}</Sig>

Registers, or replaces, the [auth rule](/security/auth-rules) that endpoints name in their `Auth` field. The rule receives `{ Name, Source, Channel, Size }` and must return exactly `true` to allow the event. Errors in the rule deny.

The rules `AlivePlayer` and `ServerOnly` are built in.

```lua copy
Network.UseAuth("HasCharacter", function(context)
    local player = context.Source
    return player.Character ~= nil and player.Character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") ~= nil
end)
```

## CancelInvocations

<Sig side="both">{"CancelInvocations(reason: string?): ()"}</Sig>

Resumes every pending `Invoke` on this module with an error, using `reason` as the message (default `Invoke was cancelled.`). Use it when tearing down a client state that should abandon outstanding requests.

## SetGroup

<Sig side="both">{"SetGroup(name: string, players: {Player}): ()"}</Sig>

Replaces the members of a named group. Groups are the audience for [`FireGroup`](/reference/api/event#firegroup) and channel `SetGroup`, `PatchGroup` and `FlushGroup`. Players are removed from every group automatically when they leave.

## AddToGroup

<Sig side="both">{"AddToGroup(name: string, player: Player): ()"}</Sig>

Adds one player to a group, creating the group if needed.

## RemoveFromGroup

<Sig side="both">{"RemoveFromGroup(name: string, player: Player): ()"}</Sig>

Removes one player from a group.

## GetGroupPlayers

<Sig side="both">{"GetGroupPlayers(name: string): {Player}"}</Sig>

Returns the group's members as an array. An unknown group returns an empty array.

```lua copy
Network.SetGroup("Admins", { owner })
Network.AddToGroup("Admins", moderator)
Network.AuditLog.FireGroup("Admins", "Server restarted")
```

## SetInterestZone

<Sig side="both">{"SetInterestZone(channelName: string, player: Player, zone: string?): ()"}</Sig>

Records which zone a player is in for one channel, or clears it with `nil`. Used by the channel `SetZone`, `PatchZone` and `FlushZone` variants. Channel endpoints also expose this as `Channel.SetInterestZone(player, zone)`.

## GetInterestZonePlayers

<Sig side="both">{"GetInterestZonePlayers(channelName: string, zone: string): {Player}"}</Sig>

Players currently in `zone` for that channel.

## SetInterestPosition

<Sig side="both">{"SetInterestPosition(channelName: string, player: Player, position: Vector3?): ()"}</Sig>

Records a player's position for distance-based interest on one channel, or clears it. The runtime does not read character positions itself; update this from your own loop.

## GetInterestDistancePlayers

<Sig side="both">{"GetInterestDistancePlayers(channelName: string, origin: Vector3, radius: number): {Player}"}</Sig>

Players whose recorded position for that channel is within `radius` studs of `origin`.

## Namespaces

| Namespace | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`Security`](/reference/api/security) | Policies, violations, kill switches, shield and integrity controls |
| [`Transport`](/reference/api/transport) | Queue and flush state, network stats, drop reason list |
| [`Protocol`](/reference/api/protocol) | Handshake results |

| [`Replication`](/reference/api/replication) | Party, match, team, cell and owner audiences; cross-server adapters |

| [`Codecs`](/reference/api/codecs) | Number, vector and angle quantization |
| [`Connection`](/reference/api/connection) | Route and lifecycle wrapper for controllers |
| [`Capture`](/reference/api/capture) | Packet capture and replay |

| [`Schema`](/reference/api/schema) | Version info and payload migrations |
| [`Diagnostics`](/reference/api/diagnostics) | Listener counts |

`docs/pages/reference/api/prediction.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Prediction"
description: "Track client predictions and resolve them with server acknowledgements."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Prediction

`Network.Prediction` tracks predictions started with an event's [`Predict`](/reference/api/event#predict) method. See [Prediction](/concepts/prediction) for the full flow.

All members error with `Prediction helpers are disabled` when [`EnablePrediction`](/reference/options/runtime#enableprediction) is off.

## Begin

<Sig side="both">{"Begin(name: string, payload: any): number"}</Sig>

Starts a prediction without sending anything and returns its id. `Predict` calls this for you; call it directly only to track predictions for actions that are not a single event. Ids count up to 65,535 and then wrap. Runs the [`Predict`](/reference/api/hooks#predict) hook.

## Ack

<Sig side="both">{"Ack(id: number): Prediction?"}</Sig>

Marks a prediction confirmed, removes it from [`Pending`](#pending), runs the [`Ack`](/reference/api/hooks#ack) hook and returns it. Returns `nil` for an unknown id. The client calls this automatically when the server accepts a predicted event.

## Rollback

<Sig side="both">{"Rollback(id: number, reason: string?): Prediction?"}</Sig>

Marks a prediction rejected, removes it, runs the [`Rollback`](/reference/api/hooks#rollback) hook and returns it. The client calls this automatically when the server fails to decode a predicted event.

## Pending

<Sig side="both">{"Pending: {[number]: { Name: string, Payload: any, Started: number }}"}</Sig>

The live table of unresolved predictions by id. `Payload` is the packed arguments.

<Callout type="warning">
The server only replies to predicted events it decodes. Events dropped earlier, by a policy, cooldown or rate limit, stay pending forever. Roll back predictions older than a timeout yourself:

```lua copy
RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
    local now = os.clock()
    for id, prediction in Network.Prediction.Pending do
        if now - prediction.Started > 2 then
            Network.Prediction.Rollback(id, "timeout")
        end
    end
end)
```
</Callout>

Handle results with hooks:

```lua copy
Network.Use("Rollback", function(context)
    Blocks.UndoLocal(context.Id)
end)
```

```

`docs/pages/reference/api/protocol.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Protocol"
description: "Results of the capability handshake."
---

import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Protocol

`Network.Protocol` reports what the [handshake](/reference/options/versioning#enableprotocolhandshake) learned about each peer.

## Info

<Sig side="both">{"Info(peer: any?): ProtocolInfo"}</Sig>

Returns this module's versions and what a peer reported:

```lua
{
    WireFormat: number,
    LocalSchemaVersion: number,
    MinimumSchemaVersion: number,
    SchemaHash: string,
    Peer: {
        WireFormat: number,
        SchemaVersion: number,
        MinimumSchemaVersion: number,
        SchemaHash: string,
        Compatible: boolean,
        LastSeen: number,
    }?,
}
```

`Peer` is `nil` until that peer's handshake has been received. On the server, pass a player. On the client, pass nothing.

```lua copy
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    task.wait(10)
    local peer = Network.Protocol.Info(player).Peer
    if peer and not peer.Compatible then
        player:Kick("Please rejoin: this server is running a different version.")
    end
end)
```

## Peers

<Sig side="both">{"Peers: {[any]: PeerCapability}"}</Sig>

The live table of every peer's handshake, keyed by player (or by an internal key for the server). Read it; do not modify it.

## QueueHandshake

<Sig side="both">{"QueueHandshake(peer: any?): ()"}</Sig>

Writes this module's handshake into the current outgoing batch if it has not been sent yet. The generated code calls it on every send, so you rarely need it.
