`docs/pages/reference/api/replication.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Replication"
description: "Party, match, team, cell and owner audiences, routing graphs, and cross-server adapters."
---

import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Replication

`Network.Replication` keeps audience memberships beyond groups, and wraps MessagingService and MemoryStoreService for cross-server traffic. See [Audiences and routing](/concepts/interest-and-routing).

Memberships are cleared automatically when a player leaves.

## SetParty

<Sig side="both">{"SetParty(partyName: string, player: Player, enabled: boolean?): ()"}</Sig>

Adds `player` to a party, or removes them with `enabled = false`.

## SetMatch

<Sig side="both">{"SetMatch(matchName: string, player: Player, enabled: boolean?): ()"}</Sig>

Adds or removes a player from a match.

## SetTeam

<Sig side="both">{"SetTeam(teamName: string, player: Player, enabled: boolean?): ()"}</Sig>

Adds or removes a player from a team. This is Cheeto's own membership; it does not read or change `Player.Team`.

## SetStreamedCell

<Sig side="both">{"SetStreamedCell(cellName: string, player: Player, enabled: boolean?): ()"}</Sig>

Adds or removes a player from a streaming cell, for games that divide the world into regions.

## SetObjectOwner

<Sig side="both">{"SetObjectOwner(object: any, player: Player, enabled: boolean?): ()"}</Sig>

Records `player` as an owner of `object`. An object can have several owners.

## GetInterestPlayers

<Sig side="both">{"GetInterestPlayers(scope: string, key: any): {Player}"}</Sig>

The players in an audience. `scope` is `"Group"`, `"Party"`, `"Match"`, `"Team"`, `"Cell"`, `"Owner"` or `"Zone"`; `key` is the group, party, match, team or cell name, or the object for `"Owner"`. Players who left are excluded.

```lua copy
for _, player in Network.Replication.GetInterestPlayers("Party", partyId) do
    Network.PartyChat.Fire(player, message)
end
```

## Graph

<Sig side="both">{"Graph(): ReplicationGraph"}</Sig>

Creates a routing graph: a private set of observer lists that override the shared memberships for specific keys.

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `graph:Observe(scope, key, player)` | Add an observer for `scope`/`key` |
| `graph:Unobserve(scope, key, player)` | Remove one |
| `graph:Players(scope, key)` | Observers for that key, or the shared membership from `GetInterestPlayers` if the graph has none |
| `graph:Route(scope, key, send)` | Call `send(player)` for each of `Players(scope, key)` |

```lua copy
local spectators = Network.Replication.Graph()
spectators:Observe("Match", matchId, spectator)

spectators:Route("Match", matchId, function(player)
    Network.MatchState.SetPlayer(player, snapshot)
end)
```

## MessagingService

<Sig side="both">{"MessagingService(topic: string, service: MessagingService?): MessagingAdapter"}</Sig>

Wraps `MessagingService` for one topic. Messages are tables `{ Channel, Payload, SchemaVersion, SchemaHash }`, so receivers can reject payloads from servers running a different schema. Use it on the server; the services are not available to clients. Errors when [`EnableReplicationAdapters`](/reference/options/runtime#enablereplicationadapters) is off.

| Method | Publishes to channel |
| --- | --- |
| `Publish(channel, payload)` | `channel` |
| `PublishGroup(groupName, payload)` | `group:<groupName>` |
| `PublishZone(channelName, zoneName, payload)` | `zone:<channelName>:<zoneName>` |
| `PublishMatch(matchServerId, payload)` | `match:<matchServerId>` |
| `Subscribe(handler)` | Calls `handler(message)` for each message |

Payloads are not encoded with the schema; MessagingService's own size limits and serialization rules apply.

## MemoryStore

<Sig side="both">{"MemoryStore(name: string, service: MemoryStoreService?): MemoryStoreAdapter"}</Sig>

Wraps one MemoryStore sorted map. Values are stored as `{ Payload, SchemaVersion, SchemaHash }`.

| Method | Key |
| --- | --- |
| `Set(scope, key, payload, expirationSeconds?)` | `<scope>:<key>`, default expiry 60 s |
| `Get(scope, key)` | `<scope>:<key>` |
| `Remove(scope, key)` | `<scope>:<key>` |
| `SetGroup(groupName, key, payload, expirationSeconds?)` | `group:<groupName>:<key>` |
| `SetZone(channelName, zoneName, key, payload, expirationSeconds?)` | `zone:<channelName>:<zoneName>:<key>` |
| `SetMatch(matchServerId, key, payload, expirationSeconds?)` | `match:<matchServerId>:<key>` |

All methods yield and can error like the underlying service calls. Wrap them in `pcall`.

```

`docs/pages/reference/api/schema.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Schema"
description: "Schema version information and helpers for migrating stored payloads."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Schema

`Network.Schema` describes the compiled schema's version and lets you migrate payloads written by older versions, such as data you saved with an [exported type](/reference/api/exports).

<Callout type="info">
Migrations are applied only when you call [`Migrate`](#migrate). Received network traffic is never migrated: both sides of a live connection run the same schema.
</Callout>

## Version

<Sig side="both">{"Version: number"}</Sig>

This module's [`Version`](/reference/options/versioning#version).

## MinimumVersion

<Sig side="both">{"MinimumVersion: number"}</Sig>

The [`MinimumSchemaVersion`](/reference/options/versioning#minimumschemaversion) it accepts.

## Hash

<Sig side="both">{"Hash: string"}</Sig>

The [schema fingerprint](/reference/options/versioning#the-schema-fingerprint) used in the handshake: 16 hex digits computed from the wire layout.

## Info

<Sig side="both">{"Info(): { Version, MinimumVersion, Hash, Defaults, Renames, Deprecated }"}</Sig>

The version fields plus copies of the registered defaults, renames and deprecations.

## RegisterMigration

<Sig side="both">{"RegisterMigration(fromVersion: number, migrate: (payload) -> payload): ()"}</Sig>

Registers the step that upgrades a payload from `fromVersion` to `fromVersion + 1`.

## SetDefault

<Sig side="both">{"SetDefault(field: string, value: any): ()"}</Sig>

Fills `field` with `value` when a migrated payload lacks it.

## RenameField

<Sig side="both">{"RenameField(from: string, to: string): ()"}</Sig>

Moves `from` to `to` when `to` is not already set.

## DeprecateField

<Sig side="both">{"DeprecateField(field: string): ()"}</Sig>

Removes `field` from migrated payloads.

## Migrate

<Sig side="both">{"Migrate(payload: any, fromVersion: number?): (any, number)"}</Sig>

Applies renames, defaults and deprecations, then every registered migration step from `fromVersion` up to the current version, then the renames, defaults and deprecations again. Returns the new payload and the current version. Missing steps are skipped. Only top-level fields of a table payload are renamed, defaulted or removed.

```lua copy
Network.Schema.RegisterMigration(1, function(save)
    save.Coins = save.Gold
    save.Gold = nil
    return save
end)
Network.Schema.SetDefault("Gems", 0)

local current, version = Network.Schema.Migrate(storedSave, storedSave.Version)
```

```

`docs/pages/reference/api/security.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Security"
description: "Policies, violation reporting, kill switches, abuse scores, and the client shield, client integrity and character integrity controls."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Security

`Network.Security` holds the runtime side of Cheeto's protections. For how the pieces fit together, start at the [Security model](/security/overview).

## Summary

| Member | Side | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`OnViolation`](#onviolation) | Both | Subscribe to every drop and security report |
| [`RegisterPolicy`](#registerpolicy) | Both | Define or replace a named policy |
| [`RegisterPolicyGroup`](#registerpolicygroup) | Both | Name a list of policies |
| [`CheckIdempotency`](#checkidempotency) | Both | One-time key check for your own code |
| [`SetRateLimit`](#setratelimit) | Both | Change an endpoint's rate limit while the game runs |
| [`SetZone`](#setzone), [`GetZone`](#getzone) | Server | The zone [`RequireZone`](/reference/fields#requirezone) checks |
| [`RegisterKnownId`](#registerknownid), [`ForgetKnownId`](#forgetknownid) | Server | Ids [`RequireServerKnownId`](/reference/fields#requireserverknownid) accepts |
| [`SetInventoryResolver`](#setinventoryresolver) | Server | The check behind [`RequireInventoryOwnership`](/reference/fields#requireinventoryownership) |
| [`Kill`](#kill), [`Unkill`](#unkill) | Both | Disable an endpoint live |
| [`KillPolicyGroup`](#killpolicygroup), [`UnkillPolicyGroup`](#unkillpolicygroup) | Both | Disable every endpoint in a policy group |
| [`AbuseScores`](#abusescores) | Both | Violation counts per sender |
| [`ReportClientShield`](#reportclientshield) | Both | Record a detection against a player |
| [`ClientShield`](#clientshield) | Both | Recent shield reports |
| [`StartClientShield`](#startclientshield) | Client | Start the shield probes manually |
| [`ClientIntegrity`](#clientintegrity) | Both | Integrity challenge state |
| [`ChallengeIntegrity`](#challengeintegrity) | Server | Send a challenge now |
| [`GrantIntegrityGrace`](#grantintegritygrace) | Server | Pause challenges for a player |
| [`OnIntegritySample`](#onintegritysample) | Client | Add a check to every receipt |
| [`CharacterIntegrity`](#characterintegrity) | Server | Movement scoring state |
| [`ObserveCharacter`](#observecharacter) | Server | Add your own movement evidence |
| [`GrantMovementGrace`](#grantmovementgrace) | Server | Pause movement scoring for a player |
| [`ReconcileCharacter`](#reconcilecharacter) | Server | Accept the current position as safe |
| [`TeleportCharacter`](#teleportcharacter) | Server | Move a character without tripping checks |
| [`EvaluateMovement`](#evaluatemovement) | Both | The pure movement classifier |

## OnViolation

<Sig side="both">{"OnViolation(callback: (report: ViolationReport) -> ()): () -> ()"}</Sig>

Calls `callback` for every dropped packet or event and every shield, integrity and movement report, with a [`ViolationReport`](/reference/violation-report). Returns a function that unsubscribes. Equivalent to `Use("Violation", callback)`, so it only fires while [`EnableMiddleware`](/reference/options/runtime#enablemiddleware) is on.

```lua copy
Network.Security.OnViolation(function(report)
    if report.Reason ~= "RateLimit" then
        warn("[net]", report.Reason, report.Player, report.Event, report.Action)
    end
end)
```

## RegisterPolicy

<Sig side="both">{"RegisterPolicy(name: string, rule: (context: PolicyContext) -> (boolean, string?)): ()"}</Sig>

Defines the [policy](/security/policies) that endpoints name in their `Policy` field, replacing any previous rule with that name. Passing `nil` removes it, after which its endpoints drop everything again.

The rule runs **before the payload is decoded**, so it cannot see the data. It receives:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Source` | `Player` or `"Server"` | The sender |
| `Name` | string | Endpoint name |
| `Channel` | string | `"Reliable"` or `"Unreliable"` |
| `Policy` | string | This policy's name |
| `PolicyGroup` | string? | The endpoint's policy group |
| `Constraints` | table | The endpoint's [constraint fields](/reference/fields#constraints) |
| `UserId` | number? | The sender's `UserId` |
| `Size` | number | Size of the received packet |

Return `true` to allow. Return `false`, or `false` and a reason string, to drop; the reason becomes the drop reason reported to `OnViolation` (default `PolicyRejected`). A rule that errors denies.

```lua copy
Network.Security.RegisterPolicy("admin", function(context)
    local level = context.Source:GetAttribute("AdminLevel")
    if typeof(level) ~= "number" or level < 100 then
        return false, "not-admin"
    end
    return true
end)
```

<Callout type="error">
There are no built-in policies: a name that is not registered denies every packet and warns once. [`--doctor`](/reference/cli#--doctor) lists every name your schema uses.
</Callout>

## RegisterPolicyGroup

<Sig side="both">{"RegisterPolicyGroup(name: string, policies: {string}): ()"}</Sig>

Defines a policy group: an endpoint with `PolicyGroup: "name"` must also pass every policy in `policies`. The list is copied, so changing your table afterwards has no effect. A policy named in the group that is not registered denies.

```lua copy
Network.Security.RegisterPolicyGroup("economy", { "not-trading-locked", "profile-loaded" })
```

## CheckIdempotency

<Sig side="both">{"CheckIdempotency(source: any, key: string, ttlSeconds: number?): boolean"}</Sig>

Returns `true` the first time a `key` is seen for `source` within `ttlSeconds` (default 120), and `false` for repeats. The runtime uses this for [`Idempotency`](/reference/fields#idempotency); you can call it from your own handlers with keys you choose, such as a purchase receipt id.

```lua copy
Network.Purchase.On(function(player, receiptId)
    if not Network.Security.CheckIdempotency(player, receiptId, 600) then
        return
    end
    Economy.Grant(player, receiptId)
end)
```

## SetRateLimit

<Sig side="both">{"SetRateLimit(key: string, rate: number?, burst: number?): ()"}</Sig>

Overrides the rate limit for `key`: an endpoint name, or `"Reliable"` / `"Unreliable"` for the per-remote limit. `rate` is packets per second per sender and `burst` how many may arrive at once (default `rate`). Pass `nil` as `rate` to go back to the compiled value. Takes effect on the next packet; token buckets already filled keep their tokens.

```lua copy
-- Tighten a chat endpoint during a spam wave, then restore it.
Network.Security.SetRateLimit("SendChat", 1, 3)
task.delay(300, function()
    Network.Security.SetRateLimit("SendChat", nil)
end)
```

## SetZone

<Sig side="server">{"SetZone(player: Player, zone: string?): ()"}</Sig>

Records which zone `player` is in, or clears it with `nil`. Endpoints with [`RequireZone`](/reference/fields#requirezone) drop packets from players who are not in the named zone. Call it from whatever decides zones in your game: region checks, teleports or round state.

```lua copy
Network.Security.SetZone(player, "Arena")
```

## GetZone

<Sig side="server">{"GetZone(player: Player): string?"}</Sig>

Returns the zone set with [`SetZone`](#setzone), or `nil`.

## RegisterKnownId

<Sig side="server">{"RegisterKnownId(id: number | string, player: Player?): ()"}</Sig>

Marks `id` as issued by the server. Endpoints with [`RequireServerKnownId`](/reference/fields#requireserverknownid) accept a packet only if the first number or string in its payload is a registered id. With `player`, only that player may use it; without, anyone may.

```lua copy
local offerId = HttpService:GenerateGUID(false)
Network.Security.RegisterKnownId(offerId, player)
Network.ShowOffer.Fire(player, offerId)
```

## ForgetKnownId

<Sig side="server">{"ForgetKnownId(id: number | string): ()"}</Sig>

Removes an id registered with [`RegisterKnownId`](#registerknownid). Call it when the offer, trade or session the id stood for ends.

## SetInventoryResolver

<Sig side="server">{"SetInventoryResolver(resolver: ((player: Player, payload: { n: number, [number]: any }) -> boolean)?): ()"}</Sig>

Sets the function that decides [`RequireInventoryOwnership`](/reference/fields#requireinventoryownership). It receives the sender and the decoded arguments (packed, with `n`) and returns `true` when the player owns what the payload names. Until one is set, those endpoints drop every packet and warn once. A resolver that errors counts as a rejection.

```lua copy
Network.Security.SetInventoryResolver(function(player, payload)
    return Inventory.Has(player, payload[1])
end)
```

## Kill

<Sig side="both">{"Kill(endpointName: string, reason: string?): ()"}</Sig>

Disables an endpoint on this module. Sends on it and events received on it are dropped with `KillSwitch`. Use it to switch off an endpoint that is being abused without shutting the server down. Client `Invoke` calls are not blocked on the client; kill the function on the server.

```lua copy
Network.Security.Kill("TradeRequest", "exploit under investigation")
```

## Unkill

<Sig side="both">{"Unkill(endpointName: string): ()"}</Sig>

Re-enables an endpoint.

## KillPolicyGroup

<Sig side="both">{"KillPolicyGroup(groupName: string, reason: string?): ()"}</Sig>

Drops every received event on endpoints whose `PolicyGroup` is `groupName`, with `KillSwitch`.

## UnkillPolicyGroup

<Sig side="both">{"UnkillPolicyGroup(groupName: string): ()"}</Sig>

Re-enables a policy group.

## AbuseScores

<Sig side="both">{"AbuseScores(source: any?): {[string]: number}"}</Sig>

Every drop and report adds to a per-sender counter, keyed by endpoint name (or channel, for packet-level drops) and by shield reason. With a player, returns that player's counters; without, returns a table of every sender's counters keyed by `tostring(sender)`. Counters are cleared when the player leaves.

```lua copy
local scores = Network.Security.AbuseScores(player)
print(scores.DealDamage, scores.Honeypot)
```

## ReportClientShield

<Sig side="both">{"ReportClientShield(source: Player, reason: string, detail: string?, score: number?, immediateKick: boolean?): number"}</Sig>

Records a detection against a player through the same path the [client shield](/security/client-shield) uses: adds `score` (default 1) to the player's count for `reason`, reports it to `OnViolation`, and kicks when [`ClientShieldKick`](/reference/options/client-shield#clientshieldkick) is on and the report is immediate, strict mode is on, or the threshold is reached. Returns the player's score for that reason. Use it to route your own server-side detections into one pipeline.

## ClientShield

<Sig side="both">{"ClientShield(): ClientShieldSnapshot"}</Sig>

Returns `{ Reports, Enabled, Strict, Kick, ScoreThreshold }`. `Reports` holds the most recent 256 recorded reports, each `{ Source, UserId, Reason, Detail, Score, Weight, Action, Time }`.

## StartClientShield

<Sig side="client">{"StartClientShield(): ()"}</Sig>

Starts the shield's probe loop. The client module calls this when it loads, so you only need it if you enabled [`EnableClientShield`](/reference/options/client-shield#enableclientshield) at runtime. Does nothing when the shield is disabled or already running.

## ClientIntegrity

<Sig side="both">{"ClientIntegrity(player: Player?): ClientIntegritySnapshot"}</Sig>

With a player (server), returns that player's challenge state:

`{ UserId, Score, PendingChallenge, PendingDeadline, NextChallengeAt, GraceUntil, LastReceiptAt, LastCompletion, LastSweep, ChallengesIssued, ValidReceipts, ConsecutiveFailures, ConsecutiveMisses, LastReason, LastAction }`

Without a player, returns `{ Enabled, Peers, Evidence, Local }`, where `Local` describes this machine's own responder (useful on the client).

## ChallengeIntegrity

<Sig side="server">{"ChallengeIntegrity(player: Player): number?"}</Sig>

Sends a [client integrity](/security/client-integrity) challenge to `player` immediately, replacing any pending one, and returns its id. Returns `nil` when integrity is disabled, the player has left, or the player is in a grace period.

## GrantIntegrityGrace

<Sig side="server">{"GrantIntegrityGrace(player: Player, seconds: number?, reason: string?): ()"}</Sig>

Stops challenging `player` for `seconds` (default [`ClientIntegrityJoinGraceSeconds`](/reference/options/client-integrity#clientintegrityjoingraceseconds)) and discards any pending challenge. Use it around long loads, such as teleports within the place or large map streaming.

```lua copy
Network.Security.GrantIntegrityGrace(player, 15, "loading-dungeon")
```

## OnIntegritySample

<Sig side="client">{"OnIntegritySample(sampler: (context) -> (boolean | { Healthy: boolean } | nil)): () -> ()"}</Sig>

Adds a check that runs for every integrity challenge. The context is `{ ChallengeId, Nonce, Completion, Sweep, WireFormat, SchemaVersion, ReceivedAt }`. The receipt reports unhealthy if any sampler errors, returns `false`, or returns a table whose `Healthy` is not `true`. `nil` and `true` count as healthy. Returns a function that removes the sampler.

```lua copy
local remove = Network.Security.OnIntegritySample(function()
    return Controllers.Combat:IsBound()
end)
```

## CharacterIntegrity

<Sig side="server">{"CharacterIntegrity(player: Player?): CharacterIntegritySnapshot"}</Sig>

With a player, returns `{ UserId, Score, ConsecutiveBreaches, GraceUntil, LastSampleAt, LastReason, LastAction, Reasons, History }`. Without, returns `{ Enabled, Mode, Kick, Players, Evidence }`. `Reasons` maps each reason to its current decaying score; `History` holds the player's recent evidence entries.

## ObserveCharacter

<Sig side="server">{"ObserveCharacter(player: Player, reason: string, weight: number?, detail: string?): (number, string)"}</Sig>

Adds your own evidence to a player's movement score, for detections the built-in sampler does not make, and applies the configured [mode](/reference/options/character-integrity#characterintegritymode). Returns the new score and the action taken: `"observe"`, `"report"`, `"correct"` or `"kick"`.

## GrantMovementGrace

<Sig side="server">{"GrantMovementGrace(player: Player, seconds: number?, reason: string?): ()"}</Sig>

Stops scoring `player`'s movement for `seconds` (default [`CharacterIntegrityTeleportGraceSeconds`](/reference/options/character-integrity#characterintegrityteleportgraceseconds)) and resets the breach count. Call it before any intended fast movement: launch pads, dashes, vehicles, cutscenes, knockback.

## ReconcileCharacter

<Sig side="server">{"ReconcileCharacter(player: Player, resetScore: boolean?): boolean"}</Sig>

Accepts the character's current position as the new safe position, for after you moved it yourself. With `resetScore`, also clears the score. Returns `false` if the player has no character with a `HumanoidRootPart` and `Humanoid`.

## TeleportCharacter

<Sig side="server">{"TeleportCharacter(player: Player, target: CFrame, graceSeconds: number?): boolean"}</Sig>

Grants movement grace, moves the character with `PivotTo`, zeroes its velocity, and reconciles. Use it for every server-initiated teleport. Returns `false` if the target is not a CFrame or there is no character.

```lua copy
Network.Security.TeleportCharacter(player, spawn.CFrame + Vector3.yAxis * 3)
```

## EvaluateMovement

<Sig side="both">{"EvaluateMovement(sample: MovementSample): MovementEvaluation"}</Sig>

The classifier the character sampler uses, exposed so you can test limits deterministically. It reads the current [character integrity options](/reference/options/character-integrity).

Input: `{ DeltaTime, HorizontalDistance, VerticalDistance, WalkSpeed?, HorizontalVelocity?, VerticalVelocity?, Ping?, Seated?, PathBlocked? }`

Output: `{ Suspicious, Resync, Reasons, Weight, AllowedHorizontal, AllowedVertical }`, where `Reasons` can contain `HorizontalDisplacement`, `VerticalDisplacement`, `WalkSpeedMutation`, `CollidableTraversal` or `NonFiniteMovement`, and `Weight` is 0 to 16.

```lua copy
local result = Network.Security.EvaluateMovement({
    DeltaTime = 0.25,
    HorizontalDistance = 40,
    VerticalDistance = 0,
    WalkSpeed = 16,
})
print(result.Suspicious, table.concat(result.Reasons, ","))
```

`docs/pages/reference/api/state.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "State"
description: "Tombstones, patch helpers, a simple interpolator and local dirty-tracking channels."
---

import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# State

`Network.State` has helpers for working with replicated state. Schema-declared [channels](/reference/api/channel) are separate; these helpers work on plain tables.

## Tombstone

<Sig side="both">{"Tombstone: userdata"}</Sig>

A marker meaning "remove this field". Use it in a channel [`Patch`](/reference/api/channel#patch) to clear an optional field, because a `nil` value in a Luau table is indistinguishable from a missing key.

```lua copy
Network.PlayerState.Patch(player, { Equipped = Network.State.Tombstone })
```

## MakePatch

<Sig side="both">{"MakePatch(previous: any, next: any): Patch"}</Sig>

Computes the difference between two tables. Nested tables produce nested patches; changed values become `{ op = "set", value = v }`; removed keys become `{ op = "delete" }`. If either argument is not a table, returns `{ op = "replace", value = next }`.

## ApplyPatch

<Sig side="both">{"ApplyPatch(base: any, patch: Patch): any"}</Sig>

Applies a patch from `MakePatch` and returns a new table. `base` is not modified.

```lua copy
local patch = Network.State.MakePatch(oldState, newState)
local rebuilt = Network.State.ApplyPatch(oldState, patch)
```

These patches are ordinary tables, not Cheeto's channel wire format. Send one through an event with an `unknown` field if you need to.

## Interpolator

<Sig side="both">{"Interpolator(initial: any): Interpolator"}</Sig>

A minimal smoother. `SetTarget(value)` sets a new target; `Step(deltaTime, speed?)` moves toward it (default speed 12 per second) and returns the current value. `Vector3` values are lerped; any other value snaps to the target.

```lua copy
local smoothing = Network.State.Interpolator(Vector3.zero)

Network.BossPosition.On(function(position)
    smoothing:SetTarget(position)
end)

RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function(deltaTime)
    boss:PivotTo(CFrame.new(smoothing:Step(deltaTime)))
end)
```

## DefineChannel

<Sig side="both">{"DefineChannel(name: string, options: table?): LocalChannel"}</Sig>

Creates a local key-value store that tracks which keys changed. It does not send anything by itself. Errors when [`EnableStateChannels`](/reference/options/runtime#enablestatechannels) is off.

| Method | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `channel:Set(key, value)` | Stores the value and marks the key dirty if it changed |
| `channel:Get(key)` | Reads a value |
| `channel:Flush()` | Returns the dirty keys and the version, and clears the dirty set |

## Channels

<Sig side="both">{"Channels: {[string]: LocalChannel}"}</Sig>

Every channel created with `DefineChannel`, by name.

```

`docs/pages/reference/api/transport.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Transport"
description: "Queue accounting, flush decisions, network stats, coalescing and the drop reason list."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Sig } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Transport

`Network.Transport` exposes the per-peer state the runtime uses to decide when to flush and what to shed. Most games only read [`Errors`](#errors) and [`Snapshot`](#snapshot). The recording functions are what the generated code calls itself; call them only if you build your own scheduling on top.

A **peer** is a `Player` on the server, or the server on the client (pass `nil` or `"Server"`).

## Errors

<Sig side="both">{"Errors: {[string]: string}"}</Sig>

A frozen table of every built-in [drop reason](/reference/drop-reasons), each key mapping to itself. Use it instead of string literals:

```lua copy
Network.Security.OnViolation(function(report)
    if report.Reason == Network.Transport.Errors.Honeypot then
        Moderation.Flag(report.Player)
    end
end)
```

## Snapshot

<Sig side="both">{"Snapshot(peer: any?): TransportState | {[string]: TransportState}"}</Sig>

A copy of one peer's transport state, or of every peer's keyed by `tostring(peer)`:

`{ QueuedBytes, QueuedEvents, SentBytes, SentPackets, DroppedLowPriority, LastFlush, LastQueueTime, Rtt, Jitter, ClockSkew, PacketLoss, Priority }`

`Priority` has `{ Bytes, Events }` for each of `Critical`, `Gameplay`, `Cosmetic` and `Background`, counted since the peer was first seen.

## UpdateNetworkStats

<Sig side="both">{"UpdateNetworkStats(peer: any, rtt: number?, jitter: number?, clockSkew: number?, packetLoss: number?): ()"}</Sig>

Stores network measurements for a peer. The runtime does not measure these itself. They only affect flushing: while `rtt > 0.25` or `jitter > 0.1`, the peer's burst budget ([`MaxBurstBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxburstbytes)) is reduced by a quarter. `nil` arguments leave the stored value unchanged.

```lua copy
Network.Transport.UpdateNetworkStats(player, player:GetNetworkPing() * 2)
```

## ShouldFlush

<Sig side="both">{"ShouldFlush(peer: any, channel: string, size: number, priority: string?): boolean"}</Sig>

The runtime's flush decision for a peer with `size` bytes queued. `true` when `priority` is `Critical`, when `size` reaches the burst budget, when the peer's tracked queue is at least half of [`MaxQueuedBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxqueuedbytes), or when at least 1/60 s has passed since the peer's last flush. `false` when `size` is 0.

## RecordQueuedEvent

<Sig side="both">{"RecordQueuedEvent(peer: any, channel: string, size: number, priority: string?): boolean"}</Sig>

Adds `size` bytes to the peer's tracked queue. Returns `false`, and drops with `Backpressure`, when the queue is over `MaxQueuedBytes`, shedding is on, and `priority` is `Cosmetic` or `Background`.

## RecordFlush

<Sig side="both">{"RecordFlush(peer: any, channel: string, size: number): ()"}</Sig>

Subtracts a sent packet from the peer's tracked queue and updates its sent counters. Emits the `transport.flush` [telemetry](/reference/api/hooks#telemetry) event.

## Coalesce

<Sig side="both">{"Coalesce(peer: any, key: string, priority: string, payload: any): ()"}</Sig>

Stores `payload` under `key` in the peer's coalesce bucket, replacing any earlier one, for your own last-value-wins bookkeeping. It does not send anything. For events whose sends should coalesce on the wire, use [`CoalesceKey`](/reference/fields#coalescekey) or `ReliabilityMode: Latest`.

## FlushCoalesced

<Sig side="both">{"FlushCoalesced(peer: any): {[string]: { Priority: string, Payload: any, Time: number }}"}</Sig>

Returns and empties the peer's coalesce bucket: the latest payload stored under each key.

<Callout type="info">
Coalescing records the latest value per key; it does not stop earlier sends. Use it to build your own latest-value-wins replication by reading `FlushCoalesced` on your own schedule and sending only what it returns.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/cli.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Command line"
description: "Every flag of the cheeto compiler, what it checks, and what it prints."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Sig } from '../../components/Reference'

# Command line

```sh
cheeto <schema> [flags]
```

`<schema>` is the path to a schema file. The extension can be left out: `cheeto network` finds `network`, `network.cheeto` or `network.txt`, in that order. Output paths inside the schema are relative to the schema file.

Flags can go in any order. Only one **mode** runs per invocation; if you pass several, the first in the [summary](#summary) order wins. `--ci` runs a fixed set of modes together.

## Summary

| Flag | Kind | Writes files | Fails the process when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *(none)* | Mode: compile | Yes | The schema is invalid |
| [`--doctor`](#--doctor) | Mode | No | Never (reports only) |
| [`--strict`](#--strict) | Mode | No | Any production check fails |
| [`--benchmark`](#--benchmark) | Mode | No | A size, generation time or measured cost exceeds its threshold, or an endpoint delivers nothing |
| [`--load-sim`](#--load-sim) | Mode | No | Never |
| [`--capture-replay`](#--capture-replay) | Mode | No | Never |
| [`--golden-snapshots`](#--golden-snapshots) | Mode | No | Never |
| [`--compatibility`](#--compatibility) | Mode | No | Never |
| [`--schema-docs`](#--schema-docs) | Mode | No | Never |
| [`--write-lock`](#--write-lock) | Mode | `cheeto.lock` | The schema is invalid |
| [`--check-lock`](#--check-lock) | Mode | No | `cheeto.lock` is missing or differs |
| [`--hardening-checklist`](#--hardening-checklist) | Mode | No | Any release check fails |
| [`--ci`](#--ci) | Mode | No | Any included mode fails |
| [`-w`, `--watch`](#--watch) | Mode | Yes | |
| [`-y`, `--yes`](#--yes) | Modifier | | |
| [`-q`, `--quiet`](#--quiet) | Modifier | | |
| [`-c`, `--compact`](#--compact) | Modifier | | |
| [`-h`, `--help`](#--help) | Info | | |
| [`-v`, `--version`](#--version) | Info | | |

Every mode parses the schema first, so a syntax error fails all of them.

## Compiling

<Sig side="cli">{"cheeto network.cheeto"}</Sig>

Writes the client and server modules, plus the types module, TypeScript definitions and shared runtime when those options are set. Prompts before creating a missing output directory unless `--yes` is given. If the schema sets [`StrictProduction`](/reference/options/security#strictproduction), the `--strict` checks run first.

## `--doctor`

<Sig side="cli">{"cheeto network --doctor"}</Sig>

Checks the schema for risky settings without writing anything, and prints each finding as a warning with its file, line and column. It always exits successfully. It reports:

- reliable packet cap above 1 MiB;
- rate limiting off outside the `Development` profile;
- missing `ClientOutput` or `ServerOutput`;
- client-origin events and functions with none of `Auth`, `Policy` or `PolicyGroup`.

It then lists every policy, policy group and auth rule name the schema uses, so you can check each one is registered: an unregistered name drops every packet on its endpoints.

```
- Policy names to register with Security.RegisterPolicy: shop, trade
- Auth names to register with UseAuth: AlivePlayer
```

## `--strict`

<Sig side="cli">{"cheeto network --strict"}</Sig>

Runs the doctor checks as errors, plus these, and exits with an error if any fail:

- `SecurityProfile` is `Production` or `Competitive`;
- reliable and unreliable size caps are set and above 0;
- `RateLimitPerSecond` is set and above 0;
- `InvokeTimeoutSeconds` is set and above 0;
- `SyncValidation` and `WriteValidations` are off;
- output paths are relative and contain no `..`.

`SyncValidation` is only on by default in the `Development` profile, so a `Production` or `Competitive` schema passes that check without writing it.

## `--hardening-checklist`

<Sig side="cli">{"cheeto network --hardening-checklist"}</Sig>

The release gate: everything `--strict` checks, plus `RequirePolicies = true`, and `NoRawCaptureInProduction` not set to `false`. Exits with an error if any fail.

## `--benchmark`

<Sig side="cli">{"cheeto network --benchmark"}</Sig>

Generates the modules and measures them:

1. **Size and generation time** of the server, client and types modules.
2. **Every endpoint, for real.** Both modules are loaded in Lune against stub remotes. Each event, function and channel sends 256 generated sample payloads (200 for functions); the bytes that reach the remote are counted, and encoding (the sends plus the replication step) and decoding (the receiver's full pipeline, through to the listener) are timed.

```
endpoint             direction         bytes/msg  encode µs  decode µs
DealDamage           client → server   6          3.1        4.2
Inventory            server → client   84         9.8        12.6
...
average over 76 endpoints: bytes/msg=17.4 encode=8.19 µs decode=11.1 µs (0 skipped)
```

The harness removes the schema's access rules, because it measures serialization and the receive pipeline rather than your policies. An endpoint whose payload type has no generated sample (such as `DateTime`) is listed as skipped.

It fails when the server module exceeds 220 KB plus 8 KB per endpoint, the client module 220 KB plus 6 KB per endpoint, the types module 250 KB, generation takes over 2 seconds, the average encode or decode cost exceeds 250 µs, or any endpoint delivers nothing. The drop reasons are printed for an endpoint that delivers nothing, which usually means its payload does not round-trip.

## `--load-sim`

<Sig side="cli">{"cheeto network --load-sim"}</Sig>

Runs the same measurement as `--benchmark`, then scales the average message to 10, 50, 100 and 200 clients sending and receiving 10, 30 and 60 messages per second each. The CSV gives bandwidth in KB/s, CPU milliseconds per second, and the share of one core. It is a projection from measured costs, so it is as accurate as the assumption that your traffic looks like the schema's average endpoint.

## `--capture-replay`

<Sig side="cli">{"cheeto network --capture-replay"}</Sig>

Prints the schema's event, function and channel counts and the capture and replay APIs the generated modules expose. It does not run a capture.

## `--golden-snapshots`

<Sig side="cli">{"cheeto network --golden-snapshots"}</Sig>

Prints the schema version, the [schema fingerprint](/reference/options/versioning#the-schema-fingerprint), the generated module sizes, and the sorted names of every event, function and channel. Commit the output and diff it in review to notice surface changes.

## `--compatibility`

<Sig side="cli">{"cheeto network --compatibility"}</Sig>

Prints a table of which peers the handshake accepts: a peer below `MinimumSchemaVersion`, a peer with a different fingerprint, and a matching peer.

## `--schema-docs`

<Sig side="cli">{"cheeto network --schema-docs"}</Sig>

Prints a Markdown summary: schema version, capture redactions, and the names of every event, function and channel.

## `--write-lock`

<Sig side="cli">{"cheeto network --write-lock"}</Sig>

Writes [`cheeto.lock`](/reference/lockfile) next to the schema, keeping the ids already recorded and marking removed endpoints as retired. Run it deliberately when you mean to change the wire layout, and commit the result.

## `--check-lock`

<Sig side="cli">{"cheeto network --check-lock"}</Sig>

Regenerates the lockfile in memory and fails if `cheeto.lock` is missing or differs, printing the lines the schema now produces. Use it in CI so a wire change cannot land without an updated lockfile.

## `--ci`

<Sig side="cli">{"cheeto network --ci --yes"}</Sig>

Runs `--doctor`, `--benchmark`, `--load-sim`, `--capture-replay`, `--golden-snapshots`, `--compatibility`, `--schema-docs` and `--check-lock` in sequence, stopping at the first failure. It does not include `--strict` or `--hardening-checklist`; run those as separate steps.

## `--watch`

<Sig side="cli">{"cheeto network --watch"}</Sig>

Compiles, then recompiles whenever the schema or any file it imports (directly or indirectly) changes. Runs quietly and answers prompts with yes.

## `--yes`

Answers every prompt with yes, for scripts and CI. Currently the only prompt is creating a missing output directory.

## `--quiet`

Silences normal output. Errors still print.

## `--compact`

Prints a short one-line form of each error first, followed by the full message.

## `--help`

Prints usage and every flag.

## `--version`

Prints the compiler version and exits.

```

`docs/pages/reference/declarations/channel.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "channel"
description: "Server-owned replicated state with snapshots, delta patches and scoped audiences."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# channel

A `channel` is a piece of state the server owns and replicates to clients. Instead of firing an event for every change, the server sets or patches the value and the runtime sends only what changed, on a schedule. Clients read the latest value at any time and can subscribe to changes.

```cheeto copy
channel PlayerState {
    Scope: Player,
    TickRate: 20,
    Delta: true,
    Data: struct {
        Health: u8,
        Stamina: u8,
        Equipped: string(0..32)?
    }
}
```

## Fields

`Data` is required. Everything else is optional.

| Field | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`Data`](/reference/fields#data) | required | The state's type. Use a `struct` to get delta patches |
| [`Scope`](/reference/fields#scope) | `Player` | What the shorthand `Set` and `Patch` target |
| [`Type`](/reference/fields#type) | `Reliable` | `Unreliable` sends each flush as its own unreliable call |
| [`TickRate`](/reference/fields#tickrate) | every flush | Maximum automatic flushes per second |
| [`Delta`](/reference/fields#delta) | `true` for structs | Send changed fields only |
| [`KeyframeRate`](/reference/fields#keyframerate) | none | Force a full snapshot this often |
| [`Interest`](/reference/fields#interest), [`InterestRadius`](/reference/fields#interestradius) | `None`, `0` | Zone or distance targeting |
| [`Priority`](/reference/fields#priority) | `Gameplay` | Shedding under backpressure |
| [`MaxPacketBytes`](/reference/fields#maxpacketbytes), [`MaxQueuedEvents`](/reference/fields#maxqueuedevents) | | Limits on the receiving client |
| [`WireId`](/reference/fields#wireid), [`ReservedId`](/reference/fields#reservedid), [`DeprecatedId`](/reference/fields#deprecatedid) | | Lockfile identity |

<Callout type="warning">
Channels are received by clients, so do not set `Auth`, `Policy` or rate-limit fields on them unless you also register those rules on the client. See the [receive-side note](/reference/fields).
</Callout>

## Generated API

| Server module | Client module |
| --- | --- |
| `Set`, `SetPlayer`, `SetAll`, `SetList`, `SetGroup`, `SetZone`, `SetDistance` | `On(listener)` |
| `Patch`, `PatchPlayer`, `PatchAll`, `PatchList`, `PatchGroup`, `PatchZone`, `PatchDistance` | `Get()` |
| `Flush`, `FlushPlayer`, `FlushAll`, `FlushList`, `FlushGroup`, `FlushZone`, `FlushDistance` | `Version()` |
| `SetInterestZone`, `SetInterestPosition`, `Get`, `Clear` | |

See [Channel endpoint](/reference/api/channel) for signatures.

```lua filename="Server.server.luau" copy
Network.PlayerState.Set(player, { Health = 100, Stamina = 100 })

-- Later: only Health goes over the wire
Network.PlayerState.Patch(player, { Health = 72 })
```

```lua filename="Client.client.luau" copy
Network.PlayerState.On(function(state, version, patch)
    HealthBar.Set(state.Health)
end)

local current = Network.PlayerState.Get()
```

## How updates are sent

- `Set` stores a full value and marks the player for a full snapshot.
- `Patch` merges fields into the stored value and marks only those fields dirty.
- Once per replication step, and no more often than [`TickRate`](/reference/fields#tickrate) allows, the server sends each player either a full snapshot (after `Set`, or on a keyframe) or a delta of the dirty fields.
- `Flush*` sends immediately instead of waiting for the tick.

To clear an optional field in a patch, set it to [`State.Tombstone`](/reference/api/state#tombstone); a `nil` in a Luau table cannot be distinguished from a missing key.

```lua copy
Network.PlayerState.Patch(player, { Equipped = Network.State.Tombstone })
```

```

`docs/pages/reference/declarations/enum.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "enum"
description: "Unit enums for a fixed set of names, and tagged enums for variants that carry data."
---

# enum

Cheeto has two kinds of enum.

## Unit enums

A unit enum is one of a fixed set of names. It is sent as a one-byte index, not as a string, and received as the string. Sending a string that is not one of the names raises `Unexpected enum` on the sender.

```cheeto copy
enum CharacterStatus = { Idling, Walking, Running, Jumping, Falling }
```

```lua copy
Network.StatusChanged.FireAll("Running")
```

## Tagged enums

A tagged enum is one of several variants, each carrying its own struct. The string after `=` names the field that holds the variant's tag.

```cheeto copy
enum MouseEvent = "Type" {
    Move {
        Delta: vector,
        Position: vector
    },
    Drag {
        Delta: vector,
        Position: vector
    },
    Click {
        Button: enum { Left, Right, Middle },
        Position: vector
    }
}
```

The Luau type is a union keyed on the tag:

```lua copy
type MouseEvent =
    | { Type: "Move", Delta: vector, Position: vector }
    | { Type: "Drag", Delta: vector, Position: vector }
    | { Type: "Click", Button: "Left" | "Right" | "Middle", Position: vector }
```

Cheeto has no general union type. A tagged enum is how to send "one of several shapes":

```cheeto copy
enum Value = "Kind" {
    Number { Value: f64 },
    Text { Value: string }
}
```

A variant tag cannot also be used as a field name inside that variant.

## Generics

Tagged enums accept type parameters:

```cheeto copy
enum Result<T> = "Status" {
    Ok { Value: T },
    Err { Message: string(0..128) }
}

enum PurchaseResult = Result<u32>
```

```

`docs/pages/reference/declarations/event.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "event"
description: "One-way messages between the server and clients, reliable or unreliable."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# event

An `event` is a one-way message. It replaces a `RemoteEvent` or `UnreliableRemoteEvent`: one side fires, the other listens. Every event shares the module's two remotes, so declaring more events does not create more instances.

```cheeto copy
event DealDamage {
    From: Client,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Policy: "damage",
    CooldownSeconds: 0.25,
    Data: struct {
        Target: Instance(Player),
        Damage: u16(0..500)
    }
}
```

## Fields

`From`, `Type` and `Call` are required. Everything else is optional.

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`From`](/reference/fields#from) | `Server` or `Client`: who sends |
| [`Type`](/reference/fields#type) | `Reliable` or `Unreliable` |
| [`Call`](/reference/fields#call) | `SingleSync`, `SingleAsync`, `ManySync`, `ManyAsync` or `Polling` |
| [`Data`](/reference/fields#data) | Payload type or type pack; omit for no data |
| [`Poll`](/reference/fields#poll), [`Predict`](/reference/fields#predict) | Delivery switches |
| [`Auth`](/reference/fields#auth), [`Policy`](/reference/fields#policy), [`PolicyGroup`](/reference/fields#policygroup), [`Honeypot`](/reference/fields#honeypot) | Access control, checked by the receiver |
| [`CooldownSeconds`](/reference/fields#cooldownseconds), [`RateLimitPerSecond`](/reference/fields#ratelimitpersecond), [`RateLimitBurst`](/reference/fields#ratelimitburst), [`MaxPacketBytes`](/reference/fields#maxpacketbytes), [`MaxQueuedEvents`](/reference/fields#maxqueuedevents) | Limits |
| [`Idempotency`](/reference/fields#idempotency) | Duplicate rejection for predicted sends |
| [`Risk`](/reference/fields#risk), [`MaxDistance`](/reference/fields#maxdistance), `Require*` | Constraints passed to your rules |
| [`Priority`](/reference/fields#priority), [`CoalesceKey`](/reference/fields#coalescekey), [`ReliabilityMode`](/reference/fields#reliabilitymode) | Scheduling |
| [`WireId`](/reference/fields#wireid), [`ReservedId`](/reference/fields#reservedid), [`DeprecatedId`](/reference/fields#deprecatedid) | Lockfile identity |

## Generated API

The sending side gets fire methods and the receiving side gets a listener. See [Event endpoint](/reference/api/event) for signatures.

| `From` | Server module | Client module |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Server` | `Fire`, `FireAll`, `FireList`, `FireExcept`, `FireGroup` | `On` (or `Iter` when polling) |
| `Client` | `On` (or `Iter` when polling) | `Fire`, `Predict` |

```lua filename="Server.server.luau" copy
local Network = require(ReplicatedStorage.Network.Server)

Network.DealDamage.On(function(player, hit)
    Combat.Apply(player, hit.Target, hit.Damage)
end)
```

```lua filename="Client.client.luau" copy
local Network = require(ReplicatedStorage.Network.Client)

Network.DealDamage.Fire({ Target = target, Damage = 25 })
```

## Type packs

Several values can be sent without a wrapper table by writing a type pack. The values become separate arguments on both sides.

```cheeto copy
event Scored {
    From: Server,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: ManyAsync,
    Data: (Instance(Player), u32, string(0..32))
}
```

```lua copy
Network.Scored.FireAll(player, 150, "Headshot")

Network.Scored.On(function(player, points, reason) end)
```

## Events without data

Omit `Data` for a signal with no payload:

```cheeto copy
event RoundStarted {
    From: Server,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: ManyAsync
}
```

```lua copy
Network.RoundStarted.FireAll()
```

## Delivery order

Reliable events to one peer arrive in the order they were fired, across all reliable events of the module, because they share one batched stream. Unreliable events are independent and can arrive in any order or not at all.

<Callout type="info">
Reliable events that arrive before any listener is connected are queued, up to [`MaxQueuedEvents`](/reference/fields#maxqueuedevents), and delivered when the first listener connects. Unreliable events that arrive with no listener are discarded.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/declarations/export.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "export"
description: "Generate standalone Read and Write functions for a type."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# export

Prefixing a type declaration with `export` adds a `Read` and `Write` pair for it to both generated modules. They serialize a value into a standalone buffer with the same encoding Cheeto uses on the wire, which is useful for DataStore payloads, custom replication, or sending a pre-encoded blob through a `buffer` field.

```cheeto copy
export struct Snapshot {
    Tick: u32,
    Position: vector<i16>,
    Health: u8
}

export type Tick = u32
```

`export` works in front of `type`, `struct`, `enum`, `map` and `set`.

## In Luau

```lua copy
local encoded: buffer = Network.Snapshot.Write({ Tick = 120, Position = position, Health = 90 })
local decoded = Network.Snapshot.Read(encoded)
```

See [Exported type](/reference/api/exports) for the full API.

<Callout type="warning">
Types that contain `Instance` or `unknown` compile, but do not round-trip: those values travel beside the buffer rather than inside it, so `Read` cannot recover them.
</Callout>

<Callout type="info">
The buffer uses the module's current [encoding options](/reference/options/encoding). A buffer written with varints on cannot be read with varints off. Keep those options fixed for anything you store.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/declarations/function.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "function"
description: "Client-to-server requests that yield for a typed reply."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# function

A `function` is a request from a client that the server answers. It replaces a `RemoteFunction`, without the risk of a client hanging a server thread, because the server never invokes clients.

```cheeto copy
function GetInventory {
    Yield: Coroutine,
    Policy: "inventory",
    InvokeTimeoutSeconds: 10,
    Data: u8,
    Return: struct {
        Items: string(0..32)[..64],
        Capacity: u8
    }
}
```

## Fields

`Yield` is required. `Data` and `Return` are optional.

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`Yield`](/reference/fields#yield) | `Coroutine`, `Future` or `Promise`: what `Invoke` returns |
| [`Data`](/reference/fields#data) | What the client sends |
| [`Return`](/reference/fields#return) | What the server returns |
| [`MaxPendingInvokes`](/reference/fields#maxpendinginvokes), [`InvokeTimeoutSeconds`](/reference/fields#invoketimeoutseconds) | Invoke limits |
| [`Auth`](/reference/fields#auth), [`Policy`](/reference/fields#policy), [`PolicyGroup`](/reference/fields#policygroup), [`Honeypot`](/reference/fields#honeypot) | Access control, checked on the server |
| [`CooldownSeconds`](/reference/fields#cooldownseconds), [`RateLimitPerSecond`](/reference/fields#ratelimitpersecond), [`RateLimitBurst`](/reference/fields#ratelimitburst), [`MaxPacketBytes`](/reference/fields#maxpacketbytes), [`MaxQueuedEvents`](/reference/fields#maxqueuedevents) | Limits on requests |
| [`Idempotency`](/reference/fields#idempotency), constraints, [`Priority`](/reference/fields#priority), identity fields | As for events |

There is no `From`, `Type` or `Call`: requests always go client to server over the reliable remote.

## Generated API

| Server module | Client module |
| --- | --- |
| `On(listener)` | `Invoke(...)` |

See [Function endpoint](/reference/api/function).

```lua filename="Server.server.luau" copy
Network.GetInventory.On(function(player, page)
    local inventory = Inventories[player]
    return { Items = inventory:Page(page), Capacity = inventory.Capacity }
end)
```

```lua filename="Client.client.luau" copy
local ok, result = pcall(Network.GetInventory.Invoke, 1)
if ok then
    Inventory.Render(result.Items)
end
```

## Errors

`Invoke` raises an error on the client when:

- the server's listener errored (`There was an exception while processing "GetInventory".`),
- the request timed out ([`InvokeTimeoutSeconds`](/reference/fields#invoketimeoutseconds)),
- too many invokes are pending ([`MaxPendingInvokes`](/reference/fields#maxpendinginvokes)),
- invokes were cancelled with [`CancelInvocations`](/reference/api/module#cancelinvocations).

Wrap `Invoke` in `pcall`, or use `Future`/`Promise`, whenever a failure should not stop the calling thread.

<Callout type="warning">
A request the server drops, by a policy, auth rule, constraint, cooldown or rate limit, is answered with the drop reason, and the client's `Invoke` raises it. The timeout covers the rest: a lost connection, or a handler that never returns.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/declarations/import.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "import"
description: "Split a schema across several files."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# import

`import` includes another schema file. Its declarations are placed in a [scope](/reference/declarations/scope) named after the file, or after the name given with `as`.

```cheeto nocheck
import "./Shared"
import "./Economy/Items" as Items

struct Loadout {
    Primary: Shared.Weapon,
    Items: Items.ItemId[..8]
}
```

- The path is relative to the importing file. The `.cheeto` extension is optional.
- `as` accepts a name or a string: `as Items` and `as "Items"` are the same.
- Importing two files that end up with the same scope name is a compile error.
- Only the root file's `option` lines apply. Options in imported files are ignored.
- `cheeto --watch` also recompiles when any imported file changes.

<Callout type="info">
In the [Studio plugin](/getting-started/studio-plugin), the path names another saved schema instead of a file. Schemas are stored as StringValues under `ServerStorage.CHEETO_CONFIGURATION_FILES`, and dots separate folders: `import "Shared"` loads the schema saved as `Shared`, and the scope is named after the last segment.
</Callout>

## In Luau

Imported declarations are used exactly like scoped ones:

```lua copy
Network.Items.Purchase.Fire(itemId)
local weapon: Network.Shared_Weapon
```

```

`docs/pages/reference/declarations/map.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "map"
description: "Key-value tables with one key type and one value type."
---

# map

A `map` is a table whose keys all have one type and whose values all have one type.

```cheeto copy
map Scores = { [string]: u32 }
map Owners = { [u16]: Instance(Player) }
```

## Size

A range after the braces bounds the number of entries. Sending a map outside it raises an error; receiving one drops the event as malformed. The entry count uses only the bytes the maximum needs, so a map of at most 255 entries spends one byte on it.

```cheeto copy
map Scores = {[string(1..20)]: u32}(0..50)
```

Without a range, a map holds at most 65,535 entries, and the runtime drops any received table with more than [`MaxTableKeys`](/reference/options/limits#maxtablekeys) keys (2,048 by default).

## Generics

```cheeto copy
map Dictionary<K, V> = { [K]: V }
map NameToId = Dictionary<string, u32>
```

## Inline maps

A map can also be written inline where a type is expected:

```cheeto copy
event Leaderboard {
    From: Server,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: ManyAsync,
    Data: map { [string]: u32 }
}
```

```

`docs/pages/reference/declarations/scope.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "scope"
description: "Group declarations under a name to organise large schemas."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# scope

A `scope` groups declarations under a name. Endpoints inside it are nested in the generated module, and types get the scope name as a prefix.

```cheeto copy
scope Combat {
    type Damage = u16(0..500)

    event Hit {
        From: Client,
        Type: Reliable,
        Call: SingleAsync,
        Policy: "damage",
        Data: Damage
    }
}

struct Summary {
    Total: Combat.Damage
}
```

## In Luau

```lua copy
local Network = require(ReplicatedStorage.Network.Client)

Network.Combat.Hit.Fire(25)

local damage: Network.Combat_Damage = 25
```

Inside a scope, names from enclosing scopes are visible without a prefix. Outside, refer to scoped names with a dot: `Combat.Damage`.

<Callout type="info">
Scopes can nest. Every [`import`](/reference/declarations/import) also creates a scope named after the file or its alias.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/declarations/set.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "set"
description: "A fixed set of named flags, sent as bits."
---

# set

A `set` is a table of named flags. When sending, pass a table with `true` for the flags that are on; missing flags count as off. The receiver gets a table with every declared flag set to `true` or `false`.

```cheeto copy
set Permissions = {
    Kick,
    Ban,
    Mute
}
```

```lua copy
Network.PermissionsChanged.Fire(player, { Kick = true, Mute = true })
```

Each flag is sent as one bit, so a set of up to 8 flags costs one byte, up to 16 costs two, and so on. Keys that are not declared flags are ignored when writing.

```

`docs/pages/reference/declarations/struct.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "struct"
description: "A table with a fixed set of named fields."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# struct

A `struct` is a table with a fixed set of named fields, each with its own type. Field names never go over the wire: fields are written in declaration order, so a struct costs only the size of its values.

```cheeto copy
struct Entity {
    Health: u8(0..100),
    Position: vector,
    Rotation: u8,
    Animations: struct {
        First: u8?,
        Second: u8,
        Third: u8
    }
}
```

Fields are separated by commas. A trailing comma is allowed. Structs can also be written inline wherever a type is expected, as `Animations` shows.

## Merging

`..Name` copies every field of another struct into this one, like a table union in Luau:

```cheeto copy
struct Named {
    Name: string(1..32)
}

struct Priced {
    Price: u32
}

struct ShopItem {
    ..Named,
    ..Priced,
    Stock: u16
}
```

`ShopItem` has the fields `Name`, `Price` and `Stock`.

## Generics

```cheeto copy
struct Entity {
    Health: u8,
    Position: vector
}

struct Page<T> {
    Items: T[..50],
    Cursor: u32?
}

event EntityPage {
    From: Server,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: ManyAsync,
    Data: Page<Entity>
}
```

A generic struct is instantiated where it is used. It cannot be given a new name with `type`.

<Callout type="info">
Changing the order of struct fields changes the wire layout. Increase [`Version`](/reference/options/versioning#version) when you reorder, add or remove fields.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/declarations/type.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "type"
description: "Name a type so it can be reused across declarations."
---

# type

`type` gives a name to any type expression. The name can then be used anywhere a type is expected, including in other files through [`import`](/reference/declarations/import).

```cheeto copy
type Health = u8(0..100)
type Position = vector<i16>
type UserIds = f64[..50]
type Nickname = string(3..20)?

event HealthChanged {
    From: Server,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: ManyAsync,
    Data: (Instance(Player), Health)
}
```

A `type` generates a Luau type alias in the generated modules, and in the [`TypesOutput`](/reference/options/output#typesoutput) module when one is configured. Types declared inside a [`scope`](/reference/declarations/scope) are prefixed with the scope name, for example `Combat_Health`.

## What a type can name

`type` names primitives and anything built from them with ranges, encodings, arrays and optionals. It can also alias any declared type, including a struct, map or enum, or a generic type with its parameters filled in:

```cheeto copy
struct Item {
    Id: u16,
    Count: u8
}

type Reward = Item

struct Pair<A, B> {
    First: A,
    Second: B
}

export type Coordinates = Pair<i16, i16>
```

An alias of a generic type with its parameters filled in is how you [export](/reference/declarations/export) a generic type, which cannot be exported directly.

`map` and `enum` aliases use their own keyword: `map Scores = Dictionary<string, u32>`, `enum Outcome = Result<u32>`.

To export read and write functions for a type, prefix it with [`export`](/reference/declarations/export).

```

`docs/pages/reference/drop-reasons.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Drop reasons"
description: "Every reason Cheeto drops a packet or event, what triggers it, and where it happens."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Drop reasons

When the runtime drops something it records a reason. The reason appears in [`Security.OnViolation`](/reference/api/security#onviolation) reports, the [`Drop`](/reference/api/hooks#drop) hook, capture entries, and `Stats().DroppedPackets`. The full list is available at runtime as [`Transport.Errors`](/reference/api/transport#errors).

Drops never throw into your code. A dropped event is skipped and the rest of its packet is still processed, unless the reason says the whole packet is dropped.

## Packet-level

These discard an entire remote call before any event in it is read.

| Reason | Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| `InvalidBuffer` | The remote was fired with something other than a buffer. Only a hand-crafted remote call does this. |
| `InvalidInstances` | The second remote argument was not a table |
| `MaxPacketBytes` | The call was larger than [`MaxReliablePacketBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxreliablepacketbytes) or [`MaxUnreliablePacketBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxunreliablepacketbytes). Also used on the sender for an outgoing batch or unreliable event over the cap |
| `RateLimit` | The sender exceeded the per-remote-call [`RateLimitPerSecond`](/reference/options/limits#ratelimitpersecond) |
| `MiddlewareRejected` | A packet-level [`BeforeReceive`](/reference/api/hooks#beforereceive) hook returned `false` |
| `FragmentOverflow` | A new fragmented packet would exceed [`MaxInFlightFragments`](/reference/options/limits#maxinflightfragments) |
| `FragmentTimeout` | A fragmented packet was not completed within [`FragmentTimeoutSeconds`](/reference/options/limits#fragmenttimeoutseconds) |

## Event-level

These discard one event. They are listed in the order the receive path checks them; see [The receive pipeline](/concepts/receive-pipeline).

| Reason | Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| `MalformedPacket` | A frame header or payload could not be read, a value failed its type or range check, or a required Instance arrived as `nil` |
| `MaxPacketBytes` | The packet was larger than the endpoint's own [`MaxPacketBytes`](/reference/fields#maxpacketbytes) |
| `Honeypot` | The endpoint is marked [`Honeypot`](/reference/fields#honeypot) |
| `RateLimit` | The sender exceeded the endpoint's [`RateLimitPerSecond`](/reference/fields#ratelimitpersecond) |
| `MiddlewareRejected` | A per-event `BeforeReceive` hook returned `false` |
| `AuthRejected` | The [`Auth`](/reference/fields#auth) rule returned something other than `true`, errored, or is not registered |
| `KillSwitch` | The endpoint or its policy group is [killed](/reference/api/security#kill) |
| `PolicyRejected` | The policy denied, errored or is not registered, the policy group is not registered, or [`RequirePolicies`](/reference/options/security#requirepolicies) is on and the endpoint has no `Policy`, `PolicyGroup` or `Auth` |
| `OutOfOrder` | A [`Sequenced`](/reference/fields#reliabilitymode) event arrived that was not newer than the last one accepted from that peer |
| `Cooldown` | The sender used the endpoint again before its [`CooldownSeconds`](/reference/fields#cooldownseconds) had passed |
| *custom* | A policy returned `false, "your-reason"` |
| `ReplayDuplicate` | A predicted event reused a sequence number, or failed [`Idempotency`](/reference/fields#idempotency) |
| `ReplayStale` | A predicted event's sequence number was too far behind ([`ReplayWindowSize`](/reference/options/limits#replaywindowsize)) |
| `Canonicalization` | The decoded payload had a non-finite number, an impossible vector or CFrame, a table too deep or too large, a sparse array, an unsupported key type, or a string over [`MaxPayloadStringBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxpayloadstringbytes) |
| `DecodeBudget` | Checking the payload took more than [`MaxDecodeOperations`](/reference/options/limits#maxdecodeoperations) steps |
| `ConstraintRejected` | A [`Validate`](/reference/api/hooks#validate) hook returned `false` |
| `QueueFull` | No listener was connected and the endpoint's queue reached [`MaxQueuedEvents`](/reference/fields#maxqueuedevents) |

## Send-side

| Reason | Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| `MiddlewareRejected` | A [`BeforeSend`](/reference/api/hooks#beforesend) hook returned `false` |
| `KillSwitch` | The endpoint is killed |
| `Backpressure` | A `Cosmetic` or `Background` event was shed because the peer's queue exceeded [`MaxQueuedBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxqueuedbytes) |

## Handshake

| Reason | Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| `MalformedHandshake` | The handshake frame could not be read |
| `IncompatibleProtocol` | The peer's handshake named another schema fingerprint or a version below `MinimumSchemaVersion`. On the server, that handshake and every later packet from the player are dropped; see [`IncompatiblePeerAction`](/reference/options/versioning#incompatiblepeeraction) |

## Security reports

These are not packet drops. They appear as `Reason` in violation reports from the shield and integrity systems.

| Reason | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `ClientShield`, `ExploitEnvironment`, `MetamethodHook`, `InfiniteYield`, `SaveInstance`, `DexExplorer`, `RemoteSpy` | [Client shield](/security/client-shield) probes |
| `RemoteDecoy` | A [decoy remote](/security/remote-hardening) was fired |
| `IntegrityReceiptMissing`, `IntegrityReceiptInvalid`, `IntegrityEvaluatorFailed` | [Client integrity](/security/client-integrity) |
| `HorizontalDisplacement`, `VerticalDisplacement`, `WalkSpeedMutation`, `CollidableTraversal`, `NonFiniteMovement` | [Character integrity](/security/character-integrity), joined with `+` when several apply |

<Callout type="info">
`ClientIntegrity` and `CharacterIntegrity` are also defined in `Transport.Errors` as category names. Reports use the specific reasons above.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/fields.mdx`:

title: "Endpoint fields"
description: "Every field accepted inside event, function and channel blocks, with type, default, and exact runtime behaviour."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Spec } from '../../components/Reference'

# Endpoint fields

Fields go inside an [`event`](/reference/declarations/event), [`function`](/reference/declarations/function) or [`channel`](/reference/declarations/channel) block as `Name: Value`, separated by commas. Field names are also accepted in all lowercase, so `from: Client` works too. An unknown field, a repeated field, or a value outside a field's allowed set is a compile error.

<Callout type="info">
**Access fields belong on what clients send.** `Auth`, `Policy`, `PolicyGroup`, `CooldownSeconds`, `Idempotency` and the constraint fields are checked where a packet arrives, and rules are registered on the server. On a server-sent event or a channel they are a compile error (`Field "Policy" cannot be used here`). Rate limits and size caps are allowed everywhere: they bound work on whichever side receives.
</Callout>
