## Delivery

### `From`

<Spec type="identifier" default="required" values={<><code>Server</code>, <code>Client</code></>} on="event" />

Which side sends the event. The sending side's module gets the fire methods and the receiving side gets `On` (or `Iter` for polling). Functions have no `From`: clients always invoke and the server always answers.

### `Type`

<Spec type="identifier" default={<>required for events; <code>Reliable</code> for channels</>} values={<><code>Reliable</code>, <code>Unreliable</code></>} on="event, channel" />

- `Reliable` events are batched per peer, sent once per frame over a `RemoteEvent`, arrive in order, and can be [fragmented](/concepts/batching-and-flushing#fragmentation) when large.
- `Unreliable` events are sent immediately, one `UnreliableRemoteEvent` call per `Fire`, may be lost or reordered, and are capped by [`MaxUnreliablePacketBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxunreliablepacketbytes).

Functions are always reliable.

### `Call`

<Spec type="identifier" default="required" values={<><code>SingleSync</code>, <code>SingleAsync</code>, <code>ManySync</code>, <code>ManyAsync</code>, <code>Polling</code></>} on="event" />

How the receiving side delivers events.

| Value | Listeners | Listener runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SingleSync` | One; connecting another replaces it | Inline, on the receive thread |
| `SingleAsync` | One; connecting another replaces it | In a new thread (`task.spawn`) |
| `ManySync` | Any number | Inline, in connection order |
| `ManyAsync` | Any number | Each in a new thread |
| `Polling` | None | Queued; read with `Iter` |

Sync listeners must not yield or error. A yielding sync listener delays every event after it in the same packet; [`SyncValidation`](/reference/options/runtime#syncvalidation) warns when it happens.

### `Poll`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} on="event" />

`Poll: true` forces `Call` to `Polling` regardless of what `Call` says. `Call` must still be present.

### `Yield`

<Spec type="identifier" default="required" values={<><code>Coroutine</code>, <code>Future</code>, <code>Promise</code></>} on="function" />

What `Invoke` returns on the client.

| Value | `Invoke` returns | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Coroutine` | The return value, after yielding | nothing |
| `Future` | A Future created with `Future.Try` | [`FutureLibrary`](/reference/options/output#futurelibrary) |
| `Promise` | A Promise | [`PromiseLibrary`](/reference/options/output#promiselibrary) |

### `Data`

<Spec type="type or type pack" default="no data" on="event, function, channel (required)" />

What the endpoint carries. Any [type](/reference/types/numbers), a reference to a declared type, an inline `struct`, or a parenthesized **type pack** of several values:

```cheeto copy
event Hit {
    From: Client,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Policy: "combat",
    Data: (Instance(Player), u16(0..500), boolean)
}
```

A type pack becomes separate arguments: `Fire(target, damage, critical)`.

### `Return`

<Spec type="type or type pack" default="no value" on="function" />

What the server's listener returns to the invoking client.

### `Predict`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<>generated unless <code>EnablePrediction = false</code></>} on="event (client-origin)" />

Client-origin events get a [`Predict`](/reference/api/event#predict) method by default. `Predict: true` keeps it even when [`EnablePrediction`](/reference/options/runtime#enableprediction) is `false` at compile time.

## Channels

### `Scope`

<Spec type="identifier" default={<code>Player</code>} values={<><code>Player</code>, <code>Global</code>, <code>Group</code>, <code>Zone</code>, <code>Party</code>, <code>Match</code>, <code>Team</code>, <code>Cell</code>, <code>Owner</code></>} on="channel" />

Chooses what the shorthand `Set`, `Patch` and `Flush` target:

| Value | `Set(...)` means |
| --- | --- |
| `Player` | `SetPlayer(player, value)` |
| `Global` | `SetAll(value)` |
| `Group` | `SetGroup(group, value)` |
| `Zone` | `SetZone(zone, value)` |
| `Party`, `Match`, `Team`, `Cell`, `Owner` | `SetScope(kind, key, value)`: every player in that party, match, team, cell or owner set |

All targeted variants are generated regardless. Party, match, cell and owner membership comes from [`Replication.SetParty`](/reference/api/replication#setparty) and its siblings; `Team` also includes every player whose Roblox `Team` has that name. [`Interest`](#interest) wins when both are set.

### `TickRate`

<Spec type="number (per second)" default="every flush" on="channel" />

How often the server automatically flushes pending changes, at most. `20` flushes at most every 50 ms. Without it, pending changes are flushed on every replication step.

### `Delta`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<><code>true</code> when <code>Data</code> is a struct</>} on="channel" />

With a struct payload, `Patch` sends only the changed fields plus a bitmask, instead of the whole value. `Delta: false` always sends the full value. Non-struct payloads always send the full value.

### `KeyframeRate`

<Spec type="number (per second)" default="none" on="channel" />

How often a full snapshot is forced even when only deltas are pending, so a client that missed state recovers.

### `Interest`

<Spec type="identifier" default={<code>None</code>} values={<><code>None</code>, <code>Zone</code>, <code>Distance</code>, <code>Party</code>, <code>Match</code>, <code>Team</code>, <code>Cell</code>, <code>Owner</code></>} on="channel" />

`Zone` maps `Set`/`Patch` to `SetZone`/`PatchZone`, and `Distance` maps them to `SetDistance`/`PatchDistance`. `Party`, `Match`, `Team`, `Cell` and `Owner` map them to `SetScope`/`PatchScope` with that kind, as for [`Scope`](#scope). `None` leaves `Scope` in charge. See [Audiences and routing](/concepts/interest-and-routing).

### `InterestRadius`

<Spec type="number (studs)" default={<code>0</code>} on="channel" />

Default radius for the `Distance` variants when no radius is passed.

## Access control

### `Auth`

<Spec type="string" default="none" on="client-sent event, function" />

Names an [auth rule](/security/auth-rules) that must return `true` for each received event. Register rules with [`UseAuth`](/reference/api/module#useauth). The built-in rules are `AlivePlayer` (sender is a player still in the game) and `ServerOnly` (sender is the server).

A rule name that was never registered drops **every** packet on the endpoint with `AuthRejected`, and logs one warning per name. A rule that errors also drops.

```cheeto copy
event UseItem {
    From: Client,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Auth: "AlivePlayer",
    Policy: "inventory",
    Data: u16
}
```

### `Policy`

<Spec type="string" default="none" on="client-sent event, function" />

Names a [policy](/security/policies) that must allow the sender. Policies run before the payload is decoded and receive a context with the sender, endpoint name, constraints and packet size. Register them with [`Security.RegisterPolicy`](/reference/api/security#registerpolicy).

Policies fail closed: a name nobody registered drops every packet on the endpoint with `PolicyRejected` and warns once. A policy can return a reason string as its second value, which becomes the drop reason and, for functions and predictions, the reason the client is told.

### `PolicyGroup`

<Spec type="string" default="none" on="event, function" />

Names a group registered with [`Security.RegisterPolicyGroup`](/reference/api/security#registerpolicygroup). Every policy in the group must allow the sender. A group that was never registered drops every packet with `PolicyRejected` and warns once, like an unregistered policy. The group name is also the unit for [`Security.KillPolicyGroup`](/reference/api/security#killpolicygroup).

### `Honeypot`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} on="event, function" />

Marks an endpoint that no legitimate code calls. Traffic on it is dropped before rate limiting and decoding, with reason `Honeypot`. See [Honeypots](/security/honeypots).

## Limits

### `CooldownSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<><code>0</code> (off)</>} on="event, function" />

Minimum time between two accepted calls from the same sender on this endpoint. Calls inside the window are dropped with `Cooldown` before decoding. Enforced by the runtime; no rule needed.

Set it looser than the client's own retry interval, or legitimate retries are dropped.

### `RateLimitPerSecond`

<Spec type="number" default={<>the schema's <code>RateLimitPerSecond</code> option if written, else off</>} on="event, function, channel" />

A per-sender token bucket for this endpoint. Excess events are dropped with `RateLimit`. See [`RateLimitPerSecond`](/reference/options/limits#ratelimitpersecond) for how this interacts with the per-packet limit.

### `RateLimitBurst`

<Spec type="number" default={<>the schema option, else equal to the rate</>} on="event, function, channel" />

Bucket capacity for this endpoint.

### `MaxPacketBytes`

<Spec type="number (bytes)" default={<>the schema's <code>MaxPacketBytes</code> option if written, else no per-endpoint check</>} on="event, function, channel" />

Drops this endpoint's event with `MaxPacketBytes` when its own frame is larger than this many bytes. Other events batched in the same packet do not count against it; the packet as a whole is bounded by [`MaxReliablePacketBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxreliablepacketbytes) and [`MaxUnreliablePacketBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxunreliablepacketbytes).

### `MaxQueuedEvents`

<Spec type="number" default={<>the schema option, else <code>256</code></>} on="event, function, channel" />

Maximum events waiting for a listener (or for `Iter`) on this endpoint before new ones are dropped with `QueueFull`.

### `MaxPendingInvokes`

<Spec type="number" default={<>the runtime's <code>MaxPendingInvokes</code></>} on="function" />

Maximum invokes of this function waiting for a reply on one client. `Invoke` raises an error beyond it, before anything is sent.

### `InvokeTimeoutSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<>the runtime's <code>InvokeTimeoutSeconds</code></>} on="function" />

How long `Invoke` waits before raising `Invoke timed out after N seconds.` Without this field the runtime value applies, which is the security profile's default (10 s for Production, 5 s for Competitive, none for Development), the schema option when written, or whatever [`Configure`](/reference/api/module#configure) set last.

## Replay

### `Idempotency`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} on="client-sent event, function" />

Every send carries a 16-bit sequence number, and the server drops a packet whose number is not newer than the last one it accepted from that sender, with reason `OutOfOrder`. A captured packet sent a second time is therefore never delivered twice. Predicted sends are also deduplicated by prediction id for 120 seconds, with `ReplayDuplicate`.

This stops replays. A packet built from scratch with a fresh number is a new request; see [Replay and idempotency](/security/replay-and-idempotency).

## Constraints

Constraints are enforced by the runtime, on the server, before your handler runs. The **sender** constraints (`RequireTeam`, `RequireZone`, `RequireMatch`, `RequireCharacterState`) are checked before the payload is decoded; the **payload** constraints (`MaxDistance`, `RequireOwnership`, `RequireObjectHandle`, `RequireServerKnownId`, `RequireInventoryOwnership`) after it, looking at the arguments and the fields of table arguments one level deep. A rejected packet is dropped with `ConstraintRejected`.

Every constraint is also passed to your policies and to the [`Validate`](/reference/api/hooks#validate) hook as `Constraints`, so you can add conditions of your own. `Validate` runs for endpoints that declare a payload constraint. See [Constraints and Validate](/security/constraints).

### `Risk`

<Spec type="identifier" default="none" on="event, function, channel" />

A free-form tag, such as `Damage` or `Currency`, passed as `Constraints.Risk`. It checks nothing and does not trigger `Validate`.

### `MaxDistance`

<Spec type="number (studs)" default={<><code>0</code> (off)</>} on="client-sent event, function" />

Every `Vector3`, `CFrame`, `BasePart`, `Model` and `Attachment` in the payload must be within this distance of the sender's `HumanoidRootPart` (or character pivot). When the payload contains a position and the sender has no character, the packet is rejected. Payloads without positions pass.

```cheeto copy
event PlaceBlock {
    From: Client,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Policy: "building",
    MaxDistance: 24,
    Data: vector
}
```

### `RequireOwnership`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} on="client-sent event, function" />

Every Instance in the payload must belong to the sender: registered to them with [`Replication.SetObjectOwner`](/reference/api/replication#setobjectowner), inside their character, or carrying an `OwnerUserId` attribute equal to their `UserId`. Ancestors count, so a part of an owned model is owned.

### `RequireTeam`

<Spec type="string" default="none" on="client-sent event, function" />

The sender's Roblox `Team` must have this name, or the sender must have been added to it with [`Replication.SetTeam`](/reference/api/replication#setteam).

### `RequireZone`

<Spec type="string" default="none" on="client-sent event, function" />

The sender must be in this zone, as set with [`Security.SetZone`](/reference/api/security#setzone).

### `RequireMatch`

<Spec type="string" default="none" on="client-sent event, function" />

The sender must be in this match, as set with [`Replication.SetMatch`](/reference/api/replication#setmatch).

### `RequireInventoryOwnership`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} on="client-sent event, function" />

Calls the resolver set with [`Security.SetInventoryResolver`](/reference/api/security#setinventoryresolver) with the sender and the decoded arguments, and rejects unless it returns `true`. Until a resolver is set, every packet is rejected and one warning is logged.

### `RequireCharacterState`

<Spec type="string" default="none" on="client-sent event, function" />

`Alive` requires a character whose Humanoid has health above 0, `Dead` the opposite. Any other value is compared with the name of the Humanoid's current state, for example `Running` or `Freefall`.

### `RequireObjectHandle`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} on="client-sent event, function" />

The first number in the payload must be a [handle](/security/handles-and-capabilities) that resolves for the sender with [`Handles.Resolve`](/reference/api/handles#resolve).

### `RequireServerKnownId`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} on="client-sent event, function" />

The first number or string in the payload must be an id registered with [`Security.RegisterKnownId`](/reference/api/security#registerknownid), for this sender or for anyone.

## Scheduling

### `Priority`

<Spec type="identifier" default={<code>Gameplay</code>} values={<><code>Critical</code>, <code>Gameplay</code>, <code>Cosmetic</code>, <code>Background</code></>} on="event, function, channel" />

Decides which outgoing events may be shed under backpressure: `Cosmetic` and `Background` events are dropped with `Backpressure` when the peer's tracked queue is over [`MaxQueuedBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxqueuedbytes) and [`LowPriorityShedding`](/reference/options/limits#lowpriorityshedding) is on. It does not reorder events or change when they are flushed.

### `ReliabilityMode`

<Spec type="identifier" default={<>follows <code>Type</code></>} values={<><code>Reliable</code>, <code>Unreliable</code>, <code>Sequenced</code>, <code>Latest</code></>} on="event" />

| Value | Delivery |
| --- | --- |
| `Reliable`, `Unreliable` | Same as `Type`; a value that contradicts `Type` is a compile error |
| `Sequenced` | Every send carries a 16-bit sequence number; the receiver drops anything not newer than the last one it accepted from that peer, with `OutOfOrder`. Use it on unreliable events where a stale value is worse than none, such as positions |
| `Latest` | Only the last send per recipient in each replication step is delivered; earlier ones are discarded before they are sent. A replaced prediction rolls back with the reason `Superseded` |

```cheeto copy
event AimDirection {
    From: Client,
    Type: Unreliable,
    Call: ManyAsync,
    ReliabilityMode: Latest,
    Data: vector
}
```

### `CoalesceKey`

<Spec type="string" default="none" on="event" />

`Latest` delivery with a shared slot: every event with the same key replaces the previous one queued for the same recipient in this replication step, whichever endpoint it came from. Use it when several endpoints describe one piece of state and only the newest matters.

## Identity

### `WireId`

<Spec type="number (0–251)" default={<>the lock's id, else the lowest free one</>} on="event, function, channel" />

Pins the id this endpoint is sent under on its channel. Two endpoints on one channel with the same id is a compile error. Without it, the endpoint keeps the id recorded in [`cheeto.lock`](/reference/lockfile), or takes the lowest free id in declaration order. See [Keeping ids stable](/concepts/schema-versioning#keeping-ids-stable).

### `ReservedId`

<Spec type="number (0–251)" default="none" on="event, function, channel" />

Reserves an id on this endpoint's channel so nothing else is assigned it, for example the id of an endpoint you removed before the project had a lockfile.

### `DeprecatedId`

<Spec type="number (0–251)" default="none" on="event, function, channel" />

The id this endpoint used before. It is sent under its current id but still accepted on this one, so builds from before a renumbering keep working, and the old id is reserved. Remove it once no such build can be running.

```

## Reading the entries

Every member starts with a signature strip:

<Sig side="server">{"Fire(player: Player, ...data): ()"}</Sig>

The badge says where the member exists. **Server** members are only on the module returned by `ServerOutput`, **Client** members only on `ClientOutput`, and **Server + Client** members on both. **Yields** means the call can suspend the current thread.

Options and fields start with a fact table instead:

<Spec type={<code>number</code>} default={<><code>0</code> (disabled)</>} on="event, function" />

In examples, `Network` is the module you required, for instance `require(ReplicatedStorage.Network.Server)`.

`docs/pages/reference/lockfile.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "cheeto.lock format"
description: "What the lockfile records, how the compiler uses it to keep ids stable, and what --check-lock catches."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# cheeto.lock format

`cheeto --write-lock` writes `cheeto.lock` next to the schema. It does two jobs:

- **It keeps endpoint ids stable.** Every command-line compile reads it, and each endpoint keeps the id the lock recorded for its name, kind and channel. Reordering endpoints or removing one no longer renumbers the rest.
- **It puts wire changes in review.** `cheeto --check-lock` fails when the schema no longer produces the same lock, listing the lines that changed.

Commit the file next to the schema.

<Callout type="info">
Only the command-line compiler reads the lock. The Studio plugin compiles without it and numbers endpoints in declaration order, so build releases with the CLI, or pin the ids that matter with [`WireId`](/reference/fields#wireid).
</Callout>

```json
{
	"schemaVersion": 7,
	"minimumSchemaVersion": 7,
	"schemaHash": "9c41d27a0b5e83f1",
	"options": {
		"securityProfile": "Production",
		"requirePolicies": true,
		"maxReliablePacketBytes": 65536,
		"maxUnreliablePacketBytes": 900
	},
	"endpoints": {
		"DealDamage": { "kind": "Event", "channel": "Reliable", "id": 0, "shape": "5d0c8e17a4b2f963" },
		"GetInventory": { "kind": "Function", "channel": "Reliable", "id": 1, "deprecatedId": 4, "shape": "e2a90b4c7d1f5836" },
		"OldTrade": { "kind": "Event", "channel": "Reliable", "id": 2, "retired": true }
	},
	"types": {
		"Hit": "0b7e2d91c4a8f356"
	}
}
```

| Field | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `schemaVersion`, `minimumSchemaVersion` | From the options |
| `schemaHash` | The [schema fingerprint](/reference/options/versioning#the-schema-fingerprint) the handshake compares |
| `options` | Security profile, `RequirePolicies`, and the two packet caps as written in the schema (defaults shown when unset) |
| `endpoints` | Every event, function and channel by scope-qualified name, with its kind, channel, id, `deprecatedId` and `reservedId` when set, and a hash of its payload shape |
| `types` | A hash of every declared type's shape |

## How ids are assigned

Reliable and unreliable endpoints are numbered separately, from 0 to 251. For each endpoint, in this order:

1. an explicit [`WireId`](/reference/fields#wireid);
2. the id the lock records for the same name, kind and channel;
3. the lowest free id, in declaration order.

`ReservedId` and `DeprecatedId` values, and the ids of retired endpoints, are never handed out. Two endpoints claiming one id is a compile error that names both.

## Retired endpoints

When an endpoint leaves the schema, `--write-lock` keeps its entry with `"retired": true`. Its id stays taken, so a new endpoint can never reuse it and be misread by a build that still has the old one. Delete a retired entry by hand only when no build using it can still be running.

## What --check-lock catches

`--check-lock` fails when:

- an endpoint is added, removed, renamed or renumbered;
- an endpoint's payload changes shape: a field's type, range, order, name or optionality, a channel's delta mode, or an event's delivery mode;
- a type is added, removed or changes shape;
- the version, fingerprint, profile, `RequirePolicies` or packet caps change.

The error lists the lines the schema now produces. Run `--write-lock` only when the change is intentional.

<Callout type="info">
The file may be checked out with CRLF line endings on Windows; `--check-lock` ignores the difference. A lock written by Cheeto 1.0, which had no `endpoints` section, is ignored until it is rewritten.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/options/character-integrity.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Character integrity options"
description: "Options for server-side movement sampling, scoring, correction and kicks."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Spec } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Character integrity options

[Character integrity](/security/character-integrity) samples each character's `HumanoidRootPart` on the server and scores movement that the configured limits cannot explain. The allowance per sample is:

```text
nominal    = max(MaxHorizontalSpeed, WalkSpeed × SpeedMultiplier)
allowedH   = nominal × dt
           + min(assembly horizontal speed, 2 × nominal) × dt × 0.5
           + DistanceSlack
           + ping (0–2 s) × nominal × PingAllowance
allowedV   = the same with MaxVerticalSpeed and vertical speed
```

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`EnableCharacterIntegrity`](#enablecharacterintegrity) | boolean | `false` (`true` under `Maximum`) |
| [`CharacterIntegrityMode`](#characterintegritymode) | identifier | `Observe` (`Correct` under `Maximum`) |
| [`CharacterIntegrityKick`](#characterintegritykick) | boolean | `false` |
| [`CharacterIntegritySampleIntervalSeconds`](#characterintegritysampleintervalseconds) | number | `0.25` |
| [`CharacterIntegrityJoinGraceSeconds`](#characterintegrityjoingraceseconds) | number | `5` |
| [`CharacterIntegrityTeleportGraceSeconds`](#characterintegrityteleportgraceseconds) | number | `2` |
| [`CharacterIntegrityMaxStepSeconds`](#characterintegritymaxstepseconds) | number | `1.5` |
| [`CharacterIntegrityMaxHorizontalSpeed`](#characterintegritymaxhorizontalspeed) | number | `64` |
| [`CharacterIntegrityMaxVerticalSpeed`](#characterintegritymaxverticalspeed) | number | `120` |
| [`CharacterIntegritySpeedMultiplier`](#characterintegrityspeedmultiplier) | number | `1.75` |
| [`CharacterIntegrityDistanceSlack`](#characterintegritydistanceslack) | number | `12` |
| [`CharacterIntegrityPingAllowance`](#characterintegritypingallowance) | number | `1.5` |
| [`CharacterIntegrityScoreDecayPerSecond`](#characterintegrityscoredecaypersecond) | number | `2` |
| [`CharacterIntegrityCorrectionScore`](#characterintegritycorrectionscore) | number | `12` |
| [`CharacterIntegrityKickScore`](#characterintegritykickscore) | number | `40` |
| [`CharacterIntegrityMaxConsecutiveBreaches`](#characterintegritymaxconsecutivebreaches) | number | `8` |
| [`CharacterIntegrityCorrectionCooldownSeconds`](#characterintegritycorrectioncooldownseconds) | number | `1` |
| [`CharacterIntegrityReportCooldownSeconds`](#characterintegrityreportcooldownseconds) | number | `1` |
| [`CharacterIntegrityHistoryLimit`](#characterintegrityhistorylimit) | number | `32` |

## `EnableCharacterIntegrity`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<><code>false</code> (<code>true</code> under <code>Maximum</code>)</>} />

Turns sampling on. Sampling runs in the server's flush step, so with [`ManualReplication`](/reference/options/runtime#manualreplication) it only runs when you call `StepReplication`.

## `CharacterIntegrityMode`

<Spec type="identifier" default={<><code>Observe</code> (<code>Correct</code> under <code>Maximum</code>)</>} values={<><code>Observe</code>, <code>Report</code>, <code>Correct</code>, <code>Kick</code></>} />

What happens when a sample is suspicious:

| Mode | Records evidence | `OnViolation` | Moves the character back | Kicks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Observe` | Yes | No | No | No |
| `Report` | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| `Correct` | Yes | Yes | Once the score reaches `CorrectionScore` | No |
| `Kick` | Yes | Yes | Yes, as `Correct` | When `CharacterIntegrityKick` is on, the score reaches `KickScore` and there have been `MaxConsecutiveBreaches` breaches in a row |

Any other value is a compile error. The mode can be changed at runtime with `Configure`.

## `CharacterIntegrityKick`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} />

Second switch required for kicks in `Kick` mode, so a mode change alone cannot start kicking players. Stays `false` under `Maximum`.

## `CharacterIntegritySampleIntervalSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<code>0.25</code>} />

Time between samples of one character. Minimum `0.05`.

## `CharacterIntegrityJoinGraceSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<code>5</code>} />

No scoring for this long after a player starts being tracked or gets a new character.

## `CharacterIntegrityTeleportGraceSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<code>2</code>} />

No scoring for this long after [`Security.TeleportCharacter`](/reference/api/security#teleportcharacter) or an automatic correction. Also the default duration of [`Security.GrantMovementGrace`](/reference/api/security#grantmovementgrace).

## `CharacterIntegrityMaxStepSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<code>1.5</code>} />

If more time than this passed between two samples, for example during a server hitch, the sample is not scored and tracking resynchronizes from the current position. Minimum `0.1`.

## `CharacterIntegrityMaxHorizontalSpeed`

<Spec type="number (studs/s)" default={<code>64</code>} />

Baseline horizontal speed the allowance is built from, before the `WalkSpeed` multiplier. A `Humanoid.WalkSpeed` above `MaxHorizontalSpeed × SpeedMultiplier` is itself reported as `WalkSpeedMutation`.

## `CharacterIntegrityMaxVerticalSpeed`

<Spec type="number (studs/s)" default={<code>120</code>} />

Baseline vertical speed for the vertical allowance. Raise it for games with high jumps, launch pads or long falls.

## `CharacterIntegritySpeedMultiplier`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>1.75</code>} />

Multiplied with the current `WalkSpeed` to allow games that change `WalkSpeed` legitimately. Minimum `1`.

## `CharacterIntegrityDistanceSlack`

<Spec type="number (studs)" default={<code>12</code>} />

Flat distance added to every sample's allowance, to absorb physics jitter and small corrections.

## `CharacterIntegrityPingAllowance`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>1.5</code>} />

Scales how much extra distance a player's ping earns. Ping is read from `Player:GetNetworkPing()` and clamped to 0–2 seconds.

## `CharacterIntegrityScoreDecayPerSecond`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>2</code>} />

How fast the movement score falls back toward 0.

## `CharacterIntegrityCorrectionScore`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>12</code>} />

Score at which `Correct` and `Kick` modes move the character back to its last server-observed safe position.

## `CharacterIntegrityKickScore`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>40</code>} />

Score required for a kick in `Kick` mode.

## `CharacterIntegrityMaxConsecutiveBreaches`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>8</code>} />

Suspicious samples in a row required for a kick in `Kick` mode. Any clean sample resets the count.

## `CharacterIntegrityCorrectionCooldownSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<code>1</code>} />

Minimum time between two corrections of the same player.

## `CharacterIntegrityReportCooldownSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<code>1</code>} />

Per player and per reason, evidence inside this window still adds to the score but is not recorded or reported again. Kicks are never throttled.

## `CharacterIntegrityHistoryLimit`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>32</code>} />

Evidence entries kept per player. The server-wide evidence list keeps eight times this many.

<Callout type="info">
Tune movement limits in `Observe` mode first, using `Security.CharacterIntegrity()` snapshots from real sessions. See [Character integrity](/security/character-integrity).
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/options/client-integrity.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Client integrity options"
description: "Options for server-issued liveness challenges and how failed receipts are scored."
---

import { Spec } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Client integrity options

[Client integrity](/security/client-integrity) has the server send each client a one-time challenge; the client runs its checks and answers with a receipt. Missing, late, invalid or unhealthy receipts add evidence to a decaying score.

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`EnableClientIntegrity`](#enableclientintegrity) | boolean | `false` (`true` under `Maximum`) |
| [`ClientIntegrityChallengeIntervalSeconds`](#clientintegritychallengeintervalseconds) | number | `4` |
| [`ClientIntegrityReceiptTimeoutSeconds`](#clientintegrityreceipttimeoutseconds) | number | `8` |
| [`ClientIntegrityJoinGraceSeconds`](#clientintegrityjoingraceseconds) | number | `20` |
| [`ClientIntegrityScoreDecayPerSecond`](#clientintegrityscoredecaypersecond) | number | `0.5` |
| [`ClientIntegrityCleanReceiptDecay`](#clientintegritycleanreceiptdecay) | number | `2` |
| [`ClientIntegrityMissWeight`](#clientintegritymissweight) | number | `4` |
| [`ClientIntegrityInvalidWeight`](#clientintegrityinvalidweight) | number | `6` |
| [`ClientIntegrityScoreThreshold`](#clientintegrityscorethreshold) | number | `16` |
| [`ClientIntegrityMaxConsecutiveFailures`](#clientintegritymaxconsecutivefailures) | number | `4` |

A player is kicked only when **all** of these hold: [`ClientShieldKick`](/reference/options/client-shield#clientshieldkick) is on, the score is at least [`ClientIntegrityScoreThreshold`](#clientintegrityscorethreshold), and there have been at least [`ClientIntegrityMaxConsecutiveFailures`](#clientintegritymaxconsecutivefailures) failures in a row. A single miss never kicks.

## `EnableClientIntegrity`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<><code>false</code> (<code>true</code> under <code>Maximum</code>)</>} />

Turns the challenge loop on. Challenges are issued from the server's flush step, so with [`ManualReplication`](/reference/options/runtime#manualreplication) they only run when you call `StepReplication`.

## `ClientIntegrityChallengeIntervalSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<code>4</code>} />

Time between challenges to one player. Minimum `0.5`. Only one challenge per player is outstanding at a time.

## `ClientIntegrityReceiptTimeoutSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<code>8</code>} />

How long a client has to answer. A challenge not answered in time is recorded as `IntegrityReceiptMissing` with weight [`ClientIntegrityMissWeight`](#clientintegritymissweight). Minimum `0.5`.

## `ClientIntegrityJoinGraceSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<code>20</code>} />

No challenges are sent for this long after the server first tracks a player, so loading does not count against them. Also the default duration of [`Security.GrantIntegrityGrace`](/reference/api/security#grantintegritygrace).

## `ClientIntegrityScoreDecayPerSecond`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>0.5</code>} />

How much a player's integrity score drops per second. The score never goes below 0 or above 1000.

## `ClientIntegrityCleanReceiptDecay`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>2</code>} />

Subtracted from the score for each valid, healthy receipt. Also resets the consecutive-failure count.

## `ClientIntegrityMissWeight`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>4</code>} />

Score added when a receipt does not arrive before the deadline.

## `ClientIntegrityInvalidWeight`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>6</code>} />

Score added when a receipt is invalid (`IntegrityReceiptInvalid`: wrong challenge, expired, replayed completion counter, no samplers, bad checksum) or when a valid receipt reports a failed check (`IntegrityEvaluatorFailed`).

## `ClientIntegrityScoreThreshold`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>16</code>} />

Minimum score before a kick is possible.

## `ClientIntegrityMaxConsecutiveFailures`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>4</code>} />

Minimum number of failures in a row before a kick is possible. Values below 1 are treated as 1.

```

`docs/pages/reference/options/client-shield.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Client shield options"
description: "Options for the client-side exploit tripwires and how their reports turn into kicks."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Spec } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Client shield options

The [client shield](/security/client-shield) runs detection probes on each client and reports hits to the server over Cheeto's own frames. These options control whether it runs and what the server does with its reports.

| Option | Type | Default | Under `Maximum` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`EnableClientShield`](#enableclientshield) | boolean | `false` | `true` |
| [`ClientShieldStrict`](#clientshieldstrict) | boolean | `false` | `true` |
| [`ClientShieldKick`](#clientshieldkick) | boolean | `false` | `true` |
| [`ClientShieldKickMessage`](#clientshieldkickmessage) | string | `"Security check failed."` | same |
| [`ClientShieldProbeIntervalSeconds`](#clientshieldprobeintervalseconds) | number | `1.25` | same |
| [`ClientShieldReportCooldownSeconds`](#clientshieldreportcooldownseconds) | number | `2` | same |
| [`ClientShieldScoreThreshold`](#clientshieldscorethreshold) | number | `10` | same |

## `EnableClientShield`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<><code>false</code> (<code>true</code> under <code>Maximum</code>)</>} />

When `true`, the client module starts the probe loop as soon as it is required. The server processes shield reports whether or not this is set on the server.

## `ClientShieldStrict`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<><code>false</code> (<code>true</code> under <code>Maximum</code>)</>} />

With [`ClientShieldKick`](#clientshieldkick) on, strict mode kicks on the **first** report of any kind instead of waiting for [`ClientShieldScoreThreshold`](#clientshieldscorethreshold).

## `ClientShieldKick`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<><code>false</code> (<code>true</code> under <code>Maximum</code>)</>} />

Allows the server to kick. It gates three things: client-shield reports, [decoy remote](/security/remote-hardening#decoys) hits, and [client integrity](/security/client-integrity) failures. With it off, all three are still recorded and reported through `Security.OnViolation` with action `report`.

A player is kicked when this is on and any of these holds:

- the report was flagged as immediate (decoy remotes, the TextChat tripwire, the save-instance safe-mode error);
- [`ClientShieldStrict`](#clientshieldstrict) is on;
- the player's score for that report's reason reached [`ClientShieldScoreThreshold`](#clientshieldscorethreshold).

<Callout type="warning">
A false positive removes a real player. Ship with `ClientShieldKick = false`, watch `Security.OnViolation` on live servers, and turn kicks on once reports look clean.
</Callout>

## `ClientShieldKickMessage`

<Spec type="string" default={<code>"Security check failed."</code>} />

The message passed to `Player:Kick` for shield, decoy and integrity kicks.

## `ClientShieldProbeIntervalSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<code>1.25</code>} />

Time between probe sweeps on the client. Values below `0.5` are treated as `0.5`.

## `ClientShieldReportCooldownSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<code>2</code>} />

Per player and per reason, repeated reports inside this window still add to the score but are not recorded or passed to `OnViolation` again. Kicks are not throttled. The same cooldown throttles client integrity evidence.

## `ClientShieldScoreThreshold`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>10</code>} />

Per-reason score at which a non-strict shield kicks. Each report adds its weight, at least 1, to the player's score for that reason.

```

import { Spec } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Capture and diagnostics options

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`EnablePacketCapture`](#enablepacketcapture) | boolean | `false` |
| [`CaptureRedactions`](#captureredactions) | string | `""` |
| [`CaptureLimit`](#capturelimit) | number | `1024` |
| [`NoRawCaptureInProduction`](#norawcaptureinproduction) | boolean | `true` |
| [`EnableInspector`](#enableinspector) | boolean | `false` |

All five are runtime options and can be changed with `Configure`. See [Capture and replay](/operations/capture-and-replay) for how captures are used.

## `EnablePacketCapture`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} />

Records every sent, received and dropped event from the moment the module loads, as if [`Capture.Start`](/reference/api/capture#start) had been called. Capturing costs a table allocation and a payload summary per event, so keep it off in live servers unless you are investigating something.

## `CaptureRedactions`

<Spec type="string" default={<><code>""</code></>} />

A comma-separated list of field names. When a captured payload summary contains a table key with one of these names, its value is written as `[redacted]`. Whitespace around names is ignored. Replace the list at runtime with [`Capture.Redact`](/reference/api/capture#redact) or `Capture.Start({ Redactions = ... })`.

```cheeto copy
option CaptureRedactions = "Password,Token,Receipt"
```

Redaction only applies to the readable summary. Raw buffers, when kept, contain the original bytes; see [`NoRawCaptureInProduction`](#norawcaptureinproduction).

## `CaptureLimit`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>1024</code>} />

Maximum number of capture entries kept. When full, the oldest entry is removed for each new one.

## `NoRawCaptureInProduction`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>true</code>} />

When the [`SecurityProfile`](/reference/options/security#securityprofile) is anything other than `Development`, capture entries do not keep a copy of the raw packet buffer and are marked `Redaction.Raw = true`. [`Capture.ReplayRaw`](/reference/api/capture#replayraw) then has nothing to inject and counts those entries as `MissingRaw`. [`--hardening-checklist`](/reference/cli#--hardening-checklist) fails if this is set to `false`.

## `EnableInspector`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} />

Allows [`Inspector.Snapshot`](/reference/api/inspector#snapshot), which otherwise errors unless `Inspector.Enable(true)` was called. While the inspector is enabled, events are also recorded into the capture buffer even if capture was not started.

`docs/pages/reference/options/encoding.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Wire encoding"
description: "Options that change how values are packed into buffers."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Spec } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Wire encoding

These options change the bytes on the wire. Both sides read them from their own `RuntimeConfig`, so they must match on the server and the client.

<Callout type="error">
Do not change the encoding options with `Configure` on only one side. A server writing varints to a client that expects fixed-width integers misreads every packet after the first differing field, and the packets are dropped as `MalformedPacket`.
</Callout>

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`UseVarints`](#usevarints) | boolean | `true` |
| [`UseBitPacking`](#usebitpacking) | boolean | `true` |
| [`UseStringDictionaries`](#usestringdictionaries) | boolean | `false` |
| [`UseBufferPooling`](#usebufferpooling) | boolean | `true` |
| [`BufferPoolLimit`](#bufferpoollimit) | number | `64` |

## `UseVarints`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>true</code>} />

Writes 16-bit and 32-bit integers (`u16`, `u32`, `i16`, `i32`) and all length prefixes as LEB128 variable-length integers: 7 bits per byte, with the high bit marking that another byte follows. Signed integers are zig-zag encoded first, so small negative numbers stay small. `u8` and `i8` are always one byte.

| Value | `u16` fixed | `u16` varint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `25` | `19 00` | `19` |
| `300` | `2C 01` | `AC 02` |
| `40000` | `40 9C` | `C0 B8 02` |

Varints win whenever values are usually small, which is typical for counts, ids and damage. A `u32` near its maximum costs 5 bytes instead of 4.

## `UseBitPacking`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>true</code>} />

Packs booleans and the presence flags of optionals into single bits, eight per byte. With it off each takes a full byte.

## `UseStringDictionaries`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} />

Interns strings within one outgoing batch: the first occurrence is written in full and later occurrences of the same string in that batch are written as a small id. The dictionary resets after every flush. It helps when a batch repeats the same strings, such as item names in a list, and costs one extra byte per string otherwise.

## `UseBufferPooling`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>true</code>} />

Reuses send buffers between flushes instead of allocating new ones, in power-of-two size buckets starting at 64 bytes. Lowers garbage collection pressure on busy servers.

## `BufferPoolLimit`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>64</code>} />

How many buffers each size bucket keeps for reuse. Buffers released beyond this are left to the garbage collector.

```

`docs/pages/reference/options/limits.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Transport limits"
description: "Packet size caps, rate limits, queues, invoke limits, fragmentation, replay windows and decode budgets."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Spec } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Transport limits

These options bound how much a peer can send and how much work a packet can cost. Every drop they cause is reported through [`Security.OnViolation`](/reference/api/security#onviolation) with one of the [drop reasons](/reference/drop-reasons).

Defaults come from [`SecurityProfile`](/reference/options/security#securityprofile). `SecurityPreset = Maximum` without an explicit profile uses `Competitive`.

| Option | Development | Production | Competitive |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`MaxPacketBytes`](#maxpacketbytes) | 1,048,576 | 262,144 | 65,536 |
| [`MaxUnreliablePacketBytes`](#maxunreliablepacketbytes) | 1,000 | 1,000 | 900 |
| [`RateLimitPerSecond`](#ratelimitpersecond) | 0 (off) | 120 | 60 |
| [`RateLimitBurst`](#ratelimitburst) | 0 | 240 | 120 |
| [`MaxQueuedBytes`](#maxqueuedbytes) | 262,144 | 131,072 | 65,536 |
| [`MaxBurstBytes`](#maxburstbytes) | 65,536 | 32,768 | 16,384 |
| [`MaxPendingInvokes`](#maxpendinginvokes) | 256 | 64 | 32 |

The remaining limits have one default regardless of profile: [`ReliableFragmentBytes`](#reliablefragmentbytes) 49,152 · [`MaxInFlightFragments`](#maxinflightfragments) 32 · [`FragmentTimeoutSeconds`](#fragmenttimeoutseconds) 10 · [`ReplayWindowSize`](#replaywindowsize) 128 · [`ReplayStaleSeconds`](#replaystaleseconds) 30 · [`MaxDecodeOperations`](#maxdecodeoperations) 100,000 · [`MaxPayloadDepth`](#maxpayloaddepth) 16 · [`MaxPayloadStringBytes`](#maxpayloadstringbytes) 8,192 · [`MaxTableKeys`](#maxtablekeys) 2,048 · [`MaxQueuedEvents`](#maxqueuedevents) 256 · [`LowPriorityShedding`](#lowpriorityshedding) `true` · [`InvokeTimeoutSeconds`](#invoketimeoutseconds) 0.

## Packet size

### `MaxPacketBytes`

<Spec type="number (bytes)" default="1,048,576 / 262,144 / 65,536 by profile" on="option, event, function, channel" />

The fallback size cap for both remotes. It is used for [`MaxReliablePacketBytes`](#maxreliablepacketbytes) when that is not set, and to cap [`MaxUnreliablePacketBytes`](#maxunreliablepacketbytes).

On receive, a remote call whose buffer is larger than the cap is dropped whole with reason `MaxPacketBytes` before anything is decoded. On send, an outgoing reliable batch over the cap is dropped whole at flush time, before fragmentation, so a batch larger than the cap is never sent.

When you set this option explicitly, or set `MaxPacketBytes` on an endpoint, the generated receive code also checks it per endpoint. That check compares the size of the **whole received packet**, which can hold many batched events, not the size of the one event. Set per-endpoint caps with that in mind.

```cheeto copy
option MaxPacketBytes = 65536
```

<Callout type="info">
`--doctor` warns when the reliable cap is above 1 MiB, and `--strict` fails when either cap is missing or `0`.
</Callout>

### `MaxReliablePacketBytes`

<Spec type="number (bytes)" default={<>same as <code>MaxPacketBytes</code></>} />

Size cap for the reliable remote only. A value of `0` disables the check.

### `MaxUnreliablePacketBytes`

<Spec type="number (bytes)" default={<>the smaller of <code>MaxPacketBytes</code> and 1,000 (900 for Competitive)</>} />

Size cap for the unreliable remote. Unreliable events are sent immediately, one remote call per `Fire`, and an event whose encoded size is over the cap is dropped on the sender with `MaxPacketBytes` instead of being passed to Roblox. Keep it at or below Roblox's limit for `UnreliableRemoteEvent` payloads.

## Rate limiting

### `RateLimitPerSecond`

<Spec type="number (per second)" default="0 / 120 / 60 by profile" on="option, event, function, channel" />

A token bucket that refills at this many tokens per second, per sender. `0` disables it. It is enforced in two places:

1. **Per remote call.** The runtime value (profile default or your option) limits how many reliable or unreliable remote calls one peer can make per second. The reliable and unreliable remotes have separate buckets. Excess calls are dropped whole with `RateLimit`.
2. **Per endpoint.** Only when you set the option explicitly in the schema, or set `RateLimitPerSecond` on the endpoint, is a bucket compiled into that endpoint's receive path. Excess events on that endpoint are dropped with `RateLimit`; other events in the same packet still run.

Both sides enforce it. A client also rate-limits what it receives from the server, so a server that sends many separate unreliable events per second to one player can hit the client's per-call limit. Unreliable events are not batched.

```cheeto copy
option RateLimitPerSecond = 60
option RateLimitBurst = 120
```

### `RateLimitBurst`

<Spec type="number" default={<>0 / 240 / 120 by profile; equal to <code>RateLimitPerSecond</code> when only that is set</>} on="option, event, function, channel" />

Bucket capacity: how many calls can arrive back to back before the per-second rate applies. `0` means "same as `RateLimitPerSecond`".

## Queues

### `MaxQueuedEvents`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>256</code>} on="option, event, function, channel" />

The per-endpoint inbound queue length. Reliable events that arrive before any `On` listener is connected are queued and delivered when one connects; polling events wait in a queue until `Iter` reads them. When the queue is full, further events are dropped with `QueueFull`.

This value is compiled into the endpoints. Security profiles do not change it and `Configure` has no effect on it.

### `MaxQueuedBytes`

<Spec type="number (bytes)" default="262,144 / 131,072 / 65,536 by profile" />

Bytes of outgoing data tracked per peer. When the tracked amount is over this value and [`LowPriorityShedding`](#lowpriorityshedding) is on, newly queued events with `Priority: Cosmetic` or `Priority: Background` are dropped with `Backpressure`. Critical and Gameplay events are never shed. At half of this value the flush step sends the peer's batch immediately.

<Callout type="warning">
The tracked amount is the bytes waiting in the peer's reliable batch: it grows as events are copied in, broadcasts counted per recipient, and resets when the batch is sent. Unreliable sends leave within the step and never add to it.
</Callout>

### `MaxBurstBytes`

<Spec type="number (bytes)" default="65,536 / 32,768 / 16,384 by profile" />

The flush step sends a peer's reliable batch as soon as it reaches this size, instead of waiting for the next frame interval. The budget shrinks by a quarter while the peer's recorded round-trip time is above 250 ms or jitter above 100 ms. Those figures come from [`Transport.UpdateNetworkStats`](/reference/api/transport#updatenetworkstats); the runtime does not measure them itself.

### `LowPriorityShedding`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>true</code>} />

Allows `Backpressure` drops of Cosmetic and Background events when [`MaxQueuedBytes`](#maxqueuedbytes) is exceeded. Set to `false` to never shed.

## Functions

### `MaxPendingInvokes`

<Spec type="number" default="256 / 64 / 32 by profile" on="option, function" />

How many `Invoke` calls can be waiting for a reply at once. Two limits apply: the module-wide runtime value, and a per-function limit taken from the function's `MaxPendingInvokes` field, or this option if set, or 256. Going over either makes `Invoke` raise `More than N calls ... are awaiting a response`.

Independently of this option, invocation ids are one byte, so at most 255 invokes can be outstanding per module.

### `InvokeTimeoutSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<><code>0</code> (wait forever)</>} on="option, function" />

How long `Invoke` waits for a reply before it raises `Invoke timed out after N seconds.` `0` waits forever. Timeouts are checked by the flush step, so with [`ManualReplication`](/reference/options/runtime#manualreplication) they only fire when you call `StepReplication`.

<Callout type="warning">
Applies to every function without its own [`InvokeTimeoutSeconds`](/reference/fields#invoketimeoutseconds) field. It is read when `Invoke` is called, so the profile default (10 s for Production, 5 s for Competitive, none for Development), the value written in the schema, and later changes through [`Configure`](/reference/api/module#configure) all take effect.
</Callout>

```cheeto copy
option InvokeTimeoutSeconds = 10
```

## Fragmentation

### `ReliableFragmentBytes`

<Spec type="number (bytes)" default={<code>49152</code>} />

An outgoing reliable batch larger than this is split into fragments of at most this many bytes, each sent as its own remote call and reassembled on the other side. `0` disables fragmentation. Fragmentation happens after the [`MaxReliablePacketBytes`](#maxreliablepacketbytes) check, so it cannot be used to send a batch larger than that cap.

### `MaxInFlightFragments`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>32</code>} />

How many partially received fragmented packets one sender may have at once. A fragment that would start another reassembly is dropped with `FragmentOverflow`. `0` means no limit.

### `FragmentTimeoutSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<code>10</code>} />

A reassembly that has not completed within this time is discarded and reported as `FragmentTimeout`.

## Replay protection

### `ReplayWindowSize`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>128</code>} />

Only applies to packets that carry a sequence number, which means events sent with [`Predict`](/reference/api/event#predict). For those, a sequence number seen before is dropped with `ReplayDuplicate`, and one at least this far behind the highest seen is dropped with `ReplayStale`. Tracked per sender and per event.

<Callout type="warning">
Events sent with `Fire` carry no sequence number, so this option has no effect on them. Use [`CooldownSeconds`](/reference/fields#cooldownseconds) to limit repeats of an unsequenced action.
</Callout>

### `ReplayStaleSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<code>30</code>} />

How long a seen sequence number is remembered before it may be reused. Same precondition as [`ReplayWindowSize`](#replaywindowsize).

## Decode budgets

After a payload is decoded and before any listener runs, the runtime walks the decoded value. These options bound that walk. Violations are dropped with `Canonicalization` or `DecodeBudget`. They apply to every endpoint on both sides, including data the server sends to clients.

### `MaxDecodeOperations`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>100000</code>} />

Maximum number of values visited in one payload. Exceeding it drops the event with `DecodeBudget`.

### `MaxPayloadDepth`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>16</code>} />

Maximum table nesting depth. Deeper payloads are dropped with `Canonicalization`.

### `MaxPayloadStringBytes`

<Spec type="number (bytes)" default={<code>8192</code>} />

Maximum length of any single string in a payload. This applies even when the schema type allows longer strings, so a `string` longer than 8 KB is dropped unless you raise this option.

### `MaxTableKeys`

<Spec type="number" default={<code>2048</code>} />

Maximum number of keys in any single table in a payload, including arrays. Larger tables are dropped with `Canonicalization`. Raise it together with array and map bounds you declare.

```

---
title: "Output and modules"
description: "Options that decide which files Cheeto writes, where, and how the generated modules name things."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Spec } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Output and modules

These options are read by the compiler only. Changing them requires recompiling.

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`Casing`](#casing) | identifier | `Pascal` |
| [`ClientOutput`](#clientoutput) | string | required |
| [`ServerOutput`](#serveroutput) | string | required |
| [`TypesOutput`](#typesoutput) | string | not written |
| [`Typescript`](#typescript) | boolean | `false` |
| [`RuntimeOutput`](#runtimeoutput) | string | runtime inlined |
| [`RuntimeRequire`](#runtimerequire) | string | none |
| [`RemoteScope`](#remotescope) | string | none |
| [`FutureLibrary`](#futurelibrary) | string | none |
| [`PromiseLibrary`](#promiselibrary) | string | none |
| [`UseColon`](#usecolon) | boolean | no effect |

## `Casing`

<Spec type="identifier" default={<code>Pascal</code>} values={<><code>Pascal</code>, <code>Camel</code>, <code>Snake</code></>} />

Sets the casing of the methods generated on each endpoint. Namespaces on the module root, such as `Security` or `Transport`, are not affected.

| Method | `Pascal` | `Camel` | `Snake` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fire | `Fire` | `fire` | `fire` |
| FireAll | `FireAll` | `fireAll` | `fire_all` |
| FireList | `FireList` | `fireList` | `fire_list` |
| FireExcept | `FireExcept` | `fireExcept` | `fire_except` |
| FireGroup | `FireGroup` | `fireGroup` | `fire_group` |
| On | `On` | `on` | `on` |
| Invoke | `Invoke` | `invoke` | `invoke` |
| Predict | `Predict` | `predict` | `predict` |
| Iter / Next | `Iter` / `Next` | `iter` / `next` | `iter` / `next` |
| StepReplication | `StepReplication` | `stepReplication` | `step_replication` |
| Read / Write (exports) | `Read` / `Write` | `read` / `write` | `read` / `write` |

```cheeto copy
option Casing = Camel
```

## `ClientOutput`

<Spec type="string (path)" default="required" />

Path of the client module, relative to the schema file. The `.luau` extension is added if you leave it out. The compiler stops with `A client output path must be defined.` when this is missing. Missing directories are created after a prompt, or silently with `--yes`.

In the [Studio plugin](/getting-started/studio-plugin) the path is relative to the instance you generate into, so `"Network/Client.luau"` writes a ModuleScript named `Client` inside a folder named `Network`.

```cheeto copy
option ClientOutput = "src/shared/Network/Client.luau"
```

<Callout type="warning">
[`--strict`](/reference/cli#--strict) rejects output paths that contain `..` or are absolute.
</Callout>

## `ServerOutput`

<Spec type="string (path)" default="required" />

Path of the server module. Same rules as [`ClientOutput`](#clientoutput). The server module errors if required from a client, and the client module errors if required from the server.

```cheeto copy
option ServerOutput = "src/shared/Network/Server.luau"
```

<Callout type="info">
The server module creates the RemoteEvents when it is first required. Place it where both sides can reach its RemoteEvents, and require it from a server Script before clients need the network.
</Callout>

## `TypesOutput`

<Spec type="string (path)" default="not written" />

Writes a third, shared module that exports the Luau types declared in the schema, so code that runs on neither side (shared libraries, tests) can reference them without requiring a networking module.

```cheeto copy
option TypesOutput = "src/shared/Network/Types.luau"
```

## `Typescript`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} />

Also writes `.d.ts` declaration files next to the client and server outputs, for [roblox-ts](https://roblox-ts.com) projects. A module named `init` gets `index.d.ts`.

```cheeto copy
option Typescript = true
```

The declaration files describe every event (including `Predict` and `FireGroup`), function (with `Promise` and `Future` results), channel and declared type, and the runtime namespaces (`Security`, `Transport`, `Protocol` and the rest). Every declaration is exported, and the output type-checks under `tsc --strict` against the roblox-ts globals. With [`UseColon`](#usecolon), endpoint members are declared as methods.

## `RuntimeOutput`

<Spec type="string (path)" default="runtime inlined into each module" />

By default every generated module contains its own copy of the runtime, about 135 KB. With `RuntimeOutput` set, the runtime is written once as a separate factory module and each generated module requires it instead. Two files are written: the path you give (server runtime) and the same path with `Client` appended to the file name (client runtime).

Use this when a large surface is split across several schemas, or when a module would exceed Studio's 200,000-character script limit. Must be set together with [`RuntimeRequire`](#runtimerequire).

```cheeto copy
option RuntimeOutput = "src/shared/Network/Runtime.luau"
option RuntimeRequire = "script.Parent.Runtime"
```

Each module that requires the shared runtime still keeps its own buffers, listeners and remotes. Only the source is shared.

## `RuntimeRequire`

<Spec type="string (Luau expression)" default="none" />

The expression placed inside `require(...)` in generated modules to reach the runtime written by [`RuntimeOutput`](#runtimeoutput). The client module appends `Client` to it. Compiling with `RuntimeOutput` but no `RuntimeRequire` fails.

```cheeto copy
option RuntimeRequire = "game:GetService('ReplicatedStorage').Network.Runtime"
```

## `RemoteScope`

<Spec type="string" default="none" />

Prefixes the names of the RemoteEvents this schema creates, and the key used to detect duplicate instances. Without it the remotes are `CHEETO_RELIABLE_REMOTE` and `CHEETO_UNRELIABLE_REMOTE`; with `RemoteScope = "PACKAGE"` they become `PACKAGE_CHEETO_RELIABLE_REMOTE` and `PACKAGE_CHEETO_UNRELIABLE_REMOTE`.

Requiring two generated modules with the same scope on one side raises `An instance of Cheeto is already running with the remote scope ...`. Give every schema in a place its own scope, which is required when a package ships its own Cheeto network alongside the game's.

```cheeto copy
option RemoteScope = "INVENTORY"
```

## `FutureLibrary`

<Spec type="string (Luau expression)" default="none" />

Required when any function uses `Yield: Future`. The value is placed inside `require(...)` at the top of both modules, so it must resolve on both sides. The generated `Invoke` returns `Future.Try(...)`, so the library must provide `Future.Try`, as [red-blox's Future](https://github.com/red-blox/Util/tree/main/libs/Future) does.

```cheeto copy
option FutureLibrary = "ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Future"
```

## `PromiseLibrary`

<Spec type="string (Luau expression)" default="none" />

Required when any function uses `Yield: Promise`. Same rules as [`FutureLibrary`](#futurelibrary). [evaera's Promise](https://eryn.io/roblox-lua-promise/) and compatible forks work.

```cheeto copy
option PromiseLibrary = "ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Promise"
```

## `UseColon`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} />

Makes every endpoint method accept the endpoint table as its first argument, so you call them with `:`. The generated methods ignore that argument. The runtime namespaces (`Security`, `Transport` and the rest) are unaffected and still use `.`.

```cheeto copy
option UseColon = true
```

```lua copy
Network.Damage:Fire(target, 25)
Network.Damage:On(function(player, target, amount) end)
local stock = Network.GetShopStock:Invoke()
```

```

```mdx
---
title: "All options"
description: "Every option a Cheeto schema accepts, with its type and the page that documents it."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Options

Options configure the compiler and the generated runtime. They go at the top of the schema, before any declaration, one per line:

```cheeto copy
option ClientOutput = "Network/Client.luau"
option ServerOutput = "Network/Server.luau"
option SecurityProfile = Production
```

An unknown option name is a compile error that lists the valid names. A value of the wrong kind, such as a string where a number is expected, is also a compile error.

## Compile time and runtime

Most options become fields of the generated module's `RuntimeConfig` table. Those can also be changed while the game runs with [`Network.Configure`](/reference/api/module#configure):

```lua copy
Network.Configure({ RateLimitPerSecond = 30, EnableHoneypots = false })
```

A few options only affect what code is generated and cannot be changed at runtime. Each entry states which kind it is.

<Callout type="warning">
Some defaults depend on [`SecurityProfile`](/reference/options/security#securityprofile) and [`SecurityPreset`](/reference/options/security#securitypreset). Entries list the default for each profile where they differ.
</Callout>

`docs/pages/reference/options/remote-hardening.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Remote hardening options"
description: "Randomized RemoteEvent names and decoy remotes."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Spec } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Remote hardening options

See [Remote names and decoys](/security/remote-hardening) for what these protect against and what they do not.

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`EnableRemoteNameRotation`](#enableremotenamerotation) | boolean | `false` (`true` under `Maximum`) |
| [`RemoteNameRotationSeconds`](#remotenamerotationseconds) | number | `45` |
| [`EnableRemoteDecoys`](#enableremotedecoys) | boolean | `false` (`true` under `Maximum`) |
| [`RemoteDecoyCount`](#remotedecoycount) | number | `0` (`8` under `Maximum`) |

These are read when the modules load. Changing them with `Configure` afterwards has no effect on remotes that already exist.

## `EnableRemoteNameRotation`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<><code>false</code> (<code>true</code> under <code>Maximum</code>)</>} />

The server creates its two RemoteEvents inside a folder named `<scope>CHEETO_REMOTE_ROOT` in ReplicatedStorage, gives them random names such as `_CHEETO_R_3f9a...`, and publishes the current names as the folder's `ReliableName` and `UnreliableName` attributes. Clients look the remotes up through those attributes and rebind when they change. Without rotation the remotes are `CHEETO_RELIABLE_REMOTE` and `CHEETO_UNRELIABLE_REMOTE` directly in ReplicatedStorage.

Both the server and the client must be compiled with the same value.

## `RemoteNameRotationSeconds`

<Spec type="number (seconds)" default={<code>45</code>} />

How often the server renames the remotes while rotation is on. `0` keeps the initial random names without renaming.

## `EnableRemoteDecoys`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<><code>false</code> (<code>true</code> under <code>Maximum</code>)</>} />

Creates extra RemoteEvents next to the real ones. Game code never fires them, so a `FireServer` on any decoy is reported as `RemoteDecoy` with weight 100 and kicks the player when [`ClientShieldKick`](/reference/options/client-shield#clientshieldkick) is on.

Decoys are created in the rotation folder when rotation is on, or directly in ReplicatedStorage when it is off. Their names follow the pattern `_CHEETO_D<n>_<random>`.

## `RemoteDecoyCount`

<Spec type="number" default={<><code>0</code> (<code>8</code> under <code>Maximum</code>)</>} />

How many decoy remotes to create.

```
