import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Spec } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Runtime features

| Option | Type | Default | Changeable at runtime |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`UsePolling`](#usepolling) | boolean | `false` | No |
| [`ManualReplication`](#manualreplication) | boolean | `false` | No |
| [`SyncValidation`](#syncvalidation) | boolean | `true` in `Development`, else `false` | No |
| [`WriteValidations`](#writevalidations) | boolean | `false` | No |
| [`ExposeMetrics`](#exposemetrics) | boolean | `true` | Yes |
| [`EnableMiddleware`](#enablemiddleware) | boolean | `true` | Yes |
| [`EnablePrediction`](#enableprediction) | boolean | `true` | Partly |
| [`EnableStateChannels`](#enablestatechannels) | boolean | `true` | Yes |
| [`EnableReplicationAdapters`](#enablereplicationadapters) | boolean | `true` | Yes |
| [`EnableMicroProfiler`](#enablemicroprofiler) | boolean | `true` | Yes |
| [`UseEmptyInstanceOptimization`](#useemptyinstanceoptimization) | boolean | `true` | Yes |
| [`BatchUnreliable`](#batchunreliable) | boolean | `true` | Yes |

## `UsePolling`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} />

Generates every event with the polling API on its receiving side, as if each declared `Call: Polling`. Received events are queued and read with [`Iter`](/reference/api/event#iter) instead of delivered to `On` listeners.

```cheeto copy
option UsePolling = true
```

## `ManualReplication`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} />

By default the module connects its flush step to `RunService.Heartbeat`, so queued reliable events are sent once per frame. With `ManualReplication = true` nothing is connected and you call [`StepReplication`](/reference/api/module#stepreplication) yourself. The flush step also expires timed-out invokes and runs the integrity samplers, so it must be called regularly.

```cheeto copy
option ManualReplication = true
```

```lua copy
RunService.PostSimulation:Connect(Network.StepReplication)
```

## `SyncValidation`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<><code>true</code> in the <code>Development</code> profile, <code>false</code> in <code>Production</code> and <code>Competitive</code></>} />

For events with `Call: SingleSync` or `ManySync`, warns when a listener yields: `Yielded in a Sync call. Event "X" uses a Sync call, consider using an Async call instead.` The check only reports; it never closes the yielded thread. It costs a coroutine check per Sync dispatch, so it is a development aid: [`--strict`](/reference/cli#--strict) rejects it, and the production profiles leave it off.

## `WriteValidations`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} />

Type-checks values on the sending side before they are serialized: primitives, instance classes and the shape of arrays, maps, sets and structs. A mismatch raises an error at the `Fire` or `Invoke` call site instead of producing a malformed packet. Useful while developing; it costs time on every send, and `--strict` rejects it.

## `ExposeMetrics`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>true</code>} />

When `false`, [`Stats`](/reference/api/module#stats), [`Report`](/reference/api/module#report) and the [Inspector](/reference/api/inspector) error with `Metrics are disabled`. Counters are still collected internally.

## `EnableMiddleware`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>true</code>} />

When `false`, no [middleware hook](/reference/api/hooks) runs, including `Validate`, `Violation` and `Telemetry`. `Security.OnViolation` callbacks are hooks, so they stop firing too. Auth rules and policies are not hooks and keep working.

## `EnablePrediction`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>true</code>} />

At compile time, `false` stops `Predict` from being generated on client-origin events unless the event sets `Predict: true`. At runtime, `false` makes [`Prediction.Begin`](/reference/api/prediction#begin) and any generated `Predict` error with `Prediction helpers are disabled`.

## `EnableStateChannels`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>true</code>} />

Gates the local [`State.DefineChannel`](/reference/api/state#definechannel) helper, which errors when this is `false`. Schema-declared [`channel`](/reference/declarations/channel) endpoints are not affected.

## `EnableReplicationAdapters`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>true</code>} />

When `false`, [`Replication.MessagingService`](/reference/api/replication#messagingservice) and [`Replication.MemoryStore`](/reference/api/replication#memorystore) error instead of returning an adapter.

## `EnableMicroProfiler`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>true</code>} />

Wraps decoding and flushing in `debug.profilebegin` labels (`Cheeto.Decode.Reliable`, `Cheeto.Decode.Unreliable`, `Cheeto.Flush.Server`, `Cheeto.Flush.Client`) so they show up in the MicroProfiler.

## `UseEmptyInstanceOptimization`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>true</code>} />

When a packet carries no Instances, sends `nil` instead of an empty table as the second remote argument, saving a few bytes per packet.

## `BatchUnreliable`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>true</code>} />

Unreliable events for the same recipient are collected during the frame and sent together in one remote call at the replication step, in batches of at most [`MaxUnreliablePacketBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxunreliablepacketbytes). With `false`, every unreliable send is its own remote call, sent immediately.

Batching cuts the number of remote calls, which also keeps high-frequency unreliable traffic under the receiver's per-call [rate limit](/reference/options/limits#ratelimitpersecond). The cost is up to one frame of added delay, the same delay reliable events already have. If a batch is lost, every event in it is lost, which is what unreliable delivery allows.

```

`docs/pages/reference/options/security.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Security options"
description: "SecurityProfile, SecurityPreset, RequirePolicies, StrictProduction and EnableHoneypots."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Spec } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Security options

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`SecurityProfile`](#securityprofile) | identifier | `Development` (`Competitive` under `Maximum`) |
| [`SecurityPreset`](#securitypreset) | identifier | none |
| [`RequirePolicies`](#requirepolicies) | boolean | `false` (`true` under `Maximum`) |
| [`StrictProduction`](#strictproduction) | boolean | `false` |
| [`EnableHoneypots`](#enablehoneypots) | boolean | `true` |

The shield, integrity and remote-hardening options have their own pages: [Client shield](/reference/options/client-shield), [Client integrity](/reference/options/client-integrity), [Character integrity](/reference/options/character-integrity), [Remote hardening](/reference/options/remote-hardening).

## `SecurityProfile`

<Spec type="identifier" default={<><code>Development</code>, or <code>Competitive</code> when <code>SecurityPreset = Maximum</code></>} values={<><code>Development</code>, <code>Production</code>, <code>Competitive</code></>} />

Chooses the default [transport limits](/reference/options/limits). Any limit you set explicitly overrides the profile.

| Limit | Development | Production | Competitive |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MaxPacketBytes` | 1,048,576 | 262,144 | 65,536 |
| `MaxUnreliablePacketBytes` | 1,000 | 1,000 | 900 |
| `RateLimitPerSecond` / `RateLimitBurst` | off | 120 / 240 | 60 / 120 |
| `MaxQueuedBytes` | 262,144 | 131,072 | 65,536 |
| `MaxBurstBytes` | 65,536 | 32,768 | 16,384 |
| `MaxPendingInvokes` | 256 | 64 | 32 |

The profile also matters elsewhere:

- With any profile other than `Development`, captures drop raw buffers when [`NoRawCaptureInProduction`](/reference/options/diagnostics#norawcaptureinproduction) is on.
- [`--strict`](/reference/cli#--strict) and [`--hardening-checklist`](/reference/cli#--hardening-checklist) require `Production` or `Competitive`.
- [`--doctor`](/reference/cli#--doctor) warns when rate limiting is off outside `Development`.

An unrecognised value is accepted and uses the `Development` limits.

```cheeto copy
option SecurityProfile = Production
```

## `SecurityPreset`

<Spec type="identifier" default="none" values={<><code>Maximum</code></>} />

`Maximum` switches every protection on in one line by changing these defaults. Anything you set explicitly still wins.

| Option | Default | Under `Maximum` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SecurityProfile` | `Development` | `Competitive` |
| `RequirePolicies` | `false` | `true` |
| `EnableClientShield` | `false` | `true` |
| `ClientShieldStrict` | `false` | `true` |
| `ClientShieldKick` | `false` | `true` |
| `EnableClientIntegrity` | `false` | `true` |
| `EnableCharacterIntegrity` | `false` | `true` |
| `CharacterIntegrityMode` | `Observe` | `Correct` |
| `EnableRemoteNameRotation` | `false` | `true` |
| `EnableRemoteDecoys` | `false` | `true` |
| `RemoteDecoyCount` | `0` | `8` |

`CharacterIntegrityKick` stays `false` under `Maximum`. Any other value of `SecurityPreset` behaves as no preset.

```cheeto copy
option SecurityPreset = Maximum
```

<Callout type="warning">
`ClientShieldStrict` and `ClientShieldKick` under `Maximum` mean a single client-shield detection kicks the player. Read [Client shield](/security/client-shield) and roll out with kicks off first.
</Callout>

## `RequirePolicies`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<><code>false</code> (<code>true</code> under <code>Maximum</code>)</>} />

Makes every endpoint the server receives from clients require a [`Policy`](/reference/fields#policy). A client-sent event or function call on an endpoint without one is dropped with `PolicyRejected`.

<Callout type="warning">
Any of `Policy`, `PolicyGroup` or `Auth` satisfies it, the same rule `--doctor` and `--strict` apply. Endpoints with none of them are dropped with `PolicyRejected`.
</Callout>

```cheeto copy
option RequirePolicies = true
```

## `StrictProduction`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>false</code>} />

Runs the [`--strict`](/reference/cli#--strict) checks every time the schema is compiled and stops compilation if any fail. Use it in the schema you ship so a production build cannot be produced with unsafe settings.

```cheeto copy
option StrictProduction = true
option SecurityProfile = Production
option SyncValidation = false
```

## `EnableHoneypots`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>true</code>} />

Master switch for [honeypot endpoints](/security/honeypots). When `false`, traffic on endpoints marked `Honeypot: true` is no longer dropped and goes through the normal checks like any other endpoint. Can be changed at runtime with `Configure({ EnableHoneypots = false })`.

```

`docs/pages/reference/options/versioning.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Versioning"
description: "Schema version options, the schema fingerprint and the handshake that enforces it."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'
import { Spec } from '../../../components/Reference'

# Versioning

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`Version`](#version) | number | `1` |
| [`SchemaVersion`](#schemaversion) | number | `1` |
| [`MinimumSchemaVersion`](#minimumschemaversion) | number | `1` |
| [`EnableProtocolHandshake`](#enableprotocolhandshake) | boolean | `true` |
| [`IncompatiblePeerAction`](#incompatiblepeeraction) | `Drop` \| `Kick` | `Drop`, or `Kick` with `SecurityPreset = Maximum` |

For how these fit together, see [Schema versioning](/concepts/schema-versioning).

## The schema fingerprint

Every build carries a fingerprint of its wire layout, a 16-digit hex string in [`Schema.Hash`](/reference/api/schema#hash) and `cheeto.lock`. It is computed from each endpoint's name, kind, channel, wire id, deprecated id, payload type (including ranges, components and field names) and delivery mode, plus the encoding options. Two builds with the same fingerprint encode every endpoint identically. Whitespace, comments, declaration order that does not change ids, and options that do not touch the wire leave it unchanged.

## `Version`

<Spec type="number (0–65535)" default={<code>1</code>} />

A version number you choose for this schema. It is sent in the handshake, stamped on captures and state, and written to `cheeto.lock`, and compared against the peer's [`MinimumSchemaVersion`](#minimumschemaversion). It is separate from the fingerprint: you do not need to raise it for the handshake to notice a wire change, but raising it gives you a readable number in logs.

```cheeto copy
option Version = 7
```

## `SchemaVersion`

<Spec type="number (0–65535)" default={<code>1</code>} />

Alias of [`Version`](#version). When both are set, `SchemaVersion` wins.

## `MinimumSchemaVersion`

<Spec type="number (0–65535)" default={<code>1</code>} />

The oldest schema version this build accepts in a peer's handshake. A peer with a lower version is incompatible even when its fingerprint matches.

```cheeto copy
option Version = 7
option MinimumSchemaVersion = 7
```

## `EnableProtocolHandshake`

<Spec type="boolean" default={<code>true</code>} />

Each side writes a small frame with its schema version, minimum version and fingerprint: the client into its first batch, the server into the first batch of every player. The receiver records the peer in [`Protocol.Peers`](/reference/api/protocol#peers) and [`Protocol.Info`](/reference/api/protocol#info) and compares the fingerprint with its own.

When they differ on the server, the frame is dropped with `IncompatibleProtocol`, and every later packet from that player is dropped before decoding, because it would be read against the wrong layout. What else happens is set by [`IncompatiblePeerAction`](#incompatiblepeeraction). A client that receives a different fingerprint from the server warns in its output; the server decides who stays.

## `IncompatiblePeerAction`

<Spec type="identifier" default={<><code>Drop</code>, or <code>Kick</code> with <code>SecurityPreset = Maximum</code></>} values={<><code>Drop</code>, <code>Kick</code></>} />

What the server does with a player whose handshake names another schema:

| Value | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `Drop` | The player stays in the game; its packets are dropped and reported with `IncompatibleProtocol`. |
| `Kick` | As `Drop`, and the player is kicked with a message asking them to rejoin. |

In Roblox, clients and servers of one place version normally run the same module, so a mismatch usually means a modified client or a stale server during an update.

```cheeto copy
option IncompatiblePeerAction = Kick
```

## Removed options

These options fail compilation with the error `Option "…" was removed`. Cheeto has a single wire protocol, so there is nothing to choose; delete the line.

| Option |
| --- |
| `ProtocolVersion` |
| `ProtocolMode` |
| `AcceptProtocolVersion1` |

`Configure` rejects them as unknown runtime options.

```

`docs/pages/reference/syntax.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Syntax"
description: "How a .cheeto file is laid out, and the lexical rules shared by every declaration."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Syntax

A schema is a plain-text file with the `.cheeto` extension. The compiler also accepts `.txt`. It has two parts, in this order:

1. **Options**, one `option Name = Value` per line. Options must come first; an `option` after the first declaration is a parse error.
2. **Declarations**: `import`, `scope`, `type`, `struct`, `enum`, `map`, `set`, `event`, `function` and `channel`, in any order.

```cheeto copy filename="network.cheeto"
-- Options come first
option ClientOutput = "Network/Client.luau"
option ServerOutput = "Network/Server.luau"

-- Then declarations
import "./Shared"

struct Hit {
    Target: Instance(Player),
    Damage: u16(0..500)
}

event DealDamage {
    From: Client,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Policy: "damage",
    Data: Hit
}
```

## Comments

Comments use Luau syntax.

```cheeto
-- A line comment
--[[ A block comment ]]
--[==[ A block comment that may contain ]] ]==]
```

## Identifiers

Names start with a letter or underscore and continue with letters, digits or underscores: `DealDamage`, `_internal`, `Hit2`. Names are case-sensitive. Referring to something inside a scope or import uses a dot: `Shared.Hit`.

These words are reserved and cannot be used as names: `event`, `function`, `channel`, `type`, `struct`, `enum`, `map`, `set`, `scope`, `option`, `export`, `import`, `as`, `true`, `false`, and every primitive type name such as `u8` or `string`.

## Values

| Kind | Written as | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| String | `"Network/Client.luau"` or `'...'` | Output paths, `Policy`, `Auth`, library paths |
| Number | `20`, `0.25`, `-5` | Limits, rates, ranges |
| Boolean | `true`, `false` | Toggles |
| Identifier | `Reliable`, `Pascal`, `Maximum` | Enumerated values such as `Type`, `Casing`, `SecurityPreset` |

## Declaration blocks

`event`, `function`, `channel` and `struct` use a brace block of `Field: Value` pairs separated by commas. A trailing comma is allowed.

```cheeto
event Announce {
    From: Server,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: ManyAsync,
    Data: string(0..128),
}
```

`type`, `map` and `enum` (unit form) use `=`:

```cheeto
type Health = u8(0..100)
map Scores = { [string]: u32 }
enum Team = { Red, Blue }
```

## Ranges

A range in parentheses bounds a number's value, or the length of a string, buffer or map, or the magnitude of a vector. In square brackets it bounds an array's length. See [Ranges](/reference/types/ranges).

```cheeto
u8(0..100)       -- value between 0 and 100
string(3..20)    -- 3 to 20 bytes long
Item[..50]       -- at most 50 elements
```

## Type modifiers

Modifiers are written after the type. A class or encoding comes first, then a range, then any sequence of `[]` and `?`, which apply from left to right.

```cheeto
Instance(Player)      -- class
vector<i16>(0..512)   -- encoding, then range
u8[1..10]?            -- an optional array of u8
u8?[1..10]            -- an array of optional u8
```

## Generics

`struct`, `map` and tagged `enum` declarations can take type parameters in angle brackets:

```cheeto
struct Page<T> {
    Items: T[..50],
    Cursor: u32?
}

event PlayerList {
    From: Server,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: ManyAsync,
    Data: Page<Instance(Player)>
}
```

<Callout type="info">
Generic parameters are resolved at compile time. The generated Luau contains one concrete serializer per use.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/types/arrays.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Arrays"
description: "Lists of one element type, with optional length bounds."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Arrays

Square brackets after a type make an array of it:

```cheeto copy
type Tags = string(1..16)[]
type Party = f64[1..4]
type Grid = u8[..16][..16]

struct Item {
    Id: u16,
    Count: u8
}

struct Inventory {
    Items: Item[..64]
}
```

- A range inside the brackets bounds the element count. A received array outside it drops the event with `MalformedPacket`.
- `[N]` is an exact length and writes no length prefix.
- Arrays can nest: `u8[..16][..16]` is an array of up to 16 arrays of up to 16 bytes.

Arrays are sent as a length followed by each element, so they must be proper Luau arrays: keys `1` to `n` with no holes.

<Callout type="warning">
The runtime drops any received table with more than [`MaxTableKeys`](/reference/options/limits#maxtablekeys) entries (2,048 by default) with `Canonicalization`, whatever the declared bound. Raise that option for larger arrays.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/types/booleans.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "boolean"
description: "true or false, packed into single bits."
---

# boolean

```cheeto copy
type Success = boolean
```

With [`UseBitPacking`](/reference/options/encoding#usebitpacking) on (the default), booleans take one bit each and share bytes with other booleans and optional flags in the same event. With it off, each takes a byte.

```

`docs/pages/reference/types/buffers.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "buffer"
description: "Raw bytes for custom serialization."
---

# buffer

A `buffer` carries raw bytes you serialized yourself, while still being batched and validated like everything else.

```cheeto copy
type Blob = buffer
type Chunk = buffer(..900)
type Hash = buffer(32)
```

The length prefix works like [`string`](/reference/types/strings): a range bounds the byte length, and an exact range removes the prefix. Unbounded buffers are limited to 65,535 bytes.

Pair it with [`export`](/reference/declarations/export) to send a value you encoded with a Cheeto type's `Write` function.

```

`docs/pages/reference/types/cframes.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "CFrame"
description: "Position and rotation, with configurable encoding."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# CFrame

```cheeto copy
type Pose = CFrame
type CompactPose = CFrame<f16>
```

A `CFrame` is written as its position (three numbers) followed by its orientation as the Euler angles from `CFrame:ToOrientation()` (three numbers). By default all six are `f32`, 24 bytes in total.

## Encoding

`CFrame<T>` uses `T` for all six numbers. `CFrame<A, B>` uses **`B` for the position and `A` for the rotation**:

| Declaration | Position | Rotation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CFrame` | `f32` | `f32` |
| `CFrame<f16>` | `f16` | `f16` |
| `CFrame<f32, i16>` | `i16` | `f32` |

<Callout type="error">
The two-parameter form is `CFrame<Position, Rotation>`: `CFrame<i16, f16>` sends a whole-number position and a half-precision rotation. With one parameter, both use it.
</Callout>

The received CFrame is rebuilt with `CFrame.new(position) * CFrame.fromOrientation(x, y, z)`. Positions more than 10⁹ studs from the origin, and non-finite values, are dropped with `Canonicalization`.

```

`docs/pages/reference/types/instances.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Instance"
description: "Send references to Roblox instances, optionally restricted to a class."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Instance

```cheeto copy
type AnyInstance = Instance
type Target = Instance(Player)
type Part = Instance(BasePart)?
```

Instances cannot go into a buffer. Cheeto sends them in a list beside the buffer, as the second argument of the remote call, and Roblox replicates the references. They cost nothing in the buffer itself.

## Class

`Instance(ClassName)` checks the received value with `IsA`, so subclasses are accepted: `Instance(BasePart)` accepts a `Part` or a `MeshPart`. A value of the wrong class drops the event with `MalformedPacket`.

## When an instance arrives as nil

An instance can be `nil` on the receiving side even though it existed on the sender: it may not have streamed in yet, exist only on the server, or have been destroyed in between. A non-optional `Instance` that arrives as `nil` fails validation, and the event is dropped with `MalformedPacket`. Other events in the same packet are unaffected.

<Callout type="warning">
Mark any instance that might be missing on the receiver as optional: `Instance(Model)?`. Streaming-enabled places especially.
</Callout>

## Security

A client can send any instance it can see. Never treat a received instance as proof of ownership or permission. For objects a client acts on, such as build pieces, inventory items or trade sessions, send a server-issued [handle](/security/handles-and-capabilities) instead and resolve it on the server.

```

`docs/pages/reference/types/numbers.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Numbers"
description: "Unsigned integers, signed integers and floating point numbers."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Numbers

Number types are a letter for the kind (`u` unsigned, `i` signed, `f` floating point) followed by the bit width. Every number is a Luau `number` in code.

## Integers

| Type | Range | Fixed size | Varint size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `u8` | 0 to 255 | 1 byte | 1 byte (never varint) |
| `u16` | 0 to 65,535 | 2 bytes | 1 to 3 bytes |
| `u32` | 0 to 4,294,967,295 | 4 bytes | 1 to 5 bytes |
| `i8` | −128 to 127 | 1 byte | 1 byte (never varint) |
| `i16` | −32,768 to 32,767 | 2 bytes | 1 to 3 bytes |
| `i32` | −2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647 | 4 bytes | 1 to 5 bytes |

With [`UseVarints`](/reference/options/encoding#usevarints) on (the default), 16 and 32-bit integers are variable length: values below 128 take one byte, below 16,384 two bytes. Signed values are zig-zag encoded, so −1 is as cheap as 1.

## Floating point

| Type | Size | Exact integers up to | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `f16` | 2 bytes | ±2,048 | Largest value ±65,504; slower to encode |
| `f32` | 4 bytes | ±16,777,216 | Same precision as a Roblox `Vector3` component |
| `f64` | 8 bytes | ±9,007,199,254,740,992 | Luau's native number |

Values beyond the `f16` range are written as infinity. NaN and infinities are rejected when received: the runtime's payload check drops non-finite numbers with `Canonicalization`.

## Bounding

```cheeto copy
type Health = u8(0..100)
type Damage = u16(..500)
type Temperature = f32(-50..60)
```

A received value outside the range drops the event with `MalformedPacket`. See [Ranges](/reference/types/ranges).

<Callout type="warning">
An integer outside its type's range raises an error at the call site instead of being sent: `Fire(300)` on a `u8` raises `u8 must be between 0 and 255, got 300`, and nothing is written into the batch. Fractions are truncated: `2.7` arrives as `2`. Declare a range (`u8(0..100)`) to narrow the accepted values further; the receiver drops anything outside it, and [`WriteValidations`](/reference/options/runtime#writevalidations) checks ranges at the call site too.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/types/optionals.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Optionals"
description: "Allow a value to be nil."
---

# Optionals

Append `?` to allow `nil`:

```cheeto copy
type Nickname = string(3..20)?
type Target = Instance(Model)?

struct Profile {
    Name: string(1..32),
    Title: string(0..32)?
}
```

An optional costs one presence bit, packed with other booleans when [`UseBitPacking`](/reference/options/encoding#usebitpacking) is on, plus the value when present.

`?` applies to everything to its left, and array brackets after it make an array of optionals:

| Declaration | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `u8[..10]?` | An array of `u8`, or `nil` |
| `u8?[..10]` | An array whose elements are `u8` or `nil` |

`unknown` cannot be made optional; it already accepts `nil`.

```

`docs/pages/reference/types/ranges.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Ranges"
description: "Bound numbers, lengths and magnitudes with ranges."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Ranges

A range limits a value. Received values outside the range fail validation and the event is dropped with `MalformedPacket` before any listener runs. Sent values are only checked when [`WriteValidations`](/reference/options/runtime#writevalidations) is on.

| Written | Minimum | Maximum |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0..100` | 0 | 100 |
| `0..` | 0 | no limit |
| `..100` | no limit | 100 |
| `36` | 36 | 36 (exact) |

## Where ranges go

| Type | Syntax | Bounds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Numbers | `u8(0..100)` | The value |
| `string` | `string(3..20)` | Length in bytes |
| `buffer` | `buffer(..900)` | Length in bytes |
| `vector` | `vector(0..1)` | Magnitude |
| Arrays | `u8[1..10]` | Number of elements |

```cheeto copy
type Health = u8(0..100)
type Username = string(3..20)
type Uuid = string(36)
type Direction = vector(0..1)
type Party = f64[1..4]
```

## Ranges change the encoding

For strings, buffers and arrays, the upper bound picks the size of the length prefix when [`UseVarints`](/reference/options/encoding#usevarints) is off: 1 byte up to 255, 2 bytes up to 65,535, 4 bytes above. An exact range such as `string(36)` has no prefix at all.

<Callout type="info">
Maps cannot take a range. Bound a collection with an array range instead.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/types/roblox-types.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Other Roblox types"
description: "Wire formats of every other Roblox datatype Cheeto can send."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Other Roblox types

Each of these is written into the buffer with a fixed layout. Sizes assume the default [encoding options](/reference/options/encoding).

| Type | Layout | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Color3` | R, G, B each rounded to 0–255 | 3 bytes |
| `BrickColor` | `BrickColor.Number` as `u16` | 1–3 bytes |
| `DateTime` | `UnixTimestamp` as `f64` | 8 bytes |
| `DateTimeMillis` | `UnixTimestampMillis` as `f64` | 8 bytes |
| `Vector2` | X, Y as `f32`, or the type in `Vector2<T>` | 8 bytes by default |
| `Vector2int16` | X, Y as `i16` | 2–6 bytes |
| `Vector3int16` | X, Y, Z as `i16` | 3–9 bytes |
| `UDim` | Scale `f32`, Offset `i32` | 5–9 bytes |
| `UDim2` | Two `UDim` | 10–18 bytes |
| `Rect` | Min and Max as `Vector2` | 16 bytes |
| `Ray` | Origin and Direction as `vector` | 24 bytes |
| `Region3` | Minimum and maximum corners as `vector` | 24 bytes |
| `NumberRange` | Min, Max as `f32` | 8 bytes |
| `NumberSequence` | Count, then Time, Value, Envelope as `f32` per keypoint | 1–3 + 12 per keypoint |
| `ColorSequence` | Count, then Time `f32` and `Color3` per keypoint | 1–3 + 7 per keypoint |
| `PhysicalProperties` | Density, Friction, Elasticity, FrictionWeight, ElasticityWeight as `f32` | 20 bytes |
| `Axes` | X, Y, Z flags in one byte | 1 byte |
| `Faces` | Six face flags in one byte | 1 byte |
| `EnumItem` | Enum type name and item name as strings | varies |
| `TweenInfo` | Time `f32`, EasingStyle and EasingDirection as `EnumItem`, RepeatCount `i32`, Reverses `boolean`, DelayTime `f32` | varies |
| `Font` | Family as string, Weight and Style as `EnumItem` | varies |

```cheeto copy
struct Appearance {
    Color: Color3,
    Material: EnumItem,
    Size: Vector2<i16>,
    Glow: NumberSequence
}
```

<Callout type="warning">
`Color3` is quantized to 8 bits per channel, the same precision as a hex colour. Channels outside 0–1, such as HDR colours built with `Color3.new(2, 0, 0)`, are clamped to the nearest valid value and rounded to the nearest step.
</Callout>

## EnumItem

`EnumItem` sends any Roblox enum value by name, so it works without declaring anything, but costs two strings. If you always send values from one enum, a schema [`enum`](/reference/declarations/enum) costs one byte:

```cheeto copy
enum Material = { Plastic, Wood, Metal }
```

`docs/pages/reference/types/strings.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "string"
description: "Text values, with optional length bounds."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# string

```cheeto copy
type Message = string
type Username = string(3..20)
type Uuid = string(36)
```

A `string` is written as a length prefix followed by its bytes. A range bounds the length in bytes, not characters; characters outside ASCII take more than one byte.

| Declaration | Prefix |
| --- | --- |
| `string` | Varint, or 2 bytes with varints off (max 65,535 bytes) |
| `string(..255)` | Varint, or 1 byte with varints off |
| `string(36)` | None: always exactly 36 bytes |

With [`UseStringDictionaries`](/reference/options/encoding#usestringdictionaries) on, a string repeated within one batch is sent once and referenced after that.

<Callout type="warning">
The runtime drops any received string longer than [`MaxPayloadStringBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxpayloadstringbytes), 8,192 bytes by default, even when the declared type allows more. Raise that option if you send long text.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/types/unknown.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "unknown"
description: "Values whose shape is only known at runtime, sent with Roblox's own serializer."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# unknown

`unknown` accepts any value Roblox can pass through a RemoteEvent argument: numbers, strings, tables, instances, datatypes, or `nil`.

```cheeto copy
event DebugPayload {
    From: Server,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: ManyAsync,
    Data: unknown
}
```

Cheeto does not encode it. The value travels beside the buffer, like an [Instance](/reference/types/instances), and Roblox serializes it with its usual rules: metatables are dropped, mixed tables lose keys, and functions cannot be sent.

<Callout type="warning">
`unknown` gives up everything Cheeto adds: no size savings, no type checking, and no range validation. The runtime's payload check still applies (depth, key count, string length, non-finite numbers). Avoid it for data clients send; use a [tagged enum](/reference/declarations/enum#tagged-enums) when a value can have several shapes.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/reference/types/vectors.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "vector"
description: "Vector3 values, with configurable component encoding and magnitude bounds."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# vector

`vector` is a Roblox `Vector3`. The schema type is spelled `vector`; `Vector3` is not a valid schema type.

```cheeto copy
type Position = vector
type Direction = vector(0..1)
type GridPosition = vector<i16>
```

## Encoding

By default each component is an `f32`, 12 bytes in total. A number type in angle brackets changes the component encoding:

| Declaration | Size | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vector` | 12 bytes | Exact positions |
| `vector<f16>` | 6 bytes | Directions, small offsets |
| `vector<i16>` | 3 to 9 bytes | Whole-stud grid positions |
| `vector<u8>` | 3 bytes | Small non-negative grids |

<Callout type="warning">
Integer encodings drop the fractional part, and `f16` keeps about three significant digits. Encodings wider than `f32` gain nothing, because Roblox stores `Vector3` components as `f32`.
</Callout>

## Bounding

A range bounds the **magnitude**: `vector(0..1)` accepts only vectors of length 0 to 1, which is how to validate a direction.

## Vector2

`Vector2` accepts an encoding the same way: `Vector2<i16>`. See [Other Roblox types](/reference/types/roblox-types).

`docs/pages/reference/violation-report.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "ViolationReport"
description: "The table passed to Security.OnViolation and the Violation hook."
---

# ViolationReport

Every drop and every security report produces one of these, passed to [`Security.OnViolation`](/reference/api/security#onviolation) callbacks and the [`Violation`](/reference/api/hooks#violation) hook.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Reason` | string | A [drop reason](/reference/drop-reasons), a custom policy reason, or a security report reason |
| `Player` | `Player`, `"Server"` or `nil` | Who sent the offending data. `nil` for some send-side drops |
| `Event` | string | Endpoint name; the channel name for packet-level drops; `$clientShield`, `$clientIntegrity` or `$characterIntegrity` for security reports |
| `Channel` | string | `"Reliable"`, `"Unreliable"`, `"ClientShield"`, `"ClientIntegrity"` or `"CharacterIntegrity"` |
| `Score` | number | The sender's running count for this `Event`, from [`AbuseScores`](/reference/api/security#abusescores) |
| `Action` | string | `"drop"` for drops; `"report"`, `"kick"`, `"correct"` for security reports |
| `PayloadSize` | number | Size of the packet, or the report's weight for security reports |
| `Time` | number | `os.clock()` when it happened |

Field names are PascalCase: `report.Reason`, not `report.reason`.

```lua copy
Network.Security.OnViolation(function(report)
    if typeof(report.Player) ~= "Instance" then
        return
    end
    Analytics.Log("net_violation", {
        userId = report.Player.UserId,
        reason = report.Reason,
        endpoint = report.Event,
        action = report.Action,
    })
end)
```

Some drops are not caused by the peer: `Backpressure` and send-side `MaxPacketBytes` come from your own server. Filter by `Reason` before punishing anyone.
