`docs/pages/security/auth-rules.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Auth rules"
description: "Named yes-or-no checks about the sender, run before decoding."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Auth rules

An auth rule is a function that decides whether a sender may use an endpoint right now. The endpoint names it with [`Auth`](/reference/fields#auth), and you register it with [`UseAuth`](/reference/api/module#useauth).

```cheeto copy
event Respawn {
    From: Client,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Auth: "Dead",
    Policy: "respawn",
    Data: u8
}
```

```lua copy
Network.UseAuth("Dead", function(context)
    local character = context.Source.Character
    local humanoid = character and character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    return humanoid == nil or humanoid.Health <= 0
end)
```

## Behaviour

- The rule receives `{ Name, Source, Channel, Size }` and runs before the payload is decoded.
- It must return exactly `true`. Anything else, including `nil`, drops the event with `AuthRejected`.
- A rule that errors drops the event and is counted in `HookErrors`.
- A name that was never registered drops **every** event on the endpoint and logs one warning.
- Two rules are built in: `AlivePlayer` (the sender is a player still in the game) and `ServerOnly` (the sender is the server).

## Auth rules and policies

Both run before decoding and both can deny. The difference is what they are for:

| | Auth rule | [Policy](/security/policies) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Question | Is this sender in a state to act at all? | May this sender use this endpoint? |
| Receives | Name, source, channel, size | Also the endpoint's constraints, policy group and user id |
| Can give a reason | No | Yes, as the drop reason |
| Satisfies `RequirePolicies` | No | Yes |

Use auth rules for broad, reusable state checks ("alive", "loaded", "not in a cutscene") and policies for per-endpoint permission.

<Callout type="warning">
Introduce an auth rule on a live game in report-only form first: log and return `true`, check the logs, then enforce. A rule that depends on something the client does on join can race the player's first input and silently drop real traffic.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/security/character-integrity.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Character integrity"
description: "Server-side movement checks that score impossible movement and can pull characters back."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Character integrity

Character integrity watches how each character moves, entirely on the server, and scores movement the configured limits cannot explain: teleports, speed hacks, fly hacks, walking through walls. It never trusts a position the client reports; it samples the replicated `HumanoidRootPart`.

Turn it on with [`EnableCharacterIntegrity`](/reference/options/character-integrity#enablecharacterintegrity), or with [`SecurityPreset = Maximum`](/security/maximum-security) (which uses `Correct` mode).

## Sampling

Every [`CharacterIntegritySampleIntervalSeconds`](/reference/options/character-integrity#characterintegritysampleintervalseconds) (0.25 s), for each player, the server compares the root part's position with the previous sample. It allows for:

- the configured speed, or the humanoid's `WalkSpeed` times a multiplier, whichever is higher;
- the assembly's current velocity (for knockback and physics);
- a flat slack distance;
- the player's ping.

Sitting players are skipped. Gaps longer than [`CharacterIntegrityMaxStepSeconds`](/reference/options/character-integrity#characterintegritymaxstepseconds) (server hitches) resynchronize instead of scoring. New characters and joins get a grace period.

| Reason | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `HorizontalDisplacement` | Moved further horizontally than allowed |
| `VerticalDisplacement` | Moved further vertically than allowed |
| `WalkSpeedMutation` | `WalkSpeed` is above the configured maximum times the multiplier |
| `CollidableTraversal` | A raycast along the movement hit a collidable part |
| `NonFiniteMovement` | Position or velocity contained NaN or infinity |

Several reasons in one sample are joined with `+`, for example `HorizontalDisplacement+CollidableTraversal`.

## Modes

[`CharacterIntegrityMode`](/reference/options/character-integrity#characterintegritymode) decides what happens:

| Mode | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `Observe` | Record evidence only; nothing reported |
| `Report` | Also report to `OnViolation` |
| `Correct` | Also move the character back to its last safe position when the score reaches the correction score |
| `Kick` | Also kick, but only with `CharacterIntegrityKick = true`, a high enough score and enough breaches in a row |

The score decays over time, so brief glitches fade.

## Working with your game's movement

Anything your game does to move characters fast must tell the checker, or it will be flagged:

```lua copy
-- Server-initiated teleports: use this instead of PivotTo
Network.Security.TeleportCharacter(player, destination)

-- Launch pads, dashes, knockback, vehicles, cutscenes
Network.Security.GrantMovementGrace(player, 3, "launch-pad")

-- After moving a character yourself
Network.Security.ReconcileCharacter(player)
```

Raise [`CharacterIntegrityMaxHorizontalSpeed`](/reference/options/character-integrity#characterintegritymaxhorizontalspeed) and [`CharacterIntegrityMaxVerticalSpeed`](/reference/options/character-integrity#characterintegritymaxverticalspeed) for games with fast movement, and use [`Security.EvaluateMovement`](/reference/api/security#evaluatemovement) to test your limits against real numbers.

## Rolling out

1. Run in `Observe` and read [`Security.CharacterIntegrity()`](/reference/api/security#characterintegrity) snapshots from real sessions.
2. Fix sources of false positives with grace calls and limits.
3. Move to `Report`, then `Correct`.
4. Only then consider `Kick` with `CharacterIntegrityKick = true`.

<Callout type="warning">
Network ownership means the client controls its character's physics. Character integrity bounds how far that control can go; it does not make movement authoritative. Games that need authoritative movement must simulate it on the server.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/security/client-integrity.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Client integrity"
description: "Server-issued liveness challenges that the client must answer with a receipt."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Client integrity

Client integrity checks that each client's Cheeto runtime is alive and answering. The server regularly sends each player a one-time challenge; the client runs a set of checks and answers with a receipt. Clients that stop answering, send malformed receipts, or report failed checks build up a decaying score.

Turn it on with [`EnableClientIntegrity`](/reference/options/client-integrity#enableclientintegrity), or with [`SecurityPreset = Maximum`](/security/maximum-security).

## The cycle

1. After a join grace period ([`ClientIntegrityJoinGraceSeconds`](/reference/options/client-integrity#clientintegrityjoingraceseconds), 20 s), the server sends a challenge with a fresh id and random nonce every [`ClientIntegrityChallengeIntervalSeconds`](/reference/options/client-integrity#clientintegritychallengeintervalseconds) (4 s). Only one challenge per player is outstanding.
2. The client runs a built-in check that its runtime functions are intact, plus every sampler you registered with [`Security.OnIntegritySample`](/reference/api/security#onintegritysample).
3. The client answers with a receipt: the challenge id and nonce, an increasing completion counter, the number of samplers, whether all passed, and a checksum.
4. The server verifies the receipt.

| Outcome | Evidence | Weight |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No receipt within [`ClientIntegrityReceiptTimeoutSeconds`](/reference/options/client-integrity#clientintegrityreceipttimeoutseconds) (8 s) | `IntegrityReceiptMissing` | 4 |
| Wrong challenge, expired, reused counter, no samplers, or bad checksum | `IntegrityReceiptInvalid` | 6 |
| Valid receipt, but a check failed | `IntegrityEvaluatorFailed` | 6 |
| Valid, healthy receipt | Score reduced by 2, failure streak reset | |

The score decays by 0.5 per second. A kick needs all of: [`ClientShieldKick`](/reference/options/client-shield#clientshieldkick) on, score at least [`ClientIntegrityScoreThreshold`](/reference/options/client-integrity#clientintegrityscorethreshold) (16), and at least [`ClientIntegrityMaxConsecutiveFailures`](/reference/options/client-integrity#clientintegritymaxconsecutivefailures) (4) failures in a row. A single missed receipt never kicks.

## Adding your own checks

Register cheap, deterministic checks that your game's client systems are running:

```lua copy filename="Client"
local remove = Network.Security.OnIntegritySample(function(context)
    return {
        Healthy = Controllers.Started
            and Controllers.Inventory:IsBound()
            and Controllers.Character:IsBound(),
    }
end)

-- Call remove() if the owning system is destroyed.
```

A sampler that errors, returns `false`, or returns a table without `Healthy = true` marks the receipt unhealthy.

## Grace periods

Grant grace when a player legitimately cannot answer, such as during a long load:

```lua copy filename="Server"
Network.Security.GrantIntegrityGrace(player, 15, "loading-dungeon")
```

Inspect a player with [`Security.ClientIntegrity(player)`](/reference/api/security#clientintegrity), or force an immediate challenge with [`Security.ChallengeIntegrity(player)`](/reference/api/security#challengeintegrity).

## Limits

<Callout type="warning">
The checksum is computed with an algorithm that is in the client module, so an exploiter can produce valid receipts without running your samplers. Treat integrity as liveness and tamper evidence: it catches clients whose runtime was broken or removed, not a careful attacker.
</Callout>

- Challenges are sent from the server's replication step; with `ManualReplication` they only run when you call `StepReplication`.
- Long client freezes (alt-tabbing on some devices, heavy loading) cause misses. Keep the kick thresholds conservative.

```

`docs/pages/security/client-shield.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Client shield"
description: "Client-side tripwires for common exploit tools, reported to the server over Cheeto's own frames."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Client shield

The client shield is a set of probes that run in the client module and look for signs of common exploit tooling. Hits are reported to the server inside Cheeto's normal traffic, not through a separate remote, and the server records them and can kick.

Turn it on with [`EnableClientShield`](/reference/options/client-shield#enableclientshield), or with [`SecurityPreset = Maximum`](/security/maximum-security).

## What it looks for

Every [`ClientShieldProbeIntervalSeconds`](/reference/options/client-shield#clientshieldprobeintervalseconds) (1.25 s by default) the shield runs a sweep:

| Probe | Looks for | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Environment globals | Executor functions such as `hookmetamethod`, `getrawmetatable`, `getgenv`, `getgc`, `gethui`, `saveinstance`, `decompile`, `writefile`, and markers like `IY_LOADED` | `ExploitEnvironment`, `InfiniteYield`, `SaveInstance`, `RemoteSpy` |
| Stack traps | Environments leaked through hooked metamethods | `MetamethodHook` |
| GUI tree | Text and names used by Infinite Yield, Dex, remote spies and save-instance tools | `InfiniteYield`, `DexExplorer`, `RemoteSpy`, `SaveInstance` |
| Weak service probes | Tools that cache services the game does not use | `DexExplorer`, `InfiniteYield`, `SaveInstance` |
| Chat tripwire | The Infinite Yield `;setcreatorid` pattern | `InfiniteYield` (immediate kick) |
| Save-instance safe mode | The error text a safe-mode save produces | `SaveInstance` (immediate kick) |

## What the server does

Each report adds its weight to the player's score for that reason. The report is recorded (at most once per reason per [`ClientShieldReportCooldownSeconds`](/reference/options/client-shield#clientshieldreportcooldownseconds)) and sent to [`OnViolation`](/security/violations) with channel `ClientShield`.

With [`ClientShieldKick`](/reference/options/client-shield#clientshieldkick) on, the player is kicked when the report is marked immediate, when [`ClientShieldStrict`](/reference/options/client-shield#clientshieldstrict) is on, or when the score for that reason reaches [`ClientShieldScoreThreshold`](/reference/options/client-shield#clientshieldscorethreshold).

Review recent reports with [`Security.ClientShield()`](/reference/api/security#clientshield). You can route your own server-side detections into the same pipeline with [`Security.ReportClientShield`](/reference/api/security#reportclientshield).

## Limits

<Callout type="error">
The shield runs on the exploiter's computer. A capable exploit can hide from every probe, block the reports, or disable the shield entirely. Absence of reports proves nothing. Presence of a report is strong evidence, but not proof: probes can misfire on unusual setups.
</Callout>

- Probes only see what a LocalScript can see. UI placed in protected containers is invisible to the GUI probe.
- The probe list targets well-known public tools. Private or new tools are not detected.
- Kicking on a single report, as `Maximum` does, will occasionally remove a legitimate player.

Roll out with `ClientShieldKick = false`, watch reports from real servers, and investigate before enforcing.

```

`docs/pages/security/constraints.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Constraints and Validate"
description: "Rules declared in the schema that the runtime enforces, and the Validate hook for everything else."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Constraints and Validate

Constraint fields write an endpoint's rules down in the schema, next to its data: how far away a target may be, whether the sender must own it, which team they must be on. The runtime enforces them on the server before your handler runs, and drops a failing packet with `ConstraintRejected`. For functions and predicted events, the client is told the reason.

| Field | Checked | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`RequireTeam`](/reference/fields#requireteam) | before decoding | The sender's Roblox team, or [`Replication.SetTeam`](/reference/api/replication#setteam) membership |
| [`RequireZone`](/reference/fields#requirezone) | before decoding | The zone set with [`Security.SetZone`](/reference/api/security#setzone) |
| [`RequireMatch`](/reference/fields#requirematch) | before decoding | Membership set with [`Replication.SetMatch`](/reference/api/replication#setmatch) |
| [`RequireCharacterState`](/reference/fields#requirecharacterstate) | before decoding | `Alive`, `Dead`, or a Humanoid state name |
| [`MaxDistance`](/reference/fields#maxdistance) | after decoding | Positions and parts in the payload are within range of the sender's character |
| [`RequireOwnership`](/reference/fields#requireownership) | after decoding | Instances in the payload belong to the sender |
| [`RequireObjectHandle`](/reference/fields#requireobjecthandle) | after decoding | The first number is a handle the sender may use |
| [`RequireServerKnownId`](/reference/fields#requireserverknownid) | after decoding | The first number or string is an id the server issued |
| [`RequireInventoryOwnership`](/reference/fields#requireinventoryownership) | after decoding | Your inventory resolver returns `true` |
| [`Risk`](/reference/fields#risk) | never | A tag passed to your code |

Sender constraints run before decoding, so a player who fails them costs the server no decode work. Payload constraints need the decoded values and run right after decoding, before the [`Validate`](/reference/api/hooks#validate) hook and the listener.

```cheeto copy
event Interact {
    From: Client,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Policy: "interact",
    RequireCharacterState: "Alive",
    MaxDistance: 12,
    RequireOwnership: true,
    Data: Instance(Model)
}
```

With that schema, a player who is dead, too far from the model, or does not own it never reaches the handler:

```lua copy
Network.Interact.On(function(player, model)
    Interactions.Run(player, model)
end)
```

## What they need from you

Some constraints check state only your game knows. Keep it current:

```lua copy
-- RequireZone
Network.Security.SetZone(player, "Arena")

-- RequireMatch
Network.Replication.SetMatch(matchId, player, true)

-- RequireOwnership: either register the owner or tag the instance
Network.Replication.SetObjectOwner(house, player, true)
house:SetAttribute("OwnerUserId", player.UserId)

-- RequireServerKnownId
Network.Security.RegisterKnownId(offerId, player)

-- RequireInventoryOwnership
Network.Security.SetInventoryResolver(function(player, payload)
    return Inventory.Has(player, payload[1])
end)
```

`RequireInventoryOwnership` with no resolver set rejects everything and warns once, so a missing resolver fails closed.

## The Validate hook

For conditions the fields cannot express, add a `Validate` hook. It runs after the built-in payload constraints and before the listener, for endpoints that declare a payload constraint. It receives `Name`, `Source`, `Channel`, `Size`, `Constraints` and `Payload` (the arguments, packed with `n`). Returning `false` drops the event with `ConstraintRejected`.

```lua copy
Network.Use("Validate", function(context)
    if context.Name ~= "Interact" then
        return true
    end

    local model = context.Payload[1]
    return not model:GetAttribute("Locked")
end)
```

One hook serves every endpoint: branch on `Name`, or write generic rules against `Constraints`.

## Where the checks stop

The payload constraints look at the arguments and the fields of table arguments, one level deep. `RequireObjectHandle` and `RequireServerKnownId` check the first number (or string) only. Values nested deeper, and rules like "the target is not the sender", belong in `Validate` or the listener. See [Limitations](/limitations#what-the-payload-constraints-examine).

<Callout type="info">
The `Validate` hook allocates a context table per event, so it is only generated for endpoints that declare a payload constraint. Endpoints without one pay nothing.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/security/handles-and-capabilities.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Handles and capabilities"
description: "Let clients refer to server objects by server-issued numbers instead of instances."
---

# Handles and capabilities

A client can send any instance it can see. If your `MoveBuildPiece` endpoint takes an `Instance`, an exploiter can pass another player's piece, or a part of the map. Checking ownership in every listener works, but it is easy to forget.

A **handle** turns this around: the server hands each client a number for each object it may act on, and the client sends the number back. The server resolves it, and only objects it registered for that player resolve.

## Handles

```lua copy filename="Server"
-- When a player places a piece
local handle = Network.Handles.Register(piece, player)
Network.PiecePlaced.Fire(player, handle, piece)

-- When the player later moves it
Network.MovePiece.On(function(player, handle, cframe)
    local piece = Network.Handles.Resolve(handle, player)
    if not piece then
        return -- unknown, expired, or someone else's
    end
    piece:PivotTo(cframe)
end)

-- When the piece is deleted
Network.Handles.Revoke(handle)
```

```cheeto copy
event MovePiece {
    From: Client,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Policy: "build",
    RequireObjectHandle: true,
    Data: (u32, CFrame)
}
```

- Always pass the sender to `Resolve`; without a player the owner check is skipped.
- `Register(object, owner, expiresAt)` accepts an absolute `os.clock()` expiry.
- Registering the same object again returns the same handle.

`RequireObjectHandle` does nothing by itself; it documents the contract and is passed to your [`Validate` hook](/security/constraints) as a constraint.

## Capabilities

A capability is a short-lived permission: "this player may `Edit` this plot for the next 15 seconds". Each call issues a new token.

```lua copy
local token = Network.Handles.IssueCapability(plot, player, { Edit = true }, 15)
Network.EditSessionStarted.Fire(player, token)

Network.EditPlot.On(function(player, token, change)
    local plot = Network.Handles.ValidateCapability(token, player, "Edit")
    if plot then
        Plots.Apply(plot, change)
    end
end)
```

Use capabilities for flows the server opens and closes: an edit session, a trade window, a one-time teleport.

## Where they live

Handles and capabilities are stored in the module that created them. Create and resolve them on the server. They are not persisted; a new server starts empty.

```

`docs/pages/security/honeypots.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Honeypots"
description: "Bait endpoints that no legitimate code ever calls, so any traffic on them identifies an exploiter."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Honeypots

A honeypot is an endpoint your game never uses. It exists only to be found. Because nothing legitimate ever sends to it, any traffic that arrives is proof that someone is crafting packets by hand, and you can act on that with near-zero risk of a false positive.

```cheeto copy
event AdminGiveCurrency {
    From: Client,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Honeypot: true,
    Data: (Instance(Player), u32)
}
```

## How it works

1. The endpoint is compiled into the modules like any other, so it appears in the generated client module with a tempting name and a `Fire` method.
2. Endpoint names never travel over the wire; frames only carry a one-byte endpoint number. So the only way to find this endpoint is to read the generated client module, which is exactly what someone writing an exploit does.
3. When a packet for it arrives, the server drops it **before rate limiting and before decoding**, with reason `Honeypot`, and reports it through [`Security.OnViolation`](/reference/api/security#onviolation) like every drop.

The check comes before the rate limit on purpose: an exploiter spamming the bait is fully reported instead of being silenced by a limit.

## Acting on it

```lua copy
Network.Security.OnViolation(function(report)
    if report.Reason == Network.Transport.Errors.Honeypot and typeof(report.Player) == "Instance" then
        Moderation.Flag(report.Player, "honeypot:" .. report.Event)
        report.Player:Kick()
    end
end)
```

Flag, log, ban or silently shadow-ban: the decision is yours. The runtime only reports.

## Choosing bait

- Name it after something an exploiter wants: `AdminGiveCurrency`, `SetWalkSpeed`, `DevSpawnItem`, `ForceWin`.
- Give it a plausible payload so it looks real.
- Declare it as you would a real endpoint. The honeypot check runs before auth and policy, so neither ever runs for it, but [`--strict`](/reference/cli#--strict) still expects a `Policy` on every client-sent endpoint, so add one if you use strict builds.
- Have a few, spread through the schema.

<Callout type="error">
**Never call a honeypot from game code**, including debug tools, admin panels or tests that run on live servers. One legitimate call would flag a real player. Reviewing honeypot names in the schema is enough to keep them out of use.
</Callout>

## Turning them off

[`EnableHoneypots`](/reference/options/security#enablehoneypots) is on by default. Set it to `false`, in the schema or live with `Network.Configure({ EnableHoneypots = false })`, to stop dropping and reporting. While it is off, honeypot endpoints are processed like any other endpoint, so do not connect listeners to them.

## Limits

- Honeypots catch people who read the client module and try endpoints. They do not catch an exploiter who only replays the game's own traffic.
- Anyone who reads this documentation knows the technique. Pick names that fit your game rather than the examples above.

```

`docs/pages/security/kill-switches.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Kill switches"
description: "Disable an endpoint or a group of endpoints on a live server."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Kill switches

When an exploit is found in one endpoint, you often cannot ship a fix right away. A kill switch turns that endpoint off on a running server, without a restart and without affecting anything else.

```lua copy
Network.Security.Kill("TradeRequest", "dupe investigation")
-- later
Network.Security.Unkill("TradeRequest")
```

While killed, events arriving on the endpoint are dropped with `KillSwitch` before decoding, and sends on it are dropped too. Function requests to a killed function are answered with `KillSwitch`, so clients' `Invoke` calls fail straight away.

## Killing a group

Endpoints that share a [`PolicyGroup`](/reference/fields#policygroup) can be switched off together:

```lua copy
Network.Security.KillPolicyGroup("economy", "market exploit")
```

Design your policy groups with this in mind: grouping everything that touches currency under `economy` gives you one switch for the whole economy.

## Doing it across servers

A kill switch affects only the server it runs on. To switch an endpoint off everywhere, broadcast the command, for example with the [MessagingService adapter](/reference/api/replication#messagingservice):

```lua copy
local control = Network.Replication.MessagingService("net-control")

control.Subscribe(function(message)
    if message.Channel == "kill" then
        Network.Security.Kill(message.Payload)
    elseif message.Channel == "unkill" then
        Network.Security.Unkill(message.Payload)
    end
end)

-- From an admin command:
control.Publish("kill", "TradeRequest")
```

<Callout type="info">
If your endpoints are split across several generated modules, kill the endpoint on the module that actually carries it.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/security/maximum-security.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Profiles and presets"
description: "SecurityProfile chooses limits; SecurityPreset = Maximum switches on every optional protection."
---

import { Callout, Steps } from 'nextra/components'

# Profiles and presets

Two options set many defaults at once.

## SecurityProfile

[`SecurityProfile`](/reference/options/security#securityprofile) picks packet, rate, queue and invoke limits.

| | Development | Production | Competitive |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Max reliable packet | 1 MiB | 256 KiB | 64 KiB |
| Max unreliable packet | 1,000 B | 1,000 B | 900 B |
| Rate limit per remote | off | 120/s, burst 240 | 60/s, burst 120 |
| Max pending invokes | 256 | 64 | 32 |

Use `Development` in Studio, `Production` for most live games, and `Competitive` where abuse is likely and traffic is predictable. Every limit can still be set individually. See [Transport limits](/reference/options/limits).

## SecurityPreset = Maximum

`option SecurityPreset = Maximum` changes these defaults:

| Option | Becomes |
| --- | --- |
| `SecurityProfile` | `Competitive` |
| `RequirePolicies` | `true`: every client-sent endpoint needs a `Policy` |
| `EnableClientShield`, `ClientShieldStrict`, `ClientShieldKick` | `true`: exploit tripwires, and kick on the first hit |
| `EnableClientIntegrity` | `true`: periodic liveness challenges |
| `EnableCharacterIntegrity` | `true`, in `Correct` mode: impossible movement is pulled back |
| `EnableRemoteNameRotation`, `EnableRemoteDecoys` | `true`, with 8 decoys |

Character kicks stay off. Anything you set explicitly overrides the preset.

```cheeto copy
option ClientOutput = "Network/Client.luau"
option ServerOutput = "Network/Server.luau"
option SecurityPreset = Maximum
option Version = 1
option MinimumSchemaVersion = 1
option InvokeTimeoutSeconds = 10

event DamageRequest {
    From: Client,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Policy: "damage",
    CooldownSeconds: 0.2,
    Data: u16(0..200)
}
```

## Rolling it out

`Maximum` kicks players. On a live game, turn it on in stages.

<Steps>

### Start reporting only

Keep every protection on but disable kicks and corrections:

```cheeto copy
option SecurityPreset = Maximum
option ClientShieldKick = false
option CharacterIntegrityMode = Report
```

### Register real policies and watch violations

Register a rule for every policy name you use (unregistered names drop everything), and log violations:

```lua copy filename="ServerScriptService/Network.server.luau"
local Network = require(ReplicatedStorage.Network.Server)

Network.Security.RegisterPolicy("damage", function(context)
    local character = context.Source.Character
    local humanoid = character and character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    return humanoid ~= nil and humanoid.Health > 0, "dead"
end)

Network.Security.OnViolation(function(report)
    Log.Warn("net", report.Reason, report.Player, report.Event, report.Action)
end)
```

Require the client module early, from a LocalScript in `StarterPlayerScripts`, so the shield starts before other code runs:

```lua copy filename="StarterPlayerScripts/Network.client.luau"
require(ReplicatedStorage.Network.Client)
```

### Tune on real sessions

Look at which reasons fire and for whom. Raise [movement limits](/reference/options/character-integrity) for mechanics that move players fast, and wrap server teleports in [`Security.TeleportCharacter`](/reference/api/security#teleportcharacter). Investigate every shield report on a real player before trusting it.

### Enforce

Remove the overrides so corrections and shield kicks apply. Enable character kicks last, and only once reports are clean:

```cheeto copy
option SecurityPreset = Maximum
option CharacterIntegrityMode = Kick
option CharacterIntegrityKick = true
```

</Steps>

<Callout type="warning">
`ClientShieldStrict` under `Maximum` means one detection kicks. A false positive from a legitimate tool or plugin removes a real player. Keep `ClientShieldKick = false` until you have watched reports on live servers.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/security/overview.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Security model"
description: "What Cheeto protects against, what it cannot, and which layer does what."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Security model

Assume every client is hostile. An exploiter can read everything the server sends them, and can fire any remote with any bytes, as often as they like. Cheeto's job is to make sure that whatever arrives either matches your contract exactly, or is dropped and reported before your code sees it.

## The layers

| Layer | Stops | Where it runs | Page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Packet limits | Oversized packets, floods, fragment abuse | Before decoding | [Rate limits and cooldowns](/security/rate-limits-and-cooldowns) |
| Honeypots | Anyone probing endpoints that nothing legitimate calls | Before decoding | [Honeypots](/security/honeypots) |
| Auth rules | Senders in the wrong state (dead, not loaded) | Before decoding | [Auth rules](/security/auth-rules) |
| Kill switches | An endpoint under active abuse | Before decoding | [Kill switches](/security/kill-switches) |
| Cooldowns | Repeating one-shot actions | Before decoding | [Rate limits and cooldowns](/security/rate-limits-and-cooldowns) |
| Replay checks | Resending captured predicted events | Before decoding | [Replay and idempotency](/security/replay-and-idempotency) |
| Policies | Senders who may not use this endpoint | Before decoding | [Policies](/security/policies) |
| Schema types | Wrong types, out-of-range numbers, wrong instance classes | Decoding | [Types](/reference/types/numbers) |
| Payload checks | NaN, huge tables, deep nesting, long strings | After decoding | [Payload validation](/security/payload-validation) |
| Validate hooks | Payload-specific rules such as distance and ownership | After decoding | [Constraints and Validate](/security/constraints) |
| Handles | Clients naming objects they should not control | Your listener | [Handles and capabilities](/security/handles-and-capabilities) |

Beside the network, three optional systems watch clients directly: the [client shield](/security/client-shield) (exploit tripwires), [client integrity](/security/client-integrity) (liveness challenges) and [character integrity](/security/character-integrity) (server-side movement checks). [Remote hardening](/security/remote-hardening) makes the remotes harder to find.

Every drop and report goes to one place: [`Security.OnViolation`](/security/violations).

## What a schema should look like

Every endpoint a client sends should have, at minimum:

- a [`Policy`](/reference/fields#policy) with a real rule registered on the server;
- tight types: bounded strings, bounded arrays, ranged numbers, classes on instances;
- a [`CooldownSeconds`](/reference/fields#cooldownseconds) or [`RateLimitPerSecond`](/reference/fields#ratelimitpersecond) that matches how often a real player can do it;
- an [`InvokeTimeoutSeconds`](/reference/fields#invoketimeoutseconds) if it is a function.

```cheeto copy
option SecurityProfile = Production
option RequirePolicies = true
option InvokeTimeoutSeconds = 10

event BuyItem {
    From: Client,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Policy: "shop",
    CooldownSeconds: 0.5,
    Data: u16(1..500)
}
```

[`SecurityPreset = Maximum`](/security/maximum-security) turns the optional systems on in one line.

## What Cheeto cannot do

<Callout type="error">
**Cheeto cannot make a client trustworthy.** It cannot stop a client from reading what you send it, from sending any bytes it wants, or from lying about its own state. The client shield and integrity checks run on hardware the exploiter controls, so they are tripwires and evidence, never proof.
</Callout>

The server must still decide everything that matters:

- Send the client what it wants to do (`BuyItem 42`), never the result (`SetCoins 900`).
- Look up prices, damage, cooldown state and ownership on the server.
- Never send secrets, other players' private data, or anything you would not want an exploiter to read.

<Callout type="warning">
Every protection fails closed: an unregistered policy, policy group, auth rule or inventory resolver drops the packets it guards. Read [Limitations](/limitations#security) for where each check stops.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/security/payload-validation.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Payload validation"
description: "What is checked in every decoded payload before any listener sees it."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Payload validation

Every received event goes through two rounds of checks before its listener runs.

## 1. Decoding against the schema

The generated decoder reads exactly the declared types, so a payload cannot contain an unexpected type or extra fields. While reading, it checks:

- number ranges: `u8(0..100)` rejects 101;
- string, buffer and array lengths: `string(3..20)` rejects a 2-byte name;
- vector magnitudes: `vector(0..1)` rejects a length-2 vector;
- instance classes: `Instance(Player)` rejects a Part;
- required instances: a non-optional `Instance` that arrives as `nil` is rejected.

Any failure drops the event with `MalformedPacket`.

## 2. Payload checks

Then the decoded value is walked once more, bounded by the [decode budget options](/reference/options/limits#decode-budgets):

| Check | Default limit | Drop reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Numbers are finite (no NaN or infinity) | | `Canonicalization` |
| Vectors and CFrame positions are finite and within 10⁹ studs | | `Canonicalization` |
| Color3 channels are finite | | `Canonicalization` |
| Strings are at most [`MaxPayloadStringBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxpayloadstringbytes) | 8,192 bytes | `Canonicalization` |
| Tables are at most [`MaxPayloadDepth`](/reference/options/limits#maxpayloaddepth) deep | 16 | `Canonicalization` |
| Tables have at most [`MaxTableKeys`](/reference/options/limits#maxtablekeys) keys | 2,048 | `Canonicalization` |
| Table keys are strings, booleans or positive whole numbers | | `Canonicalization` |
| Arrays are not sparse (highest index at most twice the entry count) | | `Canonicalization` |
| Total values visited at most [`MaxDecodeOperations`](/reference/options/limits#maxdecodeoperations) | 100,000 | `DecodeBudget` |

These matter most for [`unknown`](/reference/types/unknown) fields, which bypass the schema's types, and they protect your listeners from values that break math (NaN positions, infinite damage).

## What is left to you

Validation proves the data is well-formed. It cannot prove it is legitimate. A `u16(0..500)` damage value of 500 is valid, and whether this player's weapon can deal 500 is a game rule. Check game rules in a [`Validate` hook](/security/constraints) or in the listener, using server-side state.

<Callout type="info">
Turn on [`WriteValidations`](/reference/options/runtime#writevalidations) during development to run the type and range checks on the sender too, so mistakes fail at the `Fire` call instead of as a dropped packet on the other side.
</Callout>

```

`docs/pages/security/policies.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Policies"
description: "Per-endpoint permission rules and policy groups, and why an unregistered name drops everything."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Policies

A policy decides whether a sender may use an endpoint. Endpoints name one with [`Policy`](/reference/fields#policy); you register the rule on the server with [`Security.RegisterPolicy`](/reference/api/security#registerpolicy).

```cheeto copy
function TradeAccept {
    Yield: Coroutine,
    Policy: "trade",
    PolicyGroup: "economy",
    CooldownSeconds: 0.5,
    InvokeTimeoutSeconds: 10,
    Data: u32,
    Return: boolean
}
```

```lua copy
Network.Security.RegisterPolicy("trade", function(context)
    local player = context.Source
    if not Profiles.IsLoaded(player) then
        return false, "profile-not-loaded"
    end
    if Trading.IsLocked(player) then
        return false, "trade-locked"
    end
    return true
end)
```

## How a policy runs

- It runs before the payload is decoded, after auth, cooldown, replay and sender-constraint checks. See [The receive pipeline](/concepts/receive-pipeline).
- It receives a context: `Source`, `Name`, `Channel`, `Policy`, `PolicyGroup`, `Constraints`, `UserId` and `Size`. It does **not** receive the payload.
- Return `true` to allow. Return `false`, optionally with a reason string, to deny. The reason becomes the drop reason in violation reports, and for functions and predicted events it is the reason the client's `Invoke` fails with or its prediction rolls back with.
- A policy that errors denies.

## Unregistered names fail closed

A policy name that nothing registered denies every packet on its endpoints, and the first one logs:

```
[Cheeto]: Policy "trade" is not registered, so every packet on "TradeAccept" is dropped. Register it with Security.RegisterPolicy.
```

There are no built-in policies. A name in the schema is a promise that a rule exists, and the runtime holds you to it: a typo or a forgotten registration shows up as a drop in testing, not as an open endpoint in production.

## Policy groups

A group is a named list of policies that all must pass, in addition to the endpoint's own `Policy`. It lets several endpoints share checks, and lets you [kill](/security/kill-switches) them together.

```lua copy
Network.Security.RegisterPolicyGroup("economy", { "profile-loaded", "not-trade-locked" })
```

A group that is never registered denies, like an unregistered policy. A policy listed in a group that is not itself registered also denies.

## Requiring policies

[`RequirePolicies = true`](/reference/options/security#requirepolicies) drops any client-sent endpoint that declares none of `Policy`, `PolicyGroup` or `Auth`. Turn it on so an endpoint added without any rule fails closed instead of open. `--doctor` and `--strict` report those endpoints at compile time.

## Checking the payload

A policy cannot see the data. To check the data, use the [`Validate`](/security/constraints) hook or check it in your listener. A common split: the policy answers "can this player trade right now?", and the listener answers "does this player own the item in this trade?".

```

`docs/pages/security/rate-limits-and-cooldowns.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Rate limits and cooldowns"
description: "Bounding how often a sender can call an endpoint, and how much a packet can cost."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Rate limits and cooldowns

## Three tools

| Tool | Limits | Scope | Checked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Per-remote rate limit | Remote calls per second | All traffic from one sender on one remote | Before reading any frame |
| Per-endpoint rate limit | Events per second | One sender, one endpoint | Before auth and policy |
| Cooldown | Minimum gap between accepted calls | One sender, one endpoint | Before policy |

### Per-remote rate limit

The [`RateLimitPerSecond`](/reference/options/limits#ratelimitpersecond) and [`RateLimitBurst`](/reference/options/limits#ratelimitburst) values from the security profile (off in `Development`, 120/s in `Production`, 60/s in `Competitive`) limit remote calls per sender. Because reliable traffic is batched into one call per frame, a normal client makes about 60 reliable calls a second, well under the Production limit. A flood of hand-crafted calls is cut off before any of it is decoded.

### Per-endpoint rate limit

Setting `RateLimitPerSecond` on an endpoint, or writing the option in the schema, adds a token bucket to that endpoint. The bucket starts full at `RateLimitBurst` tokens and refills at `RateLimitPerSecond`. Each event takes one token; with none left the event is dropped with `RateLimit` and the rest of the packet continues.

```cheeto copy
event Swing {
    From: Client,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Policy: "combat",
    RateLimitPerSecond: 8,
    RateLimitBurst: 12
}
```

### Cooldown

[`CooldownSeconds`](/reference/fields#cooldownseconds) accepts at most one call per window from each sender. Unlike a rate limit, it allows no burst, which makes it right for one-shot actions: purchases, abilities, votes.

```cheeto copy
event ClaimDailyReward {
    From: Client,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Policy: "rewards",
    CooldownSeconds: 5
}
```

<Callout type="warning">
Set a cooldown looser than the client's own retry interval. If the client re-sends every 2 seconds, a 1-second cooldown is fine and a 3-second one silently drops real retries.
</Callout>

## Choosing limits

Base limits on what a legitimate player can physically do, with headroom for lag bursts: a weapon that fires 10 times per second might get `RateLimitPerSecond: 12, RateLimitBurst: 20`. Watch `Stats().RateLimitHits` on live servers. If real players hit a limit, it is too tight.

## Bounding work

Rate limits bound how often; these bound how much each packet can cost:

- [`MaxReliablePacketBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxreliablepacketbytes) and [`MaxUnreliablePacketBytes`](/reference/options/limits#maxunreliablepacketbytes) cap each remote call.
- [`MaxInFlightFragments`](/reference/options/limits#maxinflightfragments) and [`FragmentTimeoutSeconds`](/reference/options/limits#fragmenttimeoutseconds) cap memory used by half-sent fragmented packets.
- [Payload checks](/security/payload-validation) cap depth, table size, string length and total work per payload.

Drops from all of these land in [`OnViolation`](/security/violations) and in the sender's [abuse score](/reference/api/security#abusescores).

```

`docs/pages/security/remote-hardening.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Remote names and decoys"
description: "Randomized RemoteEvent names and decoy remotes, and exactly what they do and do not stop."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Remote names and decoys

Many exploit scripts and tools work by finding RemoteEvents by name and firing them. Two options make that harder.

## Name rotation

With [`EnableRemoteNameRotation`](/reference/options/remote-hardening#enableremotenamerotation), the server creates its two remotes in a folder called `CHEETO_REMOTE_ROOT` (prefixed with your [`RemoteScope`](/reference/options/output#remotescope)) with random names such as `_CHEETO_9f3a17c2e8b44d01af`, and renames them every [`RemoteNameRotationSeconds`](/reference/options/remote-hardening#remotenamerotationseconds). The current names are published as attributes on the folder; the client module follows them and reconnects automatically.

This breaks scripts that hard-code remote names, and tools that cache a path.

## Decoys

With [`EnableRemoteDecoys`](/reference/options/remote-hardening#enableremotedecoys), the server also creates [`RemoteDecoyCount`](/reference/options/remote-hardening#remotedecoycount) extra remotes next to the real ones, alternating `RemoteEvent` and `UnreliableRemoteEvent`, with names in the same format as the real pair. Nothing in your game fires them. When one is fired, the sender is reported with reason `RemoteDecoy` and a weight of 100, and kicked if [`ClientShieldKick`](/reference/options/client-shield#clientshieldkick) is on.

This catches remote spies with "fire all" features, fuzzers, and scripts that fire every remote they find.

## What they do not stop

<Callout type="warning">
Both are obstacles for generic tools, not for someone targeting your game:

- The real remote names are published as attributes that any client can read, which is how the legitimate client module finds them.
- Rotation renames the same instances. A tool holding a reference to the remote keeps working.
- Anyone who reads the generated client module can use it to send packets directly.
</Callout>

Treat rotation and decoys as noise reduction: they filter out low-effort attacks so your logs show the targeted ones. Real protection comes from [policies](/security/policies), [validation](/security/payload-validation) and server authority.

Both are enabled by [`SecurityPreset = Maximum`](/security/maximum-security).

```

`docs/pages/security/replay-and-idempotency.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Replay and idempotency"
description: "Rejecting duplicated and replayed packets, and what that does and does not protect."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Replay and idempotency

A replay attack resends a packet the attacker captured earlier, for example a valid `ClaimReward` request, hoping the server processes it twice. Cheeto rejects replayed packets on endpoints that ask for it.

## Idempotency

Set [`Idempotency: true`](/reference/fields#idempotency) on a client-sent event or function. Every send then carries a 16-bit sequence number, and the server drops any packet whose number is not newer than the last one it accepted from that sender, with reason `OutOfOrder`. The client does nothing different: `Fire` and `Invoke` stamp the number themselves.

```cheeto copy
event ClaimReward {
    From: Client,
    Type: Reliable,
    Call: SingleAsync,
    Policy: "rewards",
    Idempotency: true,
    Data: u16
}
```

A captured `ClaimReward` packet sent again is dropped, however many times it is sent.

## Predicted events

Events sent with [`Predict`](/reference/api/event#predict) also carry their prediction id, and two more checks apply to every predicted packet:

| Check | Drop reason |
| --- | --- |
| The same prediction id was already accepted | `ReplayDuplicate` |
| The id is more than [`ReplayWindowSize`](/reference/options/limits#replaywindowsize) behind the newest one | `ReplayStale` |
| With `Idempotency`, the same id within 120 seconds | `ReplayDuplicate` |

Prediction ids are 16-bit and wrap after 65,535; the window uses serial-number arithmetic, so the wrap is invisible. A dropped prediction is rolled back on the client with the reason.

## What replay protection does not cover

<Callout type="warning">
A sequence number proves a packet is not a copy of an earlier one. It does not prove the request makes sense: an exploiter can build a new `ClaimReward` packet with a fresh number, and that is an ordinary request. Protect the action itself too.
</Callout>

- **A cooldown.** [`CooldownSeconds`](/reference/fields#cooldownseconds) is enforced before decoding and needs nothing from the client.
- **A server-issued key.** Put an id the server issued in the request, such as an offer id or a [handle](/security/handles-and-capabilities), check it with [`RequireServerKnownId`](/reference/fields#requireserverknownid) or [`RequireObjectHandle`](/reference/fields#requireobjecthandle), and forget it once used. [`Security.CheckIdempotency`](/reference/api/security#checkidempotency) does the bookkeeping for keys you choose:

```lua copy
Network.AcceptOffer.On(function(player, offerId)
    if not Network.Security.CheckIdempotency(player, `offer:{offerId}`, 600) then
        return
    end
    Offers.Accept(player, offerId)
end)
```

- **Server state.** Most duplicate-effect bugs are state bugs: grant a reward only if it has not been granted, not only if the request is new.

```

`docs/pages/security/security-toolkit.mdx`:

```mdx
import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Standalone toolkit

The repository ships a set of standalone anti-exploit detectors in [`extras/security`](https://github.com/pealz1/cheeto/tree/main/extras/security). They do not depend on a Cheeto schema, so you can drop them into any game.

<Callout type="info">
  If your game already uses a Cheeto schema, start with [Profiles and presets](/security/maximum-security). It covers liveness challenges and server-side movement checks over Cheeto's own transport. Reach for this toolkit when you have not migrated yet, or want a second layer.
</Callout>

## What is included

| Detector | What it catches |
| --- | --- |
| Infinite Yield detection | The Infinite Yield admin script, through four independent GUI fingerprints |
| Movement anti-cheat | Speed, fly, noclip, infinite jump, mass, void teleport, anti-gravity and anti-knockback |

Both detectors share one signed report channel. The server issues a per-session secret, verifies every report against a strictly increasing sequence number, and removes a client that stops sending heartbeats after it has joined.

## Installing

| Script | Location |
| --- | --- |
| `IYDetector.client.luau` | `StarterPlayerScripts` |
| `MovementAnticheat.client.luau` | `StarterPlayerScripts` |
| `IYGuard.server.luau` | `ServerScriptService` |

Every script requires its dependencies from `script.Parent`, so place the shared modules (`Config`, `SecureChannel`, `SecureReport`, `IYSignatures`, `SuspicionScore`, `KnockbackForce`, `MovementConfig`) next to the scripts that use them.

## Tuning the movement detectors

Each detector feeds a per-tick condition into a scoring engine that ramps while the condition holds and decays when it clears.

- The **rollback** threshold is low. Crossing it quietly resets the player's property and position.
- The **report** threshold is much higher. Crossing it reports to the server, which removes the player.

Tune both, per detector, in `MovementConfig.luau`. Keep the gap between them wide: it is what stops lag spikes, server teleports and physics glitches from ever producing a report.

## Limitations

- The Infinite Yield scan can only read containers a LocalScript is allowed to read. UI parented to protected `CoreGui` through `gethui()` is invisible to it; the heartbeat timeout covers the case where the detector is removed.
- The session secret lives in client memory, so signing is defence in depth rather than proof. Keep authority on the server.

The [toolkit README](https://github.com/pealz1/cheeto/blob/main/extras/security/README.md) documents every file, signal and test in detail.

```

`docs/pages/security/violations.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Violations and abuse scores"
description: "One stream for every drop and security report, and per-player counters."
---

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Violations and abuse scores

Every protection reports to the same place. Subscribe once and you see drops, honeypot hits, shield reports, integrity failures and movement evidence as one stream of [`ViolationReport`](/reference/violation-report)s.

```lua copy
Network.Security.OnViolation(function(report)
    -- report.Reason, report.Player, report.Event, report.Channel,
    -- report.Score, report.Action, report.PayloadSize, report.Time
end)
```

## Sorting reports

Not every report means cheating. Group them before acting:

| Kind | Reasons | Usually means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Proof of tampering | `Honeypot`, `RemoteDecoy`, `InvalidBuffer`, `InvalidInstances` | A hand-crafted packet. Legitimate clients cannot produce these |
| Likely tampering | `MalformedPacket`, `Canonicalization`, `DecodeBudget`, `ReplayDuplicate`, shield reasons | Crafted data, or occasionally a version mismatch |
| Rule violations | `PolicyRejected`, `AuthRejected`, `ConstraintRejected`, custom policy reasons | Often exploits, but also races such as acting while dying |
| Volume | `RateLimit`, `MaxPacketBytes`, `QueueFull`, `FragmentOverflow` | Floods, or limits that are too tight for real play |
| Your side | `Backpressure`, `KillSwitch`, send-side `MaxPacketBytes`, `MiddlewareRejected` on send | Your server's own limits and switches |
| Movement and liveness | Character and client integrity reasons | Read with their own thresholds and modes |

```lua copy
local PROOF = {
    [Network.Transport.Errors.Honeypot] = true,
    [Network.Transport.Errors.RemoteDecoy] = true,
    [Network.Transport.Errors.InvalidBuffer] = true,
}

Network.Security.OnViolation(function(report)
    if typeof(report.Player) ~= "Instance" then
        return
    end
    if PROOF[report.Reason] then
        Moderation.Ban(report.Player, report.Reason)
    else
        Telemetry.Count("net." .. report.Reason)
    end
end)
```

## Abuse scores

Each report also increments a counter for the sender, keyed by endpoint name or reason. Read them with [`Security.AbuseScores(player)`](/reference/api/security#abusescores) to spot a player who hits many small limits. Counters reset when the player leaves.

`report.Score` is that counter's value for the report's `Event`.

<Callout type="info">
`OnViolation` is a middleware hook. It stops firing if [`EnableMiddleware`](/reference/options/runtime#enablemiddleware) is off, and a slow callback delays packet processing. Hand heavy work (DataStore writes, webhooks) to a separate thread.
</Callout>

```

`docs/scripts/check-examples.mjs`:

```mjs
// Compiles every ```cheeto example in the docs with the real compiler, so the
// docs cannot show syntax that does not parse. Blocks tagged `nocheck` (for
// fragments that only make sense next to another block) are skipped.
//
// Usage, from the repository root: node docs/scripts/check-examples.mjs
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { mkdtempSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { join, relative } from 'node:path'

const root = process.cwd()
const pagesDir = join(root, 'docs', 'pages')
const declaration = /^(export\s+)?(event|function|channel|type|struct|enum|map|set|scope)\s/m
const header = 'option ClientOutput = "out/Client.luau"\noption ServerOutput = "out/Server.luau"\n'

function* mdxFiles(dir) {
  for (const name of readdirSync(dir)) {
    const path = join(dir, name)
    if (statSync(path).isDirectory()) yield* mdxFiles(path)
    else if (name.endsWith('.mdx')) yield path
  }
}

function* blocks(source) {
  const fence = /```cheeto([^\n]*)\n([\s\S]*?)```/g
  let match
  while ((match = fence.exec(source))) {
    yield { meta: match[1], code: match[2], line: source.slice(0, match.index).split('\n').length }
  }
}

const work = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'cheeto-docs-'))
let checked = 0
const failures = []

for (const file of mdxFiles(pagesDir)) {
  for (const block of blocks(readFileSync(file, 'utf8'))) {
    if (block.meta.includes('nocheck') || !declaration.test(block.code) || /^\s*import\s/m.test(block.code)) continue
    const hasOutput = /option\s+ClientOutput/.test(block.code)
    const options = (block.code.match(/^option .*$/gm) ?? []).filter((line) => !/TypesOutput/.test(line))
    const body = block.code.replace(/^option .*$/gm, '')
    const source = `${hasOutput ? '' : header}${options.join('\n')}\n${body}`
    const schema = join(work, `example${checked}.cheeto`)
    writeFileSync(schema, source)
    checked += 1
    try {
      const output = execFileSync('lune', ['run', 'src/CLI/init.luau', schema.replace(/\.cheeto$/, ''), '--', '--yes'], {
        cwd: root,
        encoding: 'utf8',
        stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']
      })
      if (!output.includes('Network files generated')) throw new Error(output)
    } catch (error) {
      const text = String(error.stderr || error.stdout || error.message)
      failures.push(`${relative(root, file)}:${block.line}\n${text.split('\n').slice(0, 12).join('\n')}`)
    }
  }
}

if (failures.length > 0) {
  console.error(`${failures.length} of ${checked} cheeto examples failed to compile:\n`)
  console.error(failures.join('\n\n'))
  process.exit(1)
}
console.log(`All ${checked} cheeto examples compile.`)

```

`docs/scripts/check-links.mjs`:

```mjs
// Verifies every internal link and #anchor in the exported site points at a
// page and heading that exist. Runs after `next build` against docs/out.
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join, relative, sep } from 'node:path'

const out = new URL('../out/', import.meta.url).pathname.replace(/^\/([A-Za-z]:)/, '$1')
const basePath = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH ?? ''

function* htmlFiles(dir) {
  for (const name of readdirSync(dir)) {
    const path = join(dir, name)
    if (statSync(path).isDirectory()) yield* htmlFiles(path)
    else if (name.endsWith('.html')) yield path
  }
}

const pages = new Map()
for (const file of htmlFiles(out)) {
  let route = '/' + relative(out, file).split(sep).join('/').replace(/\.html$/, '')
  route = route.replace(/\/index$/, '') || '/'
  if (route === '/index') route = '/'
  const html = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')
  const ids = new Set([...html.matchAll(/\sid="([^"]+)"/g)].map((match) => match[1]))
  pages.set(route, { html, ids })
}

const failures = new Set()
for (const [route, { html }] of pages) {
  for (const [, raw] of html.matchAll(/href="([^"]+)"/g)) {
    const href = raw.replace(/&amp;/g, '&')
    if (/^(https?:|mailto:|data:)/.test(href) || href.startsWith('/_next/')) continue
    if (basePath && href.startsWith(`${basePath}/_next/`)) continue
    let [path, anchor] = href.split('#')
    if (path === '') path = route
    if (basePath) {
      if (!path.startsWith(basePath)) continue
      path = path.slice(basePath.length) || '/'
    }
    if (!path.startsWith('/')) continue
    path = path.replace(/\/$/, '') || '/'
    if (/\.(png|svg|jpg|ico|json|rbxm|xml|txt)$/.test(path)) continue
    const target = pages.get(path)
    if (!target) {
      failures.add(`${route}: missing page ${href}`)
    } else if (anchor && !target.ids.has(decodeURIComponent(anchor))) {
      failures.add(`${route}: missing anchor ${href}`)
    }
  }
}

if (failures.size > 0) {
  console.error(`${failures.size} broken links:\n${[...failures].sort().join('\n')}`)
  process.exit(1)
}
console.log(`Checked links across ${pages.size} pages.`)

`docs/scripts/check-reference.mjs`:

```mjs
// Fails when the reference drifts from the compiler: every option, endpoint
// field, runtime namespace member and drop reason in src/ must have an entry,
// and the docs must not reference Network.* members that do not exist.
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'

const docs = new URL('..', import.meta.url).pathname.replace(/^\/([A-Za-z]:)/, '$1')
const src = join(docs, '..', 'src')
const pages = join(docs, 'pages')
const read = (path) => readFileSync(path, 'utf8')
const failures = []

function* mdxFiles(dir) {
  for (const name of readdirSync(dir)) {
    const path = join(dir, name)
    if (statSync(path).isDirectory()) yield* mdxFiles(path)
    else if (name.endsWith('.mdx')) yield path
  }
}

const headings = (text) => new Set([...text.matchAll(/^#{2,3} `?([A-Za-z0-9]+)`?/gm)].map((match) => match[1]))

// Options
const parser = read(join(src, 'Parser.luau'))
const optionBlock = parser.match(/local OPTIONS[^{]*\{([\s\S]*?)\n\}/)[1]
const options = [...optionBlock.matchAll(/^\s+([A-Za-z0-9]+) = "/gm)].map((match) => match[1])
const removed = new Set(['ProtocolMode', 'AcceptProtocolVersion1'])
const optionDir = join(pages, 'reference', 'options')
const optionHeadings = new Set()
for (const file of readdirSync(optionDir)) {
  if (file.endsWith('.mdx') && file !== 'overview.mdx') {
    for (const heading of headings(read(join(optionDir, file)))) optionHeadings.add(heading)
  }
}
for (const option of options) {
  if (!removed.has(option) && !optionHeadings.has(option)) failures.push(`option ${option} has no entry in reference/options`)
}
const overview = read(join(optionDir, 'overview.mdx'))
for (const option of options) {
  if (!overview.includes(`\`${option}\``)) failures.push(`option ${option} is missing from reference/options/overview`)
}

// Endpoint fields
const fieldsPage = headings(read(join(pages, 'reference', 'fields.mdx')))
for (const table of ['EVENT', 'FUNCTION', 'CHANNEL']) {
  const block = parser.match(new RegExp(`local ${table}: \\{ EventOption \\} = \\{([\\s\\S]*?)\\n\\}`))[1]
  for (const [, key] of block.matchAll(/Key = "([A-Za-z]+)"/g)) {
    if (!fieldsPage.has(key)) failures.push(`${table.toLowerCase()} field ${key} has no entry in reference/fields`)
  }
}

// Runtime namespaces
const generator = read(join(src, 'Generator', 'init.luau'))
const pushBlock = generator.match(/local function PushRuntimeApi[\s\S]*?\nend\n/)[0]
const namespaces = new Map()
const rootMembers = new Set()
let current = null
for (const line of pushBlock.split('\n')) {
  const push = line.match(/Target\.Push\(`([A-Za-z]+) = /)
  if (line.includes('Target.Push(`}),`')) {
    current = null
  } else if (push && line.includes('table.freeze')) {
    current = push[1]
    namespaces.set(current, new Set())
  } else if (push) {
    ;(current ? namespaces.get(current) : rootMembers).add(push[1])
  }
}
namespaces.get('Connection')?.delete('new')
const apiDir = join(pages, 'reference', 'api')
for (const [namespace, members] of namespaces) {
  const file = join(apiDir, `${namespace.toLowerCase()}.mdx`)
  let page
  try {
    page = headings(read(file))
  } catch {
    failures.push(`namespace ${namespace} has no page reference/api/${namespace.toLowerCase()}.mdx`)
    continue
  }
  for (const member of members) {
    if (!page.has(member)) failures.push(`${namespace}.${member} has no entry in reference/api/${namespace.toLowerCase()}.mdx`)
  }
}
const modulePage = headings(read(join(apiDir, 'module.mdx')))
for (const member of [...rootMembers, 'StepReplication']) {
  if (member !== 'Connection' && !modulePage.has(member)) failures.push(`module member ${member} has no entry in reference/api/module.mdx`)
}

// Drop reasons
const base = read(join(src, 'Templates', 'Base.luau'))
const errorBlock = base.match(/local TransportError = table\.freeze\(\{([\s\S]*?)\}\)/)[1]
const dropPage = read(join(pages, 'reference', 'drop-reasons.mdx'))
for (const [, reason] of errorBlock.matchAll(/^\s+([A-Za-z]+) = "/gm)) {
  if (!dropPage.includes(`\`${reason}\``)) failures.push(`drop reason ${reason} is missing from reference/drop-reasons`)
}

// Network.Namespace.Member references anywhere in the docs
for (const file of mdxFiles(pages)) {
  for (const [, namespace, member] of read(file).matchAll(/Network\.([A-Z][A-Za-z]+)\.([A-Z][A-Za-z]+)/g)) {
    const known = namespaces.get(namespace)
    if (known && !known.has(member) && !(namespace === 'Connection' && member === 'new')) {
      failures.push(`${file.slice(pages.length + 1)} mentions Network.${namespace}.${member}, which does not exist`)
    }
  }
}

if (failures.length > 0) {
  console.error(`Reference is out of date with the compiler (${failures.length}):\n- ${failures.join('\n- ')}`)
  process.exit(1)
}
console.log(`Reference covers ${options.length} options, ${namespaces.size} namespaces and every drop reason.`)

```

`docs/scripts/check-typescript.mjs`:

```mjs
// Type-checks the TypeScript definitions generated for the test schema, so the
// .d.ts output cannot regress into something roblox-ts rejects.
//
// Usage, from the repository root: node docs/scripts/check-typescript.mjs
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'

const root = process.cwd()
const run = (command, args, options = {}) =>
  execFileSync(command, args, { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8', stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'], shell: process.platform === 'win32', ...options })

run('lune', ['run', 'src/CLI/init.luau', 'test/Sources/Test', '--', '--yes'])

const local = join(root, 'docs', 'node_modules', '.bin', process.platform === 'win32' ? 'tsc.cmd' : 'tsc')
const [command, prefix] = existsSync(local) ? [local, []] : ['npx', ['--yes', '-p', 'typescript@5', 'tsc']]
const files = ['Network/Client.d.ts', 'Network/Server.d.ts']

try {
  run(command, [...prefix, '--noEmit', '--strict', '--lib', 'es2020', ...files])
} catch (error) {
  console.error(`Generated TypeScript definitions do not type-check:\n${error.stdout || ''}${error.stderr || ''}`)
  process.exit(1)
}
console.log(`Generated TypeScript definitions type-check (${files.join(', ')}).`)

import React from 'react'
import { useRouter } from 'next/router'
import { DocsThemeConfig, useConfig } from 'nextra-theme-docs'

const basePath = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH ?? ''
// Absolute site URL for social previews, set by the deploy workflow
const siteUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? basePath
const repository = 'https://github.com/pealz1/cheeto'
const description =
  'Cheeto compiles a small schema language into fast, fully typed and hardened Luau networking code for Roblox.'

const Logo = () => (
  <span className="cheeto-logo">
    <img src={`${basePath}/cheeto.svg`} width={26} height={26} alt="" />
    <span>Cheeto</span>
    <small>1.0</small>
  </span>
)

const Head = () => {
  const { asPath } = useRouter()
  const { frontMatter, title } = useConfig()
  const pageTitle = asPath === '/' ? 'Cheeto: typed, secure networking for Roblox' : `${title} – Cheeto`
  const pageDescription = frontMatter.description || description

  return (
    <>
      <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, viewport-fit=cover" />
      <meta name="description" content={pageDescription} />
      <meta property="og:title" content={pageTitle} />
      <meta property="og:description" content={pageDescription} />
      <meta property="og:type" content="website" />
      <meta property="og:image" content={`${siteUrl}/og.png`} />
      <meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image" />
      <meta name="theme-color" media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" content="#f3efe6" />
      <meta name="theme-color" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" content="#13120f" />
      <link rel="icon" href={`${basePath}/cheeto.svg`} type="image/svg+xml" />
    </>
  )
}

const config: DocsThemeConfig = {
  logo: <Logo />,
  project: { link: repository },
  docsRepositoryBase: `${repository}/tree/main/docs`,
  primaryHue: 24,
  primarySaturation: 95,
  darkMode: true,
  nextThemes: { defaultTheme: 'system' },
  head: Head,
  useNextSeoProps() {
    const { asPath } = useRouter()
    if (asPath !== '/') {
      return { titleTemplate: '%s – Cheeto' }
    }
    return { title: 'Cheeto: typed, secure networking for Roblox' }
  },
  sidebar: {
    defaultMenuCollapseLevel: 2,
    titleComponent({ title, type }) {
      return type === 'separator' ? <span className="cheeto-sidebar-group">{title}</span> : <>{title}</>
    },
    toggleButton: true
  },
  toc: {
    backToTop: true
  },
  editLink: {
    text: 'Edit this page on GitHub →'
  },
  feedback: {
    content: 'Open an issue about this page →',
    labels: 'documentation'
  },
  search: {
    placeholder: 'Search the docs…'
  },
  footer: {
    text: (
      <div className="cheeto-footer">
        <span>

        </span>
        <span className="cheeto-footer-links">
          <a href={repository} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">GitHub</a>

          <a href={`${repository}/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md`} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">Contributing</a>

`extras/security/Config.luau`:

```luau
--[[
	Shared configuration for the security channel, required by both the client
	detector and the server guard so the two never drift.
]]

return {
	--> Single, non-descriptive RemoteEvent name. Per-call renaming is deliberately
	--> NOT done: a remote spy hooks the FireServer C-closure, not the instance
	--> name, so renaming every call costs replication churn for zero security. One
	--> obfuscated name is the honest, useful version.
	RemoteName = "f9c3a7d1",

	--> How often the client sweeps readable GUI containers for IY fingerprints.
	ScanInterval = 3,

	--> Signed heartbeat cadence and the server-side timeout before a silent client
	--> (detector removed/blocked) is kicked. Timeout comfortably exceeds several
	--> missed heartbeats to tolerate network jitter.
	HeartbeatInterval = 3,
	HeartbeatTimeout = 15,

	--> Grace after handshake before timeout enforcement begins, so a freshly joined
	--> or still-loading client is never kicked.
	JoinGraceSeconds = 20,

	--> A single server frame slower than this is treated as a lag hitch: heartbeat
	--> timers are forgiven for that tick so a laggy server never mass-kicks.
	LagHitchSeconds = 2,

	--> Neutral kick text — never reveal which signal fired to the exploiter.
	KickMessage = "Disconnected.",
}
